sec03-card-r52.expected_back: A changed medical condition or newly used special equipment may require a driving evaluation to assess continued safe vehicle control.

sec04-card-f01.front: How should your back and feet be positioned once seated behind the wheel?
sec04-card-f01.memory_hook: Sit upright, back flat, feet planted
sec04-card-f01.expected_back: Sit upright with your back against the seat and your feet on the floor.

sec04-card-f02.front: Which four comfort and safety goals guide adjusting your seat and mirrors?
sec04-card-f02.expected_back: Set the seat and mirrors for a clear surrounding view, easy pedal access and a comfortable steering reach with airbag space.

sec04-card-f03.front: How should a shorter driver gain road visibility without crowding the steering wheel?
sec04-card-f03.expected_back: Raise the seat enough to see the road, using a cushion if needed, without moving so far forward that steering is hindered.

sec04-card-f04.front: Where should your right heel stay while switching between accelerator and brake?
sec04-card-f04.expected_back: You should be able to switch between brake and accelerator easily while your heel stays on the floor.

sec04-card-f05.front: How high should the top of the steering wheel sit relative to your shoulders and chin?
sec04-card-f05.expected_back: Position the steering-wheel top no higher than your shoulders and below your chin.

sec04-card-f06.front: How many inches belong between your breastbone and the steering wheel, and how should the seatback sit?
sec04-card-f06.expected_back: Leave ten inches between your chest and the steering wheel for the airbag, and avoid reclining the seatback.

sec04-card-f07.front: Where against the back of your head should the head restraint make contact?
sec04-card-f07.memory_hook: Touch back of head, above ears
sec04-card-f07.expected_back: The head restraint should touch the back of your head above ear level.

sec04-card-f08.front: What should your interior rearview mirror cleanly frame?
sec04-card-f08.expected_back: Set the inside rearview mirror to frame the rear window.

sec04-card-f09.front: Why adjust your inside mirror's day-night setting to match outside lighting?
sec04-card-f09.expected_back: Set a day-night mirror for the current light conditions to reduce glare from following headlights.

sec04-card-f10.front: When must you finish adjusting your interior and exterior mirrors?
sec04-card-f10.expected_back: Adjust rearview and side mirrors before starting to drive.

sec04-card-f11.front: How do you position your head and aim the left outside mirror to shrink blind spots?
sec04-card-f11.expected_back: To set the left exterior mirror, rest your head against the closed left window and adjust until only a small part of the vehicle’s left rear edge is visible.

sec04-card-f12.front: Where do you lean your head when aiming the right exterior mirror?
sec04-card-f12.expected_back: To set the right exterior mirror, lean right with your head directly below the inside rearview mirror and adjust until the right vehicle side is barely visible.

sec04-card-f13.front: What overall field of view should properly aimed exterior mirrors deliver?
sec04-card-f13.expected_back: Exterior mirrors should provide the widest useful view to the sides and rear.

sec04-card-f14.front: Whose seatbelts and child seats must the driver confirm before pulling away?
sec04-card-f14.expected_back: Fasten your safety belt, and ensure occupants use belts or appropriate child seats.

sec04-card-f15.front: Beyond cutting injury and death inside the car, what fatal crash outcome do seatbelts prevent?
sec04-card-f15.expected_back: Belts reduce crash injury and death and help prevent occupants from being thrown out.

sec04-card-f16.front: How does wearing a safety belt help you avoid a secondary crash during violent swerves?
sec04-card-f16.expected_back: Belts help keep the driver behind the wheel during sudden stops or turns so control can be maintained.

sec04-card-f17.front: What happens to an unbelted rider the instant a crashing vehicle stops?
sec04-card-f17.expected_back: In a collision an unbelted occupant keeps moving until striking something inside the stopped vehicle.

sec04-card-f18.front: Even without a crash, how do safety belts help you on bumpy or winding roads?
sec04-card-f18.expected_back: Belts help resist slouching and reduce the effort of remaining in the seat as the vehicle bounces or turns.

sec04-card-f19.front: Why must you fasten your safety belt before starting the engine?
sec04-card-f19.expected_back: Buckle before starting the car because an emergency leaves no time to fasten the belt.

sec04-card-f20.front: Where must the shoulder belt cross your torso, and which two shortcuts are dangerous?
sec04-card-f20.expected_back: Wear the shoulder belt across your shoulder and chest, never beneath an arm or behind the back.

sec04-card-f21.front: Where across your lower body should a snug lap belt sit?
sec04-card-f21.expected_back: Wear the lap belt comfortably tight below the stomach and over the hips and hip bones.

sec04-card-f22.front: Do airbags replace safety belts or work alongside them?
sec04-card-f22.expected_back: Airbags provide added protection and work with safety belts; they do not replace wearing a belt.

sec04-card-f23.front: Which parts of the body do belts and frontal airbags team up to keep off the wheel and dash?
sec04-card-f23.expected_back: Airbags and belts help prevent the head and upper body from striking the wheel or dashboard.

sec04-card-f24.front: Where should you look for rules and warnings tailored to your specific car's airbags?
sec04-card-f24.expected_back: Consult the owner’s manual for information specific to the vehicle’s airbags.

sec04-card-r01.front: Which seating row is safest for a child of any age?
sec04-card-r01.expected_back: The rear seat is the safest riding position for a child of any age.

sec04-card-r02.front: Where must a rear-facing child safety seat never be installed?
sec04-card-r02.expected_back: Never install a rear-facing child seat in front of an active passenger airbag.

sec04-card-r03.front: Which two guides govern installing a child seat, and what two fastening steps matter?
sec04-card-r03.expected_back: Follow both the vehicle manual and child-restraint instructions, secure the seat correctly and buckle the child into it.

sec04-card-r04.front: How and where does the Maine manual advise children younger than two to ride?
sec04-card-r04.expected_back: The manual advises rear-facing travel in the back seat for children younger than two.

sec04-card-r05.front: What harm can an inflating airbag inflict on an unrestrained occupant?
sec04-card-r05.expected_back: An unrestrained occupant can be injured or killed by an airbag.

sec04-card-r06.front: May an infant ride in the front seat of a vehicle equipped with a passenger-side airbag?
sec04-card-r06.expected_back: An infant must not ride in the front seat of a vehicle fitted with a passenger-side airbag.

sec04-card-r07.front: How should front-row occupants—especially short, pregnant, or older riders—position their seats?
sec04-card-r07.expected_back: Drivers and front passengers should sit as far from the wheel or dashboard as possible, especially if short, pregnant or elderly.

sec04-card-r08.front: Which federal safety benchmark defines a lawful child safety seat in Maine?
sec04-card-r08.expected_back: A child safety seat is defined as one meeting Federal Motor Vehicle Safety Standards.

sec04-card-r09.front: How does Maine define a federally approved child-restraint booster system?
sec04-card-r09.expected_back: The defined federally approved child-restraint system elevates a child for correct use of a lap-and-shoulder belt and meets Federal Motor Vehicle Safety Standards.

sec04-card-r10.front: Below what weight must a child ride secured inside a child safety seat?
sec04-card-r10.expected_back: In a vehicle federally required to have safety belts, the operator must secure a child weighing less than fifty-five pounds in a child safety seat.

sec04-card-r11.front: Which age and weight bracket requires a federally approved child-restraint booster system?
sec04-card-r11.expected_back: The operator must secure a child younger than eight who weighs at least fifty-five but less than eighty pounds in a federally approved child-restraint system.

sec04-card-r12.front: When does a passenger under eighteen graduate to a standard seat belt?
sec04-card-r12.expected_back: A passenger younger than eighteen must use a seat belt when older than eight or taller than four feet nine inches, unless a child seat or child-restraint system is still required.

sec04-card-r13.front: What seatbelt rule applies to passengers aged eighteen or older in belt-equipped vehicles?
sec04-card-r13.expected_back: A passenger aged eighteen or older must be properly belted in a vehicle federally required to have seat belts.

sec04-card-r14.front: Must the vehicle operator wear a safety belt unless a specific statutory exemption applies?
sec04-card-r14.expected_back: The operator of a vehicle federally required to have seat belts must wear the operator’s own belt, subject to the stated exceptions.

sec04-card-r15.front: When is a United States Postal Service rural carrier exempt from Maine's seatbelt rule?
sec04-card-r15.expected_back: A United States Postal Service rural carrier is exempt from belt use while delivering mail.

sec04-card-r16.front: Is a taxi or limousine driver legally responsible if a fare-paying passenger leaves their belt unfastened?
sec04-card-r16.expected_back: A taxi or limousine operator is not responsible for fastening the belt of a fare-paying passenger.

sec04-card-r17.front: When is a newspaper delivery driver exempt from wearing a safety belt?
sec04-card-r17.expected_back: A newspaper deliverer is exempt from belt use during actual delivery or duties requiring frequent vehicle entry and exit.

sec06-card-f01.front: How should you treat right-of-way even when the law gives you priority?
sec06-card-f01.expected_back: Use right-of-way sensibly rather than insisting on it; remain alert even when priority is yours.

sec06-card-f02.front: Who stops and who goes first when drivers arrive one after another at a four-way stop?
sec06-card-f02.expected_back: At a four-way stop, every vehicle stops and the first arrival proceeds first.

sec06-card-f03.front: When two adjacent drivers reach a four-way stop at the exact same moment, who yields?
sec06-card-f03.expected_back: If adjacent drivers reach a four-way stop at the same time, yield to the driver on the right.

sec06-card-f04.front: Who has priority when you pull onto a public street from a private road or driveway?
sec06-card-f04.expected_back: Entering a public road from a private drive or road requires yielding to its vehicles and pedestrians without interfering with traffic.

sec06-card-f05.front: Between a car on an interstate entrance ramp and traffic already on the highway, who yields?
sec06-card-f05.expected_back: A driver on an interstate entrance ramp yields to traffic already on the highway.

sec06-card-f06.front: What must you wait for before pulling out of a parked position into a travel lane?
sec06-card-f06.expected_back: When leaving a parked position, wait for moving traffic to pass.

sec06-card-f07.front: What must you never do when a vehicle ahead stops at a crosswalk for pedestrians?
sec06-card-f07.expected_back: Never pass a vehicle stopped for pedestrians in a crosswalk.

sec06-card-f08.front: At an intersection with no signs or signals, who goes if vehicles arrive at roughly the same time?
sec06-card-f08.expected_back: When vehicles reach an uncontrolled intersection at about the same time, yield to the one on the right.

sec06-card-f09.front: How must you respond to vehicles that have already entered an intersection ahead of you?
sec06-card-f09.expected_back: Yield to vehicles that have already entered an intersection.

sec06-card-f10.front: Who yields when a vehicle approaches to enter a rotary or traffic circle?
sec06-card-f10.expected_back: A vehicle entering a traffic circle yields to vehicles already circulating.

sec06-card-f11.front: What exact steps must you take when an emergency vehicle approaches from any direction with siren and flashing lights?
sec06-card-f11.expected_back: For an emergency vehicle approaching from any direction with a siren and flashing light, move immediately to the road’s right side, clear of intersections, and stop until it passes.

sec06-card-f12.front: How does Maine law classify failing to yield properly to an emergency vehicle using siren and flashing lights?
sec06-card-f12.expected_back: Failing to yield as required to the described siren-and-flashing-light emergency vehicle is a Class E crime.

sec06-card-f13.front: How must a left-turning driver handle an oncoming bicyclist or roller skier?
sec06-card-f13.expected_back: A left-turning motorist yields to an oncoming cyclist or roller skier and turns only when safe without interfering with them.

sec06-card-f14.front: What must you do for pedestrians in a marked crosswalk where no signal or officer directs traffic?
sec06-card-f14.expected_back: Yield to pedestrians in a marked crosswalk when no traffic signal or police officer controls the intersection.

sec06-card-f15.front: Who has priority when you are turning at a signalized intersection and pedestrians are crossing with the light?
sec06-card-f15.expected_back: While turning, yield to pedestrians crossing with the signal.

sec06-card-f16.front: What must you do before driving across a sidewalk out of an alley or driveway?
sec06-card-f16.expected_back: Before crossing a sidewalk from an alley or driveway, stop and wait for pedestrians and traffic.

sec06-card-f17.front: What is your duty whenever schoolchildren are crossing the street?
sec06-card-f17.expected_back: Always yield to schoolchildren who are crossing the street.

sec06-card-f18.front: Besides signs, lights, and pavement lines, whose spoken or hand directions count as official traffic controls?
sec06-card-f18.expected_back: Traffic controls include signals, signs, markings and directions from police, highway workers or school crossing guards.

sec06-card-f19.front: Is cutting through a corner parking lot legal to skip waiting at a red light or stop sign?
sec06-card-f19.expected_back: Do not drive through a parking area to evade a traffic-control requirement.

sec06-card-f20.front: How are red, yellow, and green lenses arranged on vertical and horizontal traffic signals?
sec06-card-f20.expected_back: A vertical traffic signal places red above yellow above green; a horizontal signal places red left, yellow middle and green right.

sec06-card-f21.front: When does a steady green traffic light actually allow you to move through an intersection?
sec06-card-f21.expected_back: A green light permits proceeding cautiously only when the route is clear of vehicles and pedestrians.

sec06-card-f22.front: What does a steady yellow traffic signal warn you of, and what action does it call for?
sec06-card-f22.expected_back: A yellow signal warns of an approaching red phase and calls for slowing as the intersection clears.

sec06-card-f23.front: Where must you stop and wait when facing a steady red traffic light?
sec06-card-f23.expected_back: At red, stop before entering the intersection and remain behind the stop line or crosswalk until permitted to proceed.

sec06-card-f24.front: Under what conditions may you turn right at a steady red light in Maine?
sec06-card-f24.expected_back: A right turn on red is allowed after a stop unless signs prohibit it, and the turning driver must yield to pedestrians and all vehicle traffic.

sec06-card-f25.front: How should you respond when approaching a flashing yellow traffic signal?
sec06-card-f25.expected_back: At a flashing yellow light, slow down, proceed cautiously and be ready to stop for traffic.

sec06-card-f26.front: What must you do at a flashing red traffic light before entering the intersection?
sec06-card-f26.expected_back: A flashing red traffic light requires stopping and checking both directions before entering.

sec06-card-f27.front: At a railroad crossing with flashing red lights and lowered gates, when may you finally drive across?
sec06-card-f27.memory_hook: Wait till lights stop, gates rise
sec06-card-f27.expected_back: At a railway crossing with flashing red lights and barriers, wait until the flashing stops and the barriers rise before proceeding.

sec06-card-f28.front: What movement is allowed when a signal shows both a red light and a lighted green arrow?
sec06-card-f28.expected_back: With a red light and a green arrow, move cautiously only in the arrow’s direction while yielding to other vehicles and pedestrians.

sec06-card-f29.front: What is the purpose of a steady yellow arrow on a turn signal?
sec06-card-f29.expected_back: A steady yellow arrow clears turning traffic before red.

sec06-card-f30.front: Which direction of travel does a steady upward-pointing green arrow allow?
sec06-card-f30.expected_back: A steady upward green arrow permits straight-ahead movement.

sec06-card-f31.front: What must drivers in that turn lane do when facing a steady red turn arrow?
sec06-card-f31.expected_back: A steady red turn arrow requires the indicated turning traffic to wait until the arrow becomes green.

sec06-card-f32.front: When several traffic signals hang across a wide roadway, which signal governs you?
sec06-card-f32.expected_back: Where multiple traffic lights are present, follow the light directly above your lane.

sec06-card-f33.front: What does a steady red X suspended directly over a traffic lane mean?
sec06-card-f33.expected_back: A steady red overhead X closes that lane to driving.

sec06-card-f34.front: What action must you take when you see a steady yellow X above your lane?
sec06-card-f34.expected_back: A steady yellow overhead X means leave the lane because its signal is about to become red.

sec06-card-f35.front: For what single maneuver may you use a lane marked with an overhead flashing yellow X?
sec06-card-f35.expected_back: A flashing yellow overhead X permits that lane only for a left turn.

sec06-card-f36.front: What does a downward-pointing green arrow mounted over a traffic lane tell you?
sec06-card-f36.expected_back: A green overhead arrow identifies a lane available for use.

sec06-card-f37.front: What standard color, shape, and markings identify most general road warning signs?
sec06-card-f37.expected_back: Warning signs are generally yellow diamonds with black text or symbols that warn of hazards ahead.

sec06-card-f38.front: What roadway feature ahead is announced by a yellow diamond bearing a bold black cross?
sec06-card-f38.expected_back: A black cross on a yellow diamond warns of an intersection ahead.

sec06-card-f39.front: What does a yellow diamond showing a vertical black line met by one side branch warn about?
sec06-card-f39.expected_back: A main vertical stroke with a side branch on a yellow diamond warns of a side road.

sec06-card-f40.front: What type of junction ahead is indicated by a bold black letter T on a yellow diamond?
sec06-card-f40.expected_back: A black T on a yellow diamond warns of a T-intersection.

sec06-card-f41.front: What passing restriction is marked by a sideways-pointing yellow pennant sign?
sec06-card-f41.expected_back: The yellow No Passing Zone pennant identifies a no-passing area.

sec06-card-f42.front: What lies ahead when a yellow diamond displays a winding S-shaped black arrow?
sec06-card-f42.expected_back: A winding black arrow on a yellow diamond warns of a curving road ahead.

sec06-card-f43.front: What does a yellow diamond with a black arrow curving smoothly to the right warn of?
sec06-card-f43.expected_back: A black right-curving arrow on a yellow diamond warns of a right curve.

sec06-card-f44.front: Which warning sign shows two opposing arrows splitting around the nose of a center island?
sec06-card-f44.expected_back: The divided-highway-begins warning shows opposing arrows separating around a divider.

sec06-card-f45.front: Which warning sign depicts opposing arrows coming back together past the end of a center island?
sec06-card-f45.expected_back: The divided-highway-ends warning shows opposing traffic beside a divider ending ahead.

sec06-card-f46.front: What does a yellow warning sign with one outer black line angling inward toward the other mean?
sec06-card-f46.expected_back: The lane-ends warning depicts one lane boundary tapering toward the other.

sec06-card-f47.front: What traffic situation ahead is shown by a diagonal black branch blending into an upward arrow?
sec06-card-f47.expected_back: A diagonal branch joining an upward arrow warns of merging traffic.

sec06-card-f48.front: What does a warning sign with two upward arrows separated by a short dashed line indicate?
sec06-card-f48.expected_back: Two upward arrows separated by a dashed divider identify the illustrated added-lane warning.

sec06-card-f49.front: What is ahead when you pass a yellow diamond displaying a vertical red-yellow-green light symbol?
sec06-card-f49.expected_back: A traffic-signal picture on a yellow diamond warns that a traffic light is ahead.

sec06-card-f50.front: What does a yellow warning diamond showing a red octagon below an upward black arrow tell you?
sec06-card-f50.expected_back: A stop-sign symbol beneath an upward arrow warns that a stop sign is ahead.

sec06-card-f51.front: What hazard does a rectangular yellow panel with a bold black V-shaped chevron mark?
sec06-card-f51.expected_back: The illustrated black chevron on yellow warns of a sharp curve.

sec06-card-f52.front: What information does a small yellow speed plaque mounted below a curve diamond give?
sec06-card-f52.expected_back: A curve warning paired with an advisory-speed plaque gives a suggested speed around that curve.

sec06-card-f53.front: Which special five-sided yellow sign shows two walking figures inside?
sec06-card-f53.expected_back: The illustrated yellow school-zone pentagon contains two walking figures.

sec06-card-f54.front: What does a yellow diamond bearing a single walking person symbol warn drivers to watch for?
sec06-card-f54.expected_back: The pedestrian-crossing warning shows a walking person on a yellow diamond.

sec06-card-f55.front: Which warning combines a bicycle, a car, and a plaque reminding motorists about bicycles?
sec06-card-f55.expected_back: The Share the Road warning combines a bicycle, car and wording about sharing with bicycles.

sec06-card-f56.front: What does a yellow diamond displaying only a black bicycle symbol warn of?
sec06-card-f56.expected_back: A bicycle pictured alone on a yellow diamond warns of a bicycle crossing.

sec06-card-f57.front: What pavement condition is warned of by a car silhouette above two curvy skid lines?
sec06-card-f57.expected_back: A car above wavy skid marks warns of a road that is slippery when wet.

sec06-card-f58.front: How should you respond when you pass a round yellow warning sign marked with a black X and railroad letters?
sec06-card-f58.expected_back: A round yellow railroad warning with a black X and RR calls for slowing, looking, listening and readiness to stop.

sec06-card-f59.front: What does a white X-shaped railroad crossbuck mark, and where must you stop for an approaching train?
sec06-card-f59.expected_back: A white railroad crossbuck marks a crossing where an approaching train requires stopping behind the line or before the tracks.

sec06-card-f60.front: Why must you scan for additional tracks and trains even if no track-count plaque is posted?
sec06-card-f60.expected_back: Look for additional tracks and trains even when no track-count sign is posted.

sec06-card-f61.front: Once clear, how should you drive across railroad tracks, and what must you never do on them?
sec06-card-f61.expected_back: Look both ways and cross railroad tracks promptly without stopping on them.

sec06-card-f62.front: Right after a train finishes crossing ahead of you, how long must you wait before moving?
sec06-card-f62.memory_hook: Wait till train clears, gates allow
sec06-card-f62.expected_back: After a train crosses, wait until it is well down the track and any gates or lights indicate it is safe.

sec06-card-f63.front: Where must you wait if traffic or a red signal forces a stop near railroad tracks?
sec06-card-f63.expected_back: When traffic or a signal requires a stop near tracks, wait at the stop line before the tracks.

sec06-card-f64.front: What background color and shapes distinguish temporary work-zone warning signs?
sec06-card-f64.expected_back: Work-zone warnings are orange diamonds or rectangles with black words or symbols.

sec06-card-f65.front: Which common hazards and route changes do orange work-zone signs alert drivers to?
sec06-card-f65.expected_back: The illustrated work-zone warnings identify flaggers, workers, construction, a one-lane road and a detour.

sec06-card-f66.front: What authority do a highway work-zone flagger's paddle or hand signals carry?

sec06-card-f67.front: Where should you stop when facing a red portable traffic signal in a construction zone?
sec06-card-f67.expected_back: At a temporary traffic signal, stop at its white line if one is present.

sec06-card-f68.front: What do orange barrels, cones, tubes, and a Road Closed barrier tell you in a work zone?
sec06-card-f68.expected_back: Barrels, cones, tubes and barriers identify restricted work areas, and a Road Closed barrier prevents entry.

sec06-card-f69.front: What three driving habits keep you safe while traveling through an active work zone?
sec06-card-f69.expected_back: Slow down in work zones, avoid tailgating and be ready to stop promptly.

sec06-card-f70.front: What happens to the fine if you are ticketed for speeding inside a Maine work zone?
sec06-card-f70.expected_back: A speeding fine in a work zone is doubled.

sec06-card-r01.front: What kind of rules do regulatory signs state, and what topics do they commonly cover?
sec06-card-r01.expected_back: Regulatory signs give enforceable directions about matters such as speed, turns, lanes and parking.

sec06-card-r02.front: What universal message does a red circle with a diagonal red bar across a black symbol send?
sec06-card-r02.expected_back: A red circle crossed by a red diagonal bar prohibits the pictured action.

sec06-card-r03.front: What maneuver is outlawed by a left-pointing arrow inside a red circle and diagonal slash?
sec06-card-r03.expected_back: A crossed-out left-turn arrow prohibits a left turn.

sec06-card-r04.front: What maneuver is outlawed by a right-pointing arrow inside a red circle and diagonal slash?
sec06-card-r04.expected_back: A crossed-out right-turn arrow prohibits a right turn.

sec06-card-r05.front: What maneuver is forbidden when a bent U-shaped arrow sits inside a red circle and slash?
sec06-card-r05.expected_back: A crossed-out U-shaped arrow prohibits a U-turn.

sec06-card-r06.front: What movement does a white regulatory sign showing a single upward black arrow require?
sec06-card-r06.expected_back: A single upward regulatory arrow directs straight travel.

sec06-card-r07.front: What must drivers do when positioned in a lane governed by a left-turn-only regulatory sign?
sec06-card-r07.expected_back: The left-turn-only sign directs traffic to turn left.

sec06-card-r08.front: Which two movements are allowed by a regulatory sign combining an upward arrow with a right branch?
sec06-card-r08.expected_back: A combined upward-and-right arrow permits straight travel or a right turn.

sec06-card-r09.front: Under what roadway conditions does a black-and-white speed-limit sign state the maximum legal speed?
sec06-card-r09.expected_back: A black-and-white speed-limit sign states the legal speed for ideal conditions.

sec06-card-r10.front: What unique shape and color combination identifies a standard stop sign?
sec06-card-r10.expected_back: A stop sign is a red octagon with white lettering.

sec06-card-r11.front: Where must your vehicle come to rest at a stop sign when a stop line or crosswalk is painted?
sec06-card-r11.expected_back: At a stop sign, stop behind an available stop line or crosswalk.

sec06-card-r12.front: Where do you stop at a stop sign when neither a stop line nor a crosswalk is painted?
sec06-card-r12.expected_back: Without a stop line or crosswalk, stop near enough to see cross traffic but before any part of the vehicle enters the intersection.

sec06-card-r13.front: Once you make a full stop at a stop sign, when may you finally pull forward?
sec06-card-r13.expected_back: After stopping, proceed only when safe and yield to any vehicles or pedestrians present.

sec06-card-r14.front: What shape and colors identify modern yield signs, and what colors might older ones still show?
sec06-card-r14.expected_back: A modern yield sign is a downward-pointing red-and-white triangle; older examples may be yellow with black letters.

sec06-card-r15.front: How must you drive when approaching a yield sign with cross traffic or pedestrians nearby?
sec06-card-r15.expected_back: At a yield sign, slow and allow traffic or pedestrians with priority to clear before entering or crossing.

sec06-card-r16.front: What maneuver is a shared center left-turn lane built for, and what two uses are forbidden?
sec06-card-r16.expected_back: A shared center left-turn lane serves left turns from either direction, not through travel or passing.

sec06-card-r17.front: How must you travel when entering or driving along a signed one-way street?
sec06-card-r17.expected_back: On a one-way street, travel only in the arrow’s direction and do not turn against it.

sec06-card-r18.front: What must drivers and pedestrians do when a police officer is directing traffic?
sec06-card-r18.expected_back: Obey police directions controlling vehicles or pedestrians.

sec06-card-r19.front: What are the legal consequences of ignoring police traffic orders or trying to flee an officer?
sec06-card-r19.expected_back: Refusing or failing to follow police traffic orders is illegal, and attempting to flee can cost a license.

sec06-card-r20.front: When no officer is present on scene, what legal weight do posted traffic signs and signals carry?
sec06-card-r20.expected_back: Traffic signs and signals carry legal authority when no police officer is directing traffic.

sec06-card-r21.front: How does Maine law view removing, stealing, or defacing roadway traffic signs?
sec06-card-r21.expected_back: Removing or defacing traffic signs is unlawful.

sec06-card-r22.front: Which three background colors and shapes are generally used on guide signs, and what do they point out?
sec06-card-r22.expected_back: Guide signs are generally green, brown or blue squares or rectangles used for destinations, roads, points of interest and services.

sec06-card-r23.front: What do the distinct shapes and colors of highway route markers help you tell apart?
sec06-card-r23.expected_back: Route-marker shape and color identify the roadway type, including Interstate, U.S. and state routes.

sec06-card-r24.front: What colors and layout identify an official Interstate highway route marker?
sec06-card-r24.expected_back: The illustrated Interstate route marker is a blue shield topped with a red Interstate band.

sec06-card-r25.front: How does a United States numbered highway marker look compared with an Interstate shield?
sec06-card-r25.expected_back: The illustrated U.S. route marker is a white shield with black route numerals.

sec06-card-r26.front: What black-and-white design identifies a state-route marker in the Maine handbook?
sec06-card-r26.expected_back: The illustrated state-route marker uses a white circular area inside a black square.

sec06-card-r27.front: How should you prepare and navigate when driving through unfamiliar territory?
sec06-card-r27.expected_back: Plan a route with a map or GPS and follow route markers while traveling in an unfamiliar area.

sec06-card-r28.front: What five traffic functions do painted pavement markings perform on the road surface?
sec06-card-r28.expected_back: Pavement markings divide lanes, indicate passing or lane changes, identify turns and crosswalks, and mark stopping places.

sec06-card-r29.front: What traffic directions and passing rule does a single broken yellow center line indicate?
sec06-card-r29.expected_back: A broken yellow center line marks opposite-direction traffic where the marking permits passing.

sec06-card-r30.front: Where a solid yellow line runs beside a broken yellow center line, which side is allowed to pass?
sec06-card-r30.expected_back: With a solid-and-broken yellow center pair, passing is permitted from the broken-line side.

sec06-card-r31.front: What passing rule applies when two solid yellow lines divide the center of the road?
sec06-card-r31.memory_hook: Double yellow bans passing both ways
sec06-card-r31.expected_back: A double solid yellow center pair prohibits passing in both directions.

sec06-card-r32.front: What lane flow and maneuver does a broken white divider line indicate?
sec06-card-r32.expected_back: A broken white lane divider separates lanes traveling in the same direction in the illustrated passing-permitted example.

sec06-card-r33.front: During normal through driving, how should you choose which travel lane to stay in?
sec06-card-r33.expected_back: For ordinary through driving, prefer the lane with the smoothest flow and least repeated stopping and starting.

sec06-card-r34.front: When a roadway offers three or more lanes in your direction, which lane usually flows smoothest?
sec06-card-r34.expected_back: With at least three lanes in one direction, a middle lane usually has the smoothest traffic flow.

sec06-card-r35.front: On a multilane road, what specific purposes belong to the left lane versus the right lane?
sec06-card-r35.memory_hook: Left passes, turns; right slower, exits
sec06-card-r35.expected_back: On a multilane road, the left lane serves passing or left turns, while the right serves slower traffic and entering or exiting vehicles.

sec06-card-r36.front: When there are two lanes traveling in your direction, which lane generally offers smoother flow?
sec06-card-r36.expected_back: With two lanes in one direction, the right lane generally has the smoother flow.

sec06-card-r37.front: On which side is overtaking and passing another vehicle normally performed?
sec06-card-r37.expected_back: Passing is generally done on the left.

sec06-card-r38.front: Are you ever allowed to drive off the paved road surface onto the shoulder to pass someone?
sec06-card-r38.expected_back: Do not pass by leaving the pavement or main traveled part of the roadway.

sec06-card-r39.front: May you pull into a signed center turning-only lane to overtake slower through traffic?
sec06-card-r39.expected_back: Do not use a signed turning-only center lane for passing.

sec06-card-r40.front: When may you pass on the right of a vehicle waiting to make a left turn?
sec06-card-r40.expected_back: Passing on the right is permitted when the other vehicle is turning left and there is room for at least two same-direction lanes.

sec06-card-r41.front: Besides passing a left-turning car, when else is passing on the right legal?
sec06-card-r41.expected_back: Passing on the right is also permitted when the other car occupies the left lane of a road with at least two marked same-direction lanes.

sec06-card-r42.front: Which lanes must trucks other than pickups use on three-lane stretches of the Maine Turnpike or Interstate ninety-five?
sec06-card-r42.expected_back: On three-lane sections in either direction of the Maine Turnpike or Interstate ninety-five, trucks other than pickups must use the two rightmost lanes.

sec06-card-r43.front: Which lane do you approach a left turn from, and how should you wait near the intersection midpoint?
sec06-card-r43.expected_back: Approach a left turn in the lane nearest the center line and wait near the intersection midpoint with the wheels straight until it is clear.

sec06-card-r44.front: How should you position your vehicle before and during a right turn?
sec06-card-r44.expected_back: For a right turn, start in the rightmost lane and stay as close to the curb as possible throughout the turn.

sec06-card-r45.front: Into which lane of the cross street must you complete a left turn?
sec06-card-r45.expected_back: Complete a left turn into the leftmost lane traveling in the new direction, whether the receiving road is divided, one-way or two-way.

sec06-card-r46.front: Into which lane of the receiving street must you finish a right turn?
sec06-card-r46.expected_back: Complete a right turn into the rightmost lane traveling in the new direction.

sec06-card-r47.front: Where on the roadway should you position before turning left off a one-way street?
sec06-card-r47.expected_back: For a left turn from a one-way street, position near the left curb or roadway edge.

sec06-card-r48.front: If you want a different lane on the new street, when may you move over?
sec06-card-r48.expected_back: Change to another lane only after finishing the turn and when traffic is clear.

sec06-card-r49.front: Why must you keep your front wheels pointed straight ahead while waiting to turn left?
sec06-card-r49.expected_back: Keep the wheels straight while waiting to turn so a rear impact does not push the vehicle into oncoming traffic.

sec06-card-r50.front: What should you do if you realize mid-intersection that you picked the wrong turn or route?
sec06-card-r50.expected_back: Once committed through an intersection or into a turn, continue the maneuver rather than making a last-second change; correct a route mistake at the next intersection.

sec06-card-r51.front: On a standard two-lane control sign with left-only on the left and straight-right on the right, how does each lane move?
sec06-card-r51.expected_back: The illustrated two-lane-use sign requires a left turn from the left lane while the right lane may go straight or turn right.

sec06-card-r52.front: When three lane-use signs show left-straight, straight-only, and right-only from left to right, what does each lane allow?
sec06-card-r52.expected_back: The illustrated three-lane-use signs permit left or straight from the left lane, straight only from the center and a right turn only from the right.

sec06-card-r53.front: What does a solid white line between lanes moving the same direction signify?
sec06-card-r53.expected_back: A solid white divider separates same-direction lanes with different uses and discourages changing between them.

sec06-card-r54.front: What do broken white lines between lanes tell drivers about direction and lane changes?
sec06-card-r54.expected_back: Broken white dividers identify same-direction lanes and allow safe lane changes.

sec06-card-r55.front: Where must you stop when a painted stop line sits ahead of a crosswalk at a sign or light?
sec06-card-r55.expected_back: At a stop sign or signal, stop before the stop line or crosswalk; if a stop line precedes the crosswalk, use that line.

sec06-card-r56.front: Where do you stop at a stop control when no crosswalk or stop line is marked on the pavement?
sec06-card-r56.expected_back: Where no crosswalk is marked, stop before the intersection near enough to see approaching traffic.

sec06-card-r57.front: Where can pedestrian crosswalks be located, and what paint colors commonly mark them?
sec06-card-r57.expected_back: Crosswalks can be at intersections or midblock and are often indicated by yellow or white markings.

sec06-card-r58.front: How must you respond to a school crossing guard, and where must you yield to crossing students?
sec06-card-r58.expected_back: Stop when a school crossing guard directs you, and yield to schoolchildren crossing in rural areas as well as towns.

sec06-card-r59.front: Why is it important to stop cleanly behind a painted stop line?
sec06-card-r59.expected_back: Stop before a painted stop line so pedestrians have space ahead of the vehicle.

sec06-card-r60.front: While turning on a green light, must you yield to pedestrians in unmarked crosswalks as well as painted ones?
sec06-card-r60.expected_back: While turning, yield to pedestrians in either marked or unmarked crosswalks even when your signal is green.

sec06-card-r61.front: How far away must you halt and how long must you wait for a pedestrian using a white cane or guide dog?
sec06-card-r61.expected_back: For a roadway pedestrian using a white cane or guide dog, halt at least ten feet away and remain stopped until the person is no longer in danger.

sec06-card-r62.front: What fine range applies in Maine for failing to yield to a visually impaired pedestrian?
sec06-card-r62.expected_back: Failure to yield to a visually impaired pedestrian is a traffic infraction with a fine from fifty dollars to one thousand dollars.

sec06-card-r63.front: What four checks and signals must you complete before pulling into a shared center left-turn lane?
sec06-card-r63.expected_back: Before entering a shared left-turn lane, check mirrors and traffic ahead, signal left and check the left blind spot; turn when clear.

sec06-card-r64.front: How is a shared center left-turn lane marked on the pavement?
sec06-card-r64.expected_back: A shared center left-turn lane is illustrated with solid-and-broken yellow borders and opposing left-turn arrows.

sec06-card-r65.front: Why must you always check the overhead signal before entering a reversible traffic lane?
sec06-card-r65.expected_back: A reversible lane carries traffic in different directions at different times, so check its current overhead signal before entry.

sec06-card-r66.front: What pavement lines edge a reversible lane, and which overhead symbols open or close it?
sec06-card-r66.expected_back: Reversible lanes may have double broken yellow borders; a green arrow allows use and a red X closes the lane.

sec07-card-f01.front: What visual checks, signal step, and lane positioning come right before making a turn?
sec07-card-f01.expected_back: Before a turn, check controls, pedestrians and vehicles, signal, and enter the nearest lane in the intended direction.

sec07-card-f02.front: Where should you aim your eyes during a turn, how do you apply throttle, and what do you check after?
sec07-card-f02.expected_back: Look through the turn as far as possible, accelerate smoothly and ensure the signal cancels afterward.

sec07-card-f03.front: From which part of your lane should you start a right turn, and what steering mistake must you avoid?
sec07-card-f03.expected_back: Start a right turn from the rightmost part of your lane without swinging left first.

sec07-card-f04.front: Where inside your lane do you start a left turn, and which traffic stream gets priority?
sec07-card-f04.expected_back: Start a left turn from the leftmost part of your lane and yield to oncoming traffic.

sec07-card-f05.front: When two side-by-side lanes allow turning the same direction, how must you track through the corner?
sec07-card-f05.expected_back: When multiple lanes permit the same turn, keep the corresponding lane through the turn until it is finished.

sec07-card-f06.front: Besides standard crossroads, what other meeting points count as intersections under the Maine handbook?
sec07-card-f06.expected_back: An intersection is any meeting of traffic paths, including side streets, freeway entries and driveways or shopping-center entrances.

sec07-card-f07.front: Why must you look both ways even before crossing a signed one-way street?
sec07-card-f07.expected_back: Look in both directions even when crossing a one-way street because a vehicle may be traveling the wrong way.

sec07-card-f08.front: What six elements should you slow down and actively scan for as you approach any intersection?
sec07-card-f08.expected_back: At intersections, slow and search for controls, traffic, pedestrians, cyclists, road conditions and blocked sight lines.

sec07-card-f09.front: Why should you check cross traffic even when they face a red light or stop sign?
sec07-card-f09.expected_back: Check cross traffic even when it faces red or a stop sign, and be ready to yield to prevent a crash.

sec07-card-f10.front: After stopping at an intersection, what directional visual pattern checks for vehicles and cyclists before entry?
sec07-card-f10.expected_back: After stopping, check traffic and cyclists with a left-right-left search before entry.

sec07-card-f11.front: What two things must you verify before rolling forward when your traffic signal turns green?
sec07-card-f11.expected_back: Before moving on green, confirm the path is clear and cross traffic has stopped.

sec07-card-f12.front: Why is it dangerous to pull out in front of an oncoming car just because its turn signal is blinking?
sec07-card-f12.expected_back: Do not enter a lane merely because an approaching driver signals a turn; the signal may be mistaken or refer to a later turn.

sec07-card-f13.front: How should you handle a corner where a building, hedge, or snowbank blocks your cross-street view?
sec07-card-f13.expected_back: If a fixed obstruction blocks a cross-street view, edge forward slowly only far enough to see and wait for traffic to clear before turning.

sec07-card-f14.front: What should you do when vehicles in the nearest cross lane block your view of the next lane beyond them?
sec07-card-f14.expected_back: If cars in one lane hide another lane, wait for them to pass rather than pushing the vehicle’s nose into the hidden lane.

sec07-card-f15.front: Unless an officer or traffic device directs otherwise, who holds priority at a roundabout or traffic circle?
sec07-card-f15.expected_back: Vehicles entering a circle or roundabout yield to circulating traffic unless police or a traffic-control device directs otherwise.

sec07-card-f16.front: To which side of the central island do you enter a roundabout, and which rotational way do you drive?
sec07-card-f16.expected_back: Enter a roundabout to the right of the center island and travel counterclockwise.

sec07-card-f17.front: What is the raised inner pavement around a small roundabout island built for, and where do passenger cars stay?
sec07-card-f17.expected_back: At the described small-island roundabout, raised inner pavement accommodates trucks while ordinary vehicles remain in the outer travel lane.

sec07-card-f18.front: Which turn leaves a traffic circle, and what visual guides keep you in the proper exit path?
sec07-card-f18.expected_back: Exit a traffic circle with a right turn and pay close attention to signs and lane markings.

sec07-card-f19.front: Unless signs or markings direct otherwise, when does the handbook advise choosing the rightmost lane of a rotary?
sec07-card-f19.expected_back: In the described rotary, a driver exiting within two exits is advised to use the rightmost lane unless signs or markings assign another lane.

sec07-card-f20.front: What four actions sum up safe entry, travel, and exit through a traffic circle?
sec07-card-f20.expected_back: Slow on entering a circle, yield to circulating traffic, follow lane lines and signal the exit.

sec07-card-f21.front: Why aren't mirror glances alone enough before changing lanes, and what physical check must you add?
sec07-card-f21.expected_back: A lane change requires mirror checks and a head turn toward the intended side to inspect the blind spot.

sec07-card-f22.front: What two factors create blind spots around a motor vehicle?
sec07-card-f22.expected_back: Blind spots include areas hidden by vehicle structure and areas the mirrors do not cover.

sec07-card-f23.front: What six-step sequence takes you safely through a complete lane change from start to finish?
sec07-card-f23.expected_back: For a lane change, find a gap, signal, look again, adjust speed, move over and cancel the signal afterward.

sec07-card-f24.front: Besides switching lanes mid-road, what two other maneuvers require full lane-change precautions?
sec07-card-f24.expected_back: Lane-change precautions also apply to freeway entry and moving onto a road from its curb or shoulder.

sec07-card-f25.front: What specific traffic does each mirror check and shoulder glance target before moving sideways?
sec07-card-f25.expected_back: Before moving sideways, check mirrors for passing traffic and look over the relevant shoulder for vehicles near the rear corner.

sec07-card-f26.front: Which two slim road users require special attention during every lane-change check?
sec07-card-f26.expected_back: Watch particularly for motorcycles and bicycles during a lane-change check.

sec07-card-f27.front: Why must your over-the-shoulder checks stay brief while driving in moving traffic?
sec07-card-f27.expected_back: Make rearward checks brief so your eyes return promptly to the road ahead.

sec07-card-f28.front: Why must you scan beyond just the immediate target lane on a multilane road?
sec07-card-f28.expected_back: Inspect every relevant lane because another driver may be moving toward the same gap.

sec07-card-f29.front: How far in advance must you turn on your signal before changing lanes or turning?
sec07-card-f29.expected_back: Signal your intended movement at least one hundred feet before making the change.

sec07-card-f30.front: How should you use an expressway acceleration lane before blending into highway traffic?
sec07-card-f30.expected_back: Use the expressway acceleration lane to approach traffic speed before merging, while looking for a suitable gap.

sec07-card-f31.front: What signaling, checking, and follow-up steps complete a standard expressway merge?
sec07-card-f31.expected_back: For the described expressway entry, signal left, check the rearview mirror and over the shoulder, merge into a clear gap and cancel the signal.

sec07-card-f32.front: How do you enter an expressway when the entrance has no acceleration lane?
sec07-card-f32.expected_back: Where an expressway entrance lacks an acceleration lane, stop before entry, wait for a traffic gap, then accelerate and merge.

sec07-card-f33.front: Does traffic already cruising on an expressway have to yield to merging cars, and what speed mistake must mergers avoid?
sec07-card-f33.expected_back: Traffic already on an expressway need not yield to entering traffic, so avoid merging at a speed that obstructs its flow.

sec07-card-f34.front: Which expressway lane should you normally stay in, and which passing sides are off-limits?
sec07-card-f34.expected_back: The expressway guidance says to remain in the right lane unless passing and not to pass on the right or shoulder.

sec07-card-f35.front: Before pulling left to pass on an expressway, what three checks and signals confirm clearance?
sec07-card-f35.expected_back: Before expressway passing, signal, check mirrors and look over the shoulder to confirm clearance.

sec07-card-f36.front: What speed mistake must you never make while another driver is overtaking you?
sec07-card-f36.expected_back: Do not increase speed while another vehicle is passing you.

sec07-card-f37.front: How quickly should you pass, and what mirror cue tells you it is safe to move back right?
sec07-card-f37.expected_back: Pass promptly and safely, avoid lingering alongside, and return right only after the entire passed vehicle appears in the rearview mirror.

sec07-card-f38.front: Where beside neighboring highway vehicles should you avoid cruising steadily?
sec07-card-f38.expected_back: Avoid cruising in the neighboring driver’s blind spot.

sec07-card-f39.front: Where should you position and signal before an expressway exit, and where do you start braking?
sec07-card-f39.expected_back: For an expressway exit, move right early and signal; begin slowing in the deceleration lane rather than the through lane.

sec07-card-f40.front: Once on the exit ramp, what speed should you drop down to and what control check finishes the exit?
sec07-card-f40.expected_back: Slow to the ramp’s posted speed and ensure the exit signal cancels.

sec07-card-f41.front: For what reason may you stop along an expressway, and how should you pull off?
sec07-card-f41.expected_back: Stop on an expressway only for an emergency; signal and pull as far off the pavement as the shoulder allows.

sec07-card-f42.front: After making an emergency stop on the expressway shoulder, how does the handbook say to signal for assistance?
sec07-card-f42.expected_back: Raise the hood to request help after the described emergency stop.

sec07-card-f43.front: What three actions must you never do on the traveled lanes of an expressway?
sec07-card-f43.expected_back: Never reverse, walk or stand on an expressway’s traveled portion.

sec07-card-f44.front: What mental hazard can long stretches of straight highway driving trigger?
sec07-card-f44.expected_back: Long straight highway travel can cause drowsiness or reduced awareness, so continued concentration is essential.

sec07-card-f45.front: Which four cabin and driving habits does the Maine manual suggest to stay alert on long highway drives?
sec07-card-f45.expected_back: The manual’s alertness tips include a cool cabin, scanning ahead, conversation or music and small speed variations.

sec07-card-f46.front: What should you do at the very first sign of drowsiness behind the wheel?
sec07-card-f46.expected_back: At the first drowsiness warning, use the nearest rest or service area to stretch, nap or change drivers if possible.

sec07-card-f47.front: Why shouldn't tired drivers rely on stay-awake pills or stimulants to keep driving?
sec07-card-f47.expected_back: Do not depend on stay-awake drugs to make tired driving safe.

sec07-card-f48.front: Why does passing on a two-lane road demand signaling and waiting for a wide-open view?
sec07-card-f48.expected_back: Passing on a two-lane road uses the opposing lane, so signal and start only when it is clear.

sec07-card-f49.front: About how many seconds does the manual estimate a highway pass takes at fifty to fifty-five miles per hour?
sec07-card-f49.expected_back: The manual gives ten to twelve seconds as a passing-time guide at fifty to fifty-five miles per hour.

sec07-card-f50.front: Which five upcoming features must you evaluate passing space before?
sec07-card-f50.expected_back: Assess passing space before an approaching vehicle, hill, curve, intersection or road obstruction.

sec07-card-f51.front: What three checks and signal action precede pulling into the left lane to pass?
sec07-card-f51.expected_back: Before passing, check oncoming traffic, mirrors and the shoulder blind spot, signal and enter the left passing lane.

sec07-card-f52.front: What three steps confirm a safe return to the right lane after overtaking on a two-lane road?
sec07-card-f52.expected_back: After passing, wait until the whole vehicle is visible in the rearview mirror, signal and shoulder-check before returning right.

sec07-card-f53.front: Once safely back in the right travel lane after passing, what two final adjustments do you make?
sec07-card-f53.expected_back: After returning to the right lane, adjust speed and cancel the passing signal.

sec07-card-f54.front: How should you position and control your speed while another vehicle overtakes you?
sec07-card-f54.expected_back: When being passed, remain in your lane and keep a steady speed.

sec07-card-f55.front: When might you actually increase speed slightly if an overtaking driver aborts a pass?
sec07-card-f55.expected_back: If an overtaker abandons the pass and drops behind, you may need to increase speed before an oncoming vehicle arrives.

sec07-card-f56.front: Roughly how much road distance do two opposing highway vehicles eat up together during a single pass?
sec07-card-f56.expected_back: The highway-passing illustration allows over one thousand six hundred feet, roughly one-third mile, for the combined opposing vehicles’ travel.

sec07-card-f57.front: What visual illusion makes distant oncoming highway traffic dangerous when judging a pass?
sec07-card-f57.expected_back: A distant oncoming vehicle can appear nearly stationary while already being too close for a pass.

sec07-card-f58.front: How close to a view-blocking hill or curve is starting a pass prohibited?
sec07-card-f58.expected_back: Do not start passing within one-third mile of a hill or curve that blocks the view ahead.

sec07-card-f59.front: Why should you avoid passing near intersections, crossroads, or shopping-center entrances?
sec07-card-f59.expected_back: Avoid passing at intersections, crossroads or shopping-center entries where traffic or people may enter the road.

sec07-card-f60.front: Which two fixed roadway crossings prohibit overtaking as you approach them?
sec07-card-f60.expected_back: Do not pass while approaching a railroad crossing or bridge.

sec07-card-r01.front: What roadside hazards ahead might cause the driver in front of you to swerve suddenly into the passing lane?
sec07-card-r01.expected_back: Before passing, anticipate users moving into your space because of roadside people, cyclists, a narrow bridge, ice, damaged pavement or an obstruction.

sec07-card-r02.front: What rule governs return space before starting a pass behind a line of cars?
sec07-card-r02.expected_back: Begin passing only with known return space, without assuming several vehicles can be passed or that other drivers will make room.

sec07-card-r03.front: Where must you finish your pass and be back in your own lane relative to a no-passing zone?
sec07-card-r03.expected_back: Complete a pass before reaching the start of a no-passing zone.

sec07-card-r04.front: When is passing banned based on the yellow center stripe closest to your lane?
sec07-card-r04.expected_back: Do not pass when the center line on your side is solid.

sec07-card-r05.front: Even when the center line on your side is broken, what condition must hold before you pass?
sec07-card-r05.expected_back: A broken center line on your side permits passing only when no oncoming vehicles occupy the passing lane.

sec07-card-r06.front: Which two roadside signs, one mounted left and one mounted right, outlaw passing?
sec07-card-r06.expected_back: A yellow No Passing Zone pennant on the left or a white Do Not Pass sign on the right prohibits passing there.

sec07-card-r07.front: How must you adjust speed and lateral clearance when overtaking a bicyclist in Maine?
sec07-card-r07.expected_back: When passing a cyclist, slow down and leave at least three feet between the vehicle’s right side and the bicycle.

sec07-card-r08.front: Where must traffic from both directions stop for a school bus flashing its red lights?
sec07-card-r08.expected_back: On school property, an undivided road or a Maine parking area, stop for a school bus displaying flashing red lights when approaching from either direction.

sec07-card-r09.front: Once stopped for a flashing-red school bus on an undivided road, when may you start moving again?
sec07-card-r09.expected_back: After stopping for the described school bus, wait while children board or leave and proceed only when the bus moves or its driver signals permission.

sec07-card-r10.front: On a divided road, when are oncoming drivers excused from stopping for a school bus with red lights or stop arm?
sec07-card-r10.expected_back: On a divided road, stop for a school bus’s flashing red lights or extended stop arm unless a solid divider separates your roadway from the bus.

sec07-card-r11.front: In the divided-road school-bus rules, how should stopped drivers proceed once red lights stop and the arm retracts?
sec07-card-r11.expected_back: In the divided-road bus guidance, proceed slowly while watching for children after the red lights stop and the stop arm is no longer visible.

sec07-card-r12.front: What overarching safety standard governs anywhere you leave a parked vehicle?
sec07-card-r12.expected_back: Park so the vehicle creates no hazard or interference with public-road traffic.

sec07-card-r13.front: How should you align your vehicle along a street unless painted lines show angle stalls?
sec07-card-r13.expected_back: Park parallel to the road unless painted angle-parking lines indicate otherwise.

sec07-card-r14.front: How much clearance must you leave between your parked vehicle and cars parked ahead or behind?
sec07-card-r14.expected_back: Leave at least two feet between your parked vehicle and vehicles ahead or behind.

sec07-card-r15.front: Where should you position your vehicle relative to travel lanes when parking along a road?
sec07-card-r15.expected_back: Use a marked parking area and move as far out of travel lanes as available shoulder space permits.

sec07-card-r16.front: What is the maximum legal distance your wheels may sit from the curb when parked alongside it?
sec07-card-r16.expected_back: Beside a curb, park as close as practical and no farther than eighteen inches away.

sec07-card-r17.front: How should you secure the brake and transmission when parking an automatic versus a manual car?
sec07-card-r17.expected_back: Secure a parked vehicle with its parking brake and park gear, or first or reverse gear for a manual transmission.

sec07-card-r18.front: Which principle guides turning your front wheels when parking on any hill, with or without a curb?
sec07-card-r18.expected_back: For hill parking, arrange the wheels so an unintended roll is stopped by the curb, or without a curb moves off the road rather than into traffic.

sec07-card-r19.front: Which side should you exit from when possible, and what must you check before opening a street-side door?
sec07-card-r19.expected_back: Exit on the curb side when possible; before opening a traffic-side door, look behind for vehicles and especially bicycles.

sec07-card-r20.front: What three security steps should you take before walking away from a parked vehicle?
sec07-card-r20.expected_back: When leaving the car, switch off the engine and remove the key, and lock it if it will be out of sight.

sec07-card-r21.front: What is required to legally park in a reserved disability parking space?
sec07-card-r21.expected_back: Under the described municipal restrictions, reserved disability parking requires the appropriate permit or plates.

sec07-card-r22.front: What state-law fine does the Maine manual list for misusing disability license plates or placards?
sec07-card-r22.expected_back: The manual lists a one hundred dollars state-law fine for misuse of disability plates or placards.

sec07-card-r23.front: How may towns and cities regulate curbside loading zones?
sec07-card-r23.expected_back: A municipality may prohibit parking in loading zones.

sec07-card-r24.front: Under the handbook's municipal parking examples, how close to a fire hydrant is parking prohibited?
sec07-card-r24.expected_back: The municipal examples prohibit parking within ten feet of a hydrant where that ordinance applies.

sec07-card-r25.front: How close to a fire-station driveway, or across from it, do the municipal examples ban parking?
sec07-card-r25.expected_back: The municipal examples prohibit parking within fifteen feet of a fire-station driveway or directly opposite its entrance.

sec07-card-r26.front: Within what distance of a crosswalk do the municipal ordinance examples prohibit parking?
sec07-card-r26.expected_back: The municipal examples prohibit parking within fifteen feet of a crosswalk.

sec07-card-r27.front: How may municipalities restrict curb space outside entrances to public buildings?
sec07-card-r27.expected_back: Municipal restrictions may reserve public-place entrances from parking during designated hours.

sec07-card-r28.front: What two conditions are required to use a disability parking space paired with a striped access aisle?
sec07-card-r28.expected_back: Using a disability space with an access aisle requires displaying a disability plate or placard and using the aisle for vehicle entry or exit, such as with a lift or mobility device.

sec07-card-r29.front: Is parking inside a striped disability access aisle ever allowed, and what minimum fine applies?
sec07-card-r29.expected_back: Parking in an access aisle is prohibited, and misuse is a traffic infraction with a fine of at least two hundred dollars.

sec07-card-r30.front: What two visual cues along a street or lot tell you whether parking is banned or time-limited?
sec07-card-r30.expected_back: Check signs and painted curbs for parking prohibitions or limits.

sec07-card-r31.front: What four steps take you cleanly into an angle or ninety-degree parking stall?
sec07-card-r31.expected_back: To enter an angle or perpendicular space, check traffic, signal, center the vehicle and stop at the front of the space.

sec07-card-r32.front: How far straight back should you reverse before turning the wheel when leaving an angle or perpendicular stall?
sec07-card-r32.expected_back: When leaving an angle or perpendicular space, keep checking traffic and reverse until the front bumper clears the neighboring vehicle.

sec07-card-r33.front: Once your front bumper clears the car beside you while backing from a stall, how do you finish leaving?
sec07-card-r33.expected_back: After that clearance, steer toward the desired rearward direction, stop once clear of the space, select drive and move ahead.

sec07-card-r34.front: How do you line up beside the forward car to begin parallel parking?
sec07-card-r34.expected_back: For the described parallel-parking setup, check traffic and signal, then align beside the car ahead of the space about two feet away.

sec07-card-r35.front: Once aligned and traffic is clear, which way do you steer as you start backing into a right-side parallel space?
sec07-card-r35.expected_back: In the parallel-parking method, select reverse only when clear, look rearward and turn right while backing slowly.

sec07-card-r36.front: At what visual landmark do you straighten the wheels during the Maine parallel-parking method?
sec07-card-r36.expected_back: In that method, straighten the wheels after the front door passes the forward car’s rear bumper, then continue backing straight.

sec07-card-r37.front: Once your front end clears the forward car during parallel parking, how do you swing the nose into line?
sec07-card-r37.expected_back: Once clear of the forward car, steer left while backing and stop before touching the rear vehicle.

sec07-card-r38.front: How do you finish centering your car inside a parallel space on flat ground?
sec07-card-r38.expected_back: Steer right and pull forward to center the vehicle in the parallel space; straighten the wheels unless parked on a hill.

sec07-card-r39.front: After parallel parking, what target distance from the curb should you aim for, and what is the hard limit?
sec07-card-r39.expected_back: After parallel parking, aim for about six inches from the curb and never exceed eighteen inches.

sec07-card-r40.front: Why might you need to tweak standard parallel-parking reference landmarks?
sec07-card-r40.expected_back: The described parking reference points may require adjustment for the vehicle’s size.

sec07-card-r41.front: What first move creates steering room before pulling forward out of a tight parallel space?
sec07-card-r41.expected_back: To leave a parallel space, check traffic, brake and back near the rear vehicle, then signal, select drive and move forward slowly.

sec07-card-r42.front: What must you verify before angling out of a parallel spot, and what if the gap is too tight?
sec07-card-r42.expected_back: Before steering out of a parallel space, confirm the front bumper clears the forward car; otherwise reverse and readjust.

sec07-card-r43.front: During a parallel-parking exit, when should you move promptly out into the travel lane?
sec07-card-r43.expected_back: In the described parallel-space exit, move promptly into the lane once the doorpost clears the forward car’s rear bumper.

sec07-card-r44.front: Which shoulder do you look over when pulling out from a right curb versus a left one-way curb?
sec07-card-r44.expected_back: From a right-side parking position, look over the left shoulder; from a left curb, look over the right shoulder before entering traffic.

sec07-card-r45.front: When is it safe to signal and pull slowly away from a curb parking space?
sec07-card-r45.expected_back: Signal and pull out slowly only when the destination lane is clear for a safe distance.

sec07-card-r46.front: If circling around the block is not possible, what roadside openings allow a two-point turnaround?
sec07-card-r46.expected_back: When going around the block is unavailable, a street, alley or driveway may serve for a two-point turnaround.

sec07-card-r47.front: Why is backing into a driveway preferred for a two-point turnaround, and where do you stop first?
sec07-card-r47.expected_back: For a reverse two-point turnaround, check behind, signal right and drive one car length beyond the driveway before looking over the right shoulder and backing into it.

sec07-card-r48.front: Once backed into the driveway during a reverse two-point turnaround, how do you re-enter the road?
sec07-card-r48.expected_back: After backing into the driveway for that turnaround, select drive, check traffic and turn left into the proper lane only when clear, with a left signal.

sec07-card-r49.front: How do you enter a driveway or alley when starting a forward two-point turnaround?
sec07-card-r49.expected_back: For a forward two-point turnaround, check oncoming traffic, signal left and turn into the drive or alley near its right side.

sec07-card-r50.front: After pulling nose-first into a driveway for a turnaround, when do you stop and how do you prep reverse?
sec07-card-r50.expected_back: In the forward method, stop once the rear clears the driveway edge, then check traffic, signal right and select reverse.

sec07-card-r51.front: How do you back out and complete a forward two-point turnaround once traffic is clear?
sec07-card-r51.expected_back: When clear, back with a sharp right steer, straighten and stop centered in the lane, then select drive and cancel the signal.

sec07-card-r52.front: Under what narrow condition should you ever perform a three-point turnaround?
sec07-card-r52.expected_back: Use a three-point turnaround only on a two-lane road too narrow for a U-turn, preferring a trip around the block where possible.

sec07-card-r53.front: How do you position and signal to begin a three-point turnaround?
sec07-card-r53.expected_back: Begin the three-point method by checking mirrors, signaling right and stopping at the road’s right side.

sec07-card-r54.front: After stopping at the right edge in a three-point turn, what checks, signal, and steering move cross the road?
sec07-card-r54.expected_back: Next signal left, check traffic and the left blind spot, and when clear turn sharply left across the road and stop.

sec07-card-r55.front: What checks and wheel cut take you backward during the middle leg of a three-point turn?
sec07-card-r55.expected_back: Then select reverse, check traffic and both blind spots, and when clear steer sharply right while backing across and stop.

sec07-card-r56.front: How do you complete the final forward leg of a three-point turnaround?
sec07-card-r56.expected_back: Finish by selecting drive, signaling left and checking traffic and blind spots before moving into the right lane in the new direction, then cancel the signal.

sec09-card-f01.front: Which three vehicle-control options does the Maine manual give to avoid a crash or soften impact?
sec09-card-f01.expected_back: Braking, steering and acceleration are the manual’s three possible ways to avoid a collision or lessen its impact.

sec09-card-f02.front: What vital control advantage do antilock brakes preserve during a hard stop?
sec09-card-f02.expected_back: Antilock brakes help maintain steering control during a stop.

sec09-card-f03.front: Where should you check the operating instructions for your vehicle's antilock braking system?
sec09-card-f03.expected_back: Read the vehicle owner’s manual for instructions on using its antilock braking system.

sec09-card-f04.front: What pedal sensation and sound can occur while an antilock braking system is working?
sec09-card-f04.expected_back: An ABS pedal can vibrate and the system can make a clicking sound during operation.

sec09-card-f05.front: Where should you look to confirm the proper emergency braking method for a vehicle without ABS?
sec09-card-f05.expected_back: For a vehicle without ABS, consult its owner’s manual for the appropriate braking method.

sec09-card-f06.front: When braking in time cannot prevent a crash, what maneuver may offer a safe escape?
sec09-card-f06.expected_back: If a collision cannot be avoided by stopping in time, steering around the hazard may provide an escape.

sec09-card-f07.front: Why should you stay off the brakes while steering around a hazard, especially onto a soft shoulder?
sec09-card-f07.expected_back: When steering around a hazard, avoid braking during the turn if possible, particularly when entering a soft shoulder.

sec09-card-f08.front: Which clock-face hand placements on opposite sides of the wheel give quick steering response?
sec09-card-f08.expected_back: For a quick steering response, hold opposite sides of the wheel at nine and three or eight and four.

sec09-card-f09.front: What steering follow-through applies immediately after you swerve clear of an obstacle?
sec09-card-f09.expected_back: After steering clear of an obstacle, countersteer toward the original lane and remain ready for another correction.

sec09-card-f10.front: How should you hold the steering wheel whenever performing an emergency steering move?
sec09-card-f10.expected_back: Grip the wheel with both hands when making an emergency steering maneuver.

sec09-card-f11.front: How do you choose an emergency escape direction and recover after passing the hazard?
sec09-card-f11.expected_back: Choose an escape direction that avoids other traffic, then straighten and reduce speed after clearing the hazard.

sec09-card-f12.front: Why must your eyes scan your escape path rather than locking only onto the obstacle?
sec09-card-f12.expected_back: A swerve can lead to a second collision, so watch the escape path as well as the initial obstacle.

sec09-card-f13.front: From which two approach angles might brisk acceleration help you dodge an incoming vehicle?
sec09-card-f13.expected_back: Acceleration may sometimes avoid a vehicle about to strike from the side or rear.

sec09-card-f14.front: How does executing an emergency acceleration escape differ between manual and automatic transmissions?
sec09-card-f14.expected_back: For that acceleration escape, a manual-transmission vehicle may need a downshift; the automatic-transmission example uses the accelerator.

sec09-card-f15.front: What rule governs reading printed material behind the wheel in Maine, and what two items are excluded?
sec09-card-f15.expected_back: Reading printed material while driving is prohibited, with a map and written directions to a particular destination excluded from that definition.

sec09-card-f16.front: What pedal action should you stay ready for if a vehicle is about to rear-end you?
sec09-card-f16.expected_back: If a rear impact is imminent, be prepared to brake so the vehicle is not pushed into one ahead.

sec09-card-f17.front: What should you stay prepared to do if a side collision spins your vehicle?
sec09-card-f17.expected_back: If a side impact spins the vehicle, be ready to steer to try to regain control.

sec09-card-f18.front: What are your first three responsibilities immediately after being involved in a crash?
sec09-card-f18.expected_back: After a crash, stop immediately, assist injured people as possible and arrange an ambulance when needed.

sec09-card-f19.front: When is moving an injured person at a crash scene justified?
sec09-card-f19.expected_back: Do not move an injured person unless another danger requires moving them to safety.

sec09-card-f20.front: How long does the Maine manual direct crash-involved drivers to remain at the scene?
sec09-card-f20.expected_back: The manual directs involved drivers to remain at the crash scene until police arrive and question those involved.

sec09-card-f21.front: What should you do with your crashed vehicle if it can still be driven safely?
sec09-card-f21.expected_back: Move the crashed vehicle out of the traffic path if you can do so.

sec09-card-f22.front: From which three groups at a crash scene should you gather names and addresses?
sec09-card-f22.expected_back: Collect names and addresses for everyone involved, injured people and witnesses.

sec09-card-f23.front: Which details should you record from the other driver, and what cross-check should you perform?
sec09-card-f23.expected_back: Record the other driver’s name, address and license number, checking that the name matches the license.

sec09-card-f24.front: What six vehicle, damage, and coverage items should you write down about the other car?
sec09-card-f24.memory_hook: Make, model, year, plate, damage, insurer
sec09-card-f24.expected_back: Record the other vehicle’s make, model, year and plate number, its damage and the insurance company’s name.

sec09-card-f25.front: Which time, location, and movement details should you document at a collision site?
sec09-card-f25.expected_back: Document when and where the crash occurred and the vehicles’ and pedestrians’ positions and travel directions before and after it.

sec09-card-f26.front: Why should you jot down poor weather or pavement conditions right after a crash?
sec09-card-f26.expected_back: Record poor weather or road conditions relevant to the crash.

sec09-card-f27.front: When a crash involves injury, whom must you contact and how should you describe the event?
sec09-card-f27.expected_back: Contact police for a crash involving injury and give factual information about the event.

sec09-card-f28.front: What two-step duty applies if you bump or damage an unattended parked vehicle?
sec09-card-f28.expected_back: If you damage a parked vehicle, try to locate its owner; if unsuccessful, leave a note where the owner can find it.

sec09-card-f29.front: Which seven identification and incident details belong on a note left for a damaged parked car?
sec09-card-f29.memory_hook: Name, address, license, plate, time, damage
sec09-card-f29.expected_back: The parked-vehicle note should identify you by name, address, driver-license number and plate, and give the crash date, time and damage description.

sec09-card-f30.front: Which crashes must be reported to Maine police or the local sheriff?
sec09-card-f30.expected_back: The pinned manual requires a report to police or the local sheriff for any crash injury or property damage of at least two thousand dollars.

sec09-card-f31.front: What two serious consequences can follow failing to report a legally reportable crash?
sec09-card-f31.expected_back: Failing to report a reportable crash can lead to criminal charges and suspension of the driver’s license.

sec09-card-f32.front: Whom must you notify after hitting and injuring or killing a dog, cat, or livestock in an otherwise minor crash?
sec09-card-f32.expected_back: For an otherwise nonreportable crash injuring or killing a dog, cat or livestock, take reasonable steps to notify the owner or, if unavailable, law enforcement or animal control.

sec09-card-f33.front: How should you drive past a collision where medical crews and officers are already working?
sec09-card-f33.expected_back: When emergency medical responders are already at a crash, follow their instructions and keep attention on the road and traffic officers.

sec09-card-r01.front: What should you do if you come upon an injury crash before anyone else is there?
sec09-card-r01.expected_back: If you encounter an injury crash with no one else present, try to help the victims.

sec09-card-r02.front: How should bystanders treat fallen utility wires at a crash scene?
