sec08-card-r74.front: How should you handle another driver's blind spot during normal cruising and while overtaking?
sec08-card-r74.expected_back: Move ahead or fall back to leave another driver’s blind spot, and pass through it promptly when overtaking.

sec11-card-f01.front: How does darkness change sight distance, and where should your eyes scan?
sec11-card-f01.expected_back: Night driving reduces the distance you can see, so search ahead and along both pavement edges.

sec11-card-f02.front: When should you use high-beam headlights at night, and when must you dim them?
sec11-card-f02.expected_back: Use high beams when there is no oncoming traffic, and dim them for an approaching vehicle.

sec11-card-f03.front: Where should you look if an oncoming driver forgets to dim bright high beams?
sec11-card-f03.expected_back: If an approaching driver leaves bright headlights on, look toward the roadway’s right edge instead of staring at the lights.

sec11-card-f04.front: Behind traffic and in which three weather conditions must you run low-beam headlights?
sec11-card-f04.expected_back: Use low beams when following another vehicle and in fog, rain or snow.

sec11-card-f05.front: Why should you keep scanning past the bright pool of your headlights at night?
sec11-card-f05.expected_back: Keep scanning around the vehicle and beyond the lit area for dark objects or shapes.

sec11-card-f06.front: Why must you avoid sunglasses or colored lenses at night and on overcast days?
sec11-card-f06.expected_back: Avoid sunglasses and colored lenses at night or on cloudy days because they reduce available light.

sec11-card-f07.front: At least how much extra following time does the Maine manual add for ordinary night driving?
sec11-card-f07.expected_back: At night, the manual advises adding at least one second to the following gap.

sec11-card-f08.front: How much time should you add to your following gap on unfamiliar roads at night?
sec11-card-f08.expected_back: For unfamiliar roads at night, the manual specifies an addition of at least two seconds.

sec11-card-f09.front: What three roadway changes commonly appear inside a construction work zone?
sec11-card-f09.expected_back: A work zone can include closed lanes, detours and heavy equipment near or on the road.

sec11-card-f10.front: Why must you still slow down through a work zone when no workers are on site?
sec11-card-f10.expected_back: Slow through a work zone even when workers are absent because narrowed lanes and uneven pavement remain hazards.

sec11-card-f11.front: Which five markers, vehicles, and people require active scanning in a work zone?
sec11-card-f11.expected_back: Watch work-zone signs, cones, drums, large vehicles and people.

sec11-card-f12.front: What does a flashing or sequencing arrow panel warn of, and how should you respond?
sec11-card-f12.expected_back: A flashing or sequencing arrow panel can announce a lane closure; slow and move toward the indicated open lane.

sec11-card-f13.front: What color combination and typical shape identify construction warning signs?
sec11-card-f13.expected_back: Construction warning signs generally show black text or symbols on orange and are often diamond-shaped.

sec11-card-f14.front: Which five physical devices guide traffic safely along construction paths?
sec11-card-f14.expected_back: Barricades, vertical panels, concrete barriers, drums and cones guide drivers through construction areas.

sec11-card-f15.front: How should you position your car and set your speed alongside construction channeling devices?
sec11-card-f15.expected_back: Near channeling devices, keep the vehicle centered in its lane and use a responsible speed.

sec11-card-f16.front: What lane-change rule applies as you are leaving a construction work zone?
sec11-card-f16.expected_back: On leaving a work zone, hold your lane and speed and wait until fully clear before changing lanes.

sec11-card-f17.front: What gear and signals do work-zone flaggers use, and how must drivers respond?
sec11-card-f17.expected_back: Flaggers use high-visibility clothing, paddles, flags and hand signals to direct traffic; follow their signals patiently.

sec11-card-f18.front: What three speed and spacing adjustments protect you inside every work zone?
sec11-card-f18.expected_back: In a work zone, lower speed, enlarge the following gap and remain ready to stop.

sec11-card-f19.front: How should you position around crews and equipment, and how should you treat empty night work zones?
sec11-card-f19.expected_back: Keep clear of workers and construction vehicles and use extra caution at night even when workers are absent.

sec11-card-f20.front: How far must you keep obeying temporary work-zone controls?
sec11-card-f20.expected_back: Continue following work-zone controls until the End Road Work sign.

sec11-card-f21.front: Which three pre-trip steps help you handle construction delays calmly?
sec11-card-f21.expected_back: Plan for construction delays, leave early and choose another route when possible.

sec11-card-f22.front: Why must you drop speed and stretch your following gap on dirt or gravel roads?
sec11-card-f22.expected_back: On dirt or gravel, slow and increase the following gap because tire grip is reduced.

sec11-card-f23.front: How should you drive along narrow rural roads where opposing cars may crowd the middle?
sec11-card-f23.expected_back: On narrow rural roads, slow, stay centered in your lane and watch for oncoming vehicles crowding it.

sec11-card-f24.front: Who holds priority at a single-lane rural bridge, and how should traffic flow?
sec11-card-f24.expected_back: The single-lane bridge guidance gives the first arriving driver priority and calls for taking turns.

sec11-card-f25.front: What three adjustments apply when crossing an open-grating or steel bridge?
sec11-card-f25.expected_back: For an open-grating or steel bridge, reduce speed, increase the gap ahead and hold the wheel firmly.

sec11-card-f26.front: How should you drive where dense woods, tall crops, or hill crests block sightlines?
sec11-card-f26.expected_back: Where woods, crops or hills block the view, slow and prepare to stop.

sec11-card-f27.front: How should you approach a rural intersection that has no traffic signals or stop-or-yield signs?
sec11-card-f27.expected_back: At a rural intersection without signals or stop slash yield signs, approach slowly and be ready for crossing traffic or an oncoming turn.

sec11-card-f28.front: Which three driving adjustments belong on slick winter pavement?
sec11-card-f28.expected_back: On slick winter roads, use lower speeds, gentler braking and turns, and a larger following gap.

sec11-card-f29.front: Which vehicle parts and systems should be checked and inspected before winter weather arrives?
sec11-card-f29.memory_hook: Tires, antifreeze, hoses, exhaust, battery, brakes
sec11-card-f29.expected_back: Before winter weather, check vehicle condition and tires and have antifreeze, hoses, exhaust, battery and brakes inspected.

sec11-card-f30.front: What engine-oil and battery-terminal care helps vehicles start reliably in Maine winters?
sec11-card-f30.expected_back: Use oil suitable for winter conditions and keep battery terminals clean.

sec11-card-f31.front: How can you safely gauge road grip and pick a safe speed in winter?
sec11-card-f31.expected_back: At low speed, occasional gentle brake checks can help assess grip and choose an appropriate speed.

sec11-card-f32.front: Why must you avoid sudden hard braking on snowy or icy pavement?
sec11-card-f32.expected_back: Avoid sudden hard braking on slippery pavement because a locked wheel can worsen a skid.

sec11-card-f33.front: How much space should you leave behind the car ahead on snow-covered or icy roads?
sec11-card-f33.expected_back: Allow a substantial gap behind the vehicle ahead on snow or ice.

sec11-card-f34.front: How should you approach winter hills and curves and handle the steering wheel?
sec11-card-f34.expected_back: Approach hills and bends more slowly and turn the steering wheel gradually.

sec11-card-f35.front: Which glass, heating, lighting, and fluid checks maintain winter visibility?
sec11-card-f35.memory_hook: Clear glass, wipers, defroster, headlights, washer
sec11-card-f35.expected_back: Keep windows clear and check that wipers, defroster and headlights work, with enough washer fluid available.

sec11-card-f36.front: What four techniques help free a vehicle stuck in deep snow without digging deeper?
sec11-card-f36.expected_back: If stuck in snow, avoid spinning the wheels, keep them near straight, clear snow around them and use traction mats, sand or cat litter.

sec11-card-f37.front: Where should you stay while rescue help is on the way during a winter breakdown?
sec11-card-f37.expected_back: The winter-stranding guidance advises staying with the vehicle while awaiting help.

sec11-card-r01.front: What visual markers should you display on and around a winter-stranded vehicle?
sec11-card-r01.expected_back: For a winter-stranded vehicle, display a red flag and, if available, warning flares in front and behind.

sec11-card-r02.front: How should you and your passengers stay warm inside a winter-stranded car?
sec11-card-r02.expected_back: Use blankets or available warm clothing for yourself and passengers while awaiting winter assistance.

sec11-card-r03.front: Why must you keep snow cleared away from a stranded vehicle's exhaust pipe?
sec11-card-r03.expected_back: The manual warns to keep snow clear of the exhaust outlet to reduce carbon-monoxide danger.

sec11-card-r04.front: Which eight items belong in the Maine manual's suggested winter emergency kit?
sec11-card-r04.memory_hook: Shovel, scraper, sand, cables, gear, flares
sec11-card-r04.expected_back: The suggested winter kit includes a shovel, ice scraper, sand, jumper cables, warm clothes and footwear, plus flares and a red flag.

sec11-card-r05.front: Which drivers must take reasonable steps to prevent snow or ice from blowing off their vehicle?
sec11-card-r05.expected_back: Drivers of vehicles weighing less than ten thousand pounds must take reasonable measures to keep snow or ice from falling off while driving.

sec11-card-r06.front: What is the safest choice in heavy fog, and how fast may you drive if travel is unavoidable?
sec11-card-r06.expected_back: Avoid driving in fog when possible; if travel is necessary, slow enough to stop within the distance you can see.

sec11-card-r07.front: Which headlight setting and pavement reference help guide you through fog?
sec11-card-r07.expected_back: In fog, use low-beam headlights and road-edge markings for guidance.

sec11-card-r08.front: What should you do if dense fog drops visibility too low to continue safely?
sec11-card-r08.expected_back: If fog makes visibility extremely poor, leave the road, stop with emergency flashers and wait for improvement.

sec11-card-r09.front: What three speed, space, and steering habits prevent skids on wet roads?
sec11-card-r09.expected_back: On wet roads, reduce speed, allow more stopping room and avoid sharp turns that can trigger a skid.

sec11-card-r10.front: Why is pavement especially slippery right as light rain begins falling?
sec11-card-r10.expected_back: The start of light rain can be particularly slick as road oil mixes with water.

sec11-card-r11.front: Which three vehicle features help you see and stay visible during rain?
sec11-card-r11.expected_back: Maintain wipers and defroster and use headlights so you can see and be seen in rain.

sec11-card-r12.front: How should you adjust turn signals and braking timing in rainy traffic?
sec11-card-r12.expected_back: In rain, signal turns and begin slowing early to give following drivers notice.

sec11-card-r13.front: What happens between your tires and the pavement during hydroplaning?
sec11-card-r13.expected_back: Hydroplaning occurs when tires ride on a water film instead of maintaining road contact.

sec11-card-r14.front: Which three speed and tire-care steps lower hydroplaning risk?
sec11-card-r14.expected_back: Reduce hydroplaning risk by slowing in rain, replacing worn tires and maintaining proper inflation.

sec11-card-r15.front: Should you ever try driving across a flooded stretch of roadway?
sec11-card-r15.expected_back: Do not attempt to drive through a flooded roadway.

sec11-card-r16.front: What structural hazard can murky floodwater hide, and when is it hardest to spot?
sec11-card-r16.expected_back: Floodwater can conceal an eroded or missing road, with the danger harder to recognize after dark.

sec11-card-r17.front: What must you do promptly if your vehicle stalls inside a flooded roadway?
sec11-card-r17.expected_back: If the vehicle stalls in a flooded roadway, the manual directs leaving it promptly and seeking higher ground.

sec11-card-r18.front: Why should you combine extra caution with lower speeds after dark?
sec11-card-r18.expected_back: Use extra caution and lower speed at night because darkness restricts visibility.

sec11-card-r19.front: Do wildlife collisions happen only during peak seasons, or when must Maine drivers stay alert?
sec11-card-r19.expected_back: Wildlife collisions can happen throughout the year, even though the manual describes seasonal peaks.

sec11-card-r20.front: During which season do Maine deer crashes climb, and which single month peaks?
sec11-card-r20.expected_back: The pinned manual describes deer-collision increases in autumn with a November peak.

sec11-card-r21.front: Which two late-spring months mark peak moose collisions in Maine, alongside autumn?
sec11-card-r21.expected_back: The manual identifies May and June as peak moose-collision months and notes autumn incidents too.

sec11-card-r22.front: Why are moose harder to spot by eye shine at night than deer?
sec11-card-r22.expected_back: At night, look for reflected deer eyes and the outline of a moose, whose greater height can hide its eye reflection from headlights.

sec11-card-r23.front: During which daily hours are moose and deer most active, and can crossings happen outside them?
sec11-card-r23.expected_back: Be especially watchful for moose and deer from dusk to dawn, while remembering an encounter can occur at any hour.

sec11-card-r24.front: What do posted moose and deer warning signs tell you about that stretch of road?
sec11-card-r24.expected_back: Moose and deer signs mark places with concentrated wildlife or a history of collisions.

sec11-card-r25.front: Why must you keep scanning after one deer or moose clears your lane?
sec11-card-r25.expected_back: After one deer or moose crosses, watch for others because these animals often move in groups.

sec11-card-r26.front: What should you do when you encounter a moose standing on or beside the road?
sec11-card-r26.expected_back: For a moose near or on the road, slow, remain in the vehicle and allow room and time for it to leave.

sec11-card-r27.front: Why must you never try squeezing around a moose or stepping out to shoo it off?
sec11-card-r27.expected_back: Do not drive around a moose or get out to watch or chase it away.

sec11-card-r28.front: What is the initial rule if a collision with an animal in your path cannot be avoided?
sec11-card-r28.expected_back: If impact with an animal is imminent, the initial guidance is to brake and keep steering straight.

sec11-card-r29.front: How far may cargo project past the left and right fenders of a passenger vehicle in Maine?
sec11-card-r29.expected_back: A passenger-vehicle load must not project beyond the left fenders or more than six inches beyond the right fenders.

sec11-card-r30.front: When is carrying passengers or cargo inside your cabin unlawful?
sec11-card-r30.expected_back: Do not drive with passengers or a load blocking forward or side vision or interfering with control use.

sec11-card-r31.front: Are riders ever permitted to perch on the exterior hood, roof, or trunk while moving?
sec11-card-r31.expected_back: Passengers must not sit on the hood, roof or trunk of a moving vehicle.

sec11-card-r32.front: In which enclosed cargo areas and towed trailers is riding barred on a highway?
sec11-card-r32.expected_back: While a vehicle moves on a highway, people may not ride in its trunk or in a camp trailer, mobile home, semitrailer or utility trailer.

sec11-card-r33.front: Under what age must pickup passengers ride inside the cab, and what four exceptions exist?
sec11-card-r33.expected_back: Pickup passengers younger than nineteen must use the passenger compartment, except qualifying work or training travel, licensed-hunter travel to or from hunting, parade participation, or a belted manufacturer-installed outside seat.

sec11-card-r34.front: How must a dog riding in an open pickup bed be protected on public ways, and what exceptions apply?
sec11-card-r34.expected_back: On a public way, an open vehicle must secure a dog against falling, jumping or being thrown out, except qualifying farmer or farm-employee agricultural work needing the dog, a hunting dog at a hunting site, or licensed-hunter transport between hunting sites.

sec01-card-f01.question_text: What mental focus and three physical responses must you stay ready for to prevent collisions?
sec01-card-f01.teaching_text: Split-second hazards vanish cleanly only when your eyes stay engaged and hands anticipate braking or steering.

sec01-card-f02.question_text: Unless a permit or statutory exemption applies, what credential does a Maine resident need to drive?
sec01-card-f02.teaching_text: Driving on public roads as a settled state resident without a Maine credential or valid exemption breaks law.

sec01-card-f03.question_text: Within how many days after establishing Maine residency must a licensed newcomer apply and surrender their old license?
sec01-card-f03.teaching_text: Holding onto an out-of-state card past thirty days of Maine residency leaves your driving status invalid.

sec01-card-f04.question_text: What minimum age and licensing experience must a resident learner-permit holder's accompanying driver have?
sec01-card-f04.teaching_text: Riding with a nineteen-year-old friend or brand-new licensee counts as unsupervised permit driving.

sec01-card-f05.question_text: Where inside the vehicle must the licensed supervisor sit when accompanying a resident permit holder?
sec01-card-f05.teaching_text: Sitting in the front passenger seat lets the coach spot hazards and intervene immediately.

sec01-card-f06.question_text: At what minimum age may a nonresident drive in Maine using a valid home-state license or permit?
sec01-card-f06.teaching_text: Even if another state issues permits at fourteen or fifteen, Maine roads require nonresidents to be sixteen.

sec01-card-f07.question_text: When may military personnel drive in Maine using a valid military license?
sec01-card-f07.teaching_text: Federal military credentials cover official duty vehicles, whereas personal cars follow regular licensing rules.

sec01-card-f08.question_text: How old must an applicant be to qualify for a Maine learner permit?
sec01-card-f08.teaching_text: Fifteen marks the earliest birthday you can enter Maine's supervised learning stage.

sec01-card-f09.question_text: What educational requirement applies to any Maine learner-permit applicant under age eighteen?
sec01-card-f09.teaching_text: Maine requires structured classroom and behind-the-wheel instruction before any minor obtains a learner permit.

sec01-card-f10.question_text: Which examination must you pass to receive a Maine learner permit?
sec01-card-f10.teaching_text: Proving command of road signs, right-of-way, and state traffic laws comes before supervised street practice.

sec01-card-f11.question_text: How long does a Maine learner permit generally remain valid?
sec01-card-f11.teaching_text: Two full years gives ample time to log required practice hours and pass your road test.

sec01-card-f12.question_text: Which vehicle class must a permit supervisor's own license cover?
sec01-card-f12.teaching_text: A standard passenger-car driver cannot legally supervise someone practicing in a heavier vehicle class.

sec01-card-f13.question_text: What does Maine's learner-permit guidance forbid regarding mobile phones and handheld electronics?
sec01-card-f13.teaching_text: New learners need undivided visual and mental bandwidth without phone calls or screen taps.

sec01-card-f14.question_text: How are written exams and vision screenings arranged at Maine motor-vehicle branches?
sec01-card-f14.teaching_text: Booking your appointment ahead prevents wasted walk-in trips when local branch testing rooms fill up.

sec01-card-f15.question_text: How many identification documents does Maine's permit application guidance call for?
sec01-card-f15.teaching_text: Arriving short one acceptable ID stalls your permit application at the counter.

sec01-card-f16.question_text: When must you provide your Social Security number, and does Maine print it on the license face?
sec01-card-f16.teaching_text: State records verify your Social Security number at application and renewal while keeping the card private.

sec01-card-f17.question_text: Which two documents establish date of birth for Maine applicants aged twenty-two or younger?
sec01-card-f17.teaching_text: Younger applicants must verify exact age for graduated licensing rules using official civil records.

sec01-card-f18.question_text: What makes a birth-certificate photocopy acceptable at the BMV, and why does a notary stamp fail?
sec01-card-f18.teaching_text: Only the vital-records agency's raised seal or stamp proves authenticity; private notary stamps get rejected.

sec01-card-f19.question_text: Which lettered license class does Maine issue to most standard everyday drivers?
sec01-card-f19.teaching_text: Knowing Maine's standard noncommercial passenger credential is Class C prevents confusion with Class A or B.

sec01-card-f20.question_text: How can a Maine teen qualify for a driver license as early as age sixteen?
sec01-card-f20.teaching_text: Finishing an approved driver-education course unlocks Maine's earliest full-test eligibility at sixteen.

sec01-card-f21.question_text: What is the minimum age to obtain a Maine driver license without completing approved driver education?
sec01-card-f21.teaching_text: Skipping approved driver education delays license eligibility by two full years until your eighteenth birthday.

sec01-card-f22.question_text: How long must an applicant younger than twenty-one hold a learner permit before requesting a road test?
sec01-card-f22.teaching_text: Maine enforces a six-month supervised holding period from issue date for everyone under twenty-one.

sec01-card-f23.question_text: How many total and night practice hours—and with what supervisor—must an under-21 applicant complete?
sec01-card-f23.teaching_text: Logging seventy supervised hours including ten after dark with a 20-plus two-year driver builds real road seasoning.

sec01-card-f24.question_text: What final behind-the-wheel requirement stands between a road-test applicant and a Maine license?
sec01-card-f24.teaching_text: Demonstrating live traffic control to an examiner is the final step before licensure.

sec01-card-f25.question_text: Where do you mail your request form or driving log to schedule a Maine road test?
sec01-card-f25.teaching_text: Centralized scheduling runs through the main Bureau of Motor Vehicles headquarters in Augusta.

sec01-card-f26.question_text: Which two personal documents must you bring to your scheduled road test?
sec01-card-f26.teaching_text: Forgetting either your permit or your scheduled notice cancels the exam at check-in.

sec01-card-f27.question_text: What kind of vehicle and vehicle document must a road-test applicant supply?
sec01-card-f27.teaching_text: BMV examiners do not supply cars and verify valid registration and inspection stickers before getting in.

sec01-card-f28.question_text: Who must accompany a learner-permit holder arriving for a scheduled road test?
sec01-card-f28.teaching_text: Driving solo to your road test violates your permit before the exam even starts.

sec01-card-f29.question_text: What option do you have if snow or ice hits on your scheduled road-test day?
sec01-card-f29.teaching_text: Maine waives rescheduling fees during winter storms so learners never feel pressured onto icy roads.

sec01-card-f30.question_text: May a newly licensed Maine driver younger than eighteen use a mobile phone or handheld device?
sec01-card-f30.teaching_text: Solo driving raises cognitive load sharply, making phone calls or texts illegal for minor licensees.

sec01-card-f31.question_text: Between which overnight hours may an initially restricted driver under eighteen not drive?
sec01-card-f31.teaching_text: Fatigue and dark rural highways make midnight-to-5-a.m. hours the riskiest window for new teen drivers.

sec01-card-f32.question_text: When may an initially restricted driver under eighteen carry nonfamily passengers?
sec01-card-f32.teaching_text: Peer passengers spike teen crash rates unless a 20-plus two-year class-licensed supervisor sits adjacent.

sec01-card-f33.question_text: How many days do initial restrictions last for newly licensed Maine drivers younger than eighteen?
sec01-card-f33.teaching_text: Roughly nine clean months of solo experience bridges the gap between road test and unrestricted teen driving.

sec01-card-f34.question_text: What two penalties hit if you violate an initial under-18 license restriction, even near age eighteen?
sec01-card-f34.teaching_text: That fresh 270-day restriction clock keeps running right past your eighteenth birthday.

sec01-card-f35.question_text: How long is a first Maine license provisional when issued before twenty-one versus at twenty-one or older?
sec01-card-f35.teaching_text: Every brand-new Maine driver starts on provisional status regardless of age, with younger drivers serving double.

sec01-card-f36.question_text: What happens to a provisional driver convicted of a moving violation?
sec01-card-f36.teaching_text: Even a single speeding or stop-sign conviction on a provisional card triggers a thirty-day suspension.

sec01-card-f37.question_text: What topics does Maine's written exam test, and which laws receive special emphasis?
sec01-card-f37.teaching_text: Expect heavy questioning on Maine drinking-and-driving statutes alongside road signs and safe handling.

sec01-card-f38.question_text: Which two visual abilities does Maine's BMV vision screening evaluate?
sec01-card-f38.teaching_text: Spotting cross-street hazards early demands wide peripheral awareness alongside crisp straight-ahead visual focus.

sec01-card-f39.question_text: What vehicle skills and traffic responses does the Maine road-test examiner score?
sec01-card-f39.teaching_text: Smooth handling counts only alongside timely reactions to walkers, signs, signals, and changing surfaces.

sec01-card-f40.question_text: When in the testing sequence does the behind-the-wheel road test take place?
sec01-card-f40.teaching_text: Written and vision checks must be passed completely before stepping onto the road course.

sec01-card-f41.question_text: Which examinations must a first-time Maine license applicant complete?
sec01-card-f41.teaching_text: Only prior valid license holders qualify for exam waivers; brand-new drivers complete the full slate.

sec01-card-f42.question_text: Which two Maine exams may be waived when transferring a valid out-of-state driver license?
sec01-card-f42.teaching_text: Holding a current license elsewhere often spares newcomers from retaking knowledge and driving exams.

sec01-card-f43.question_text: How old must an out-of-state licensed driver be to apply for a Maine transfer license?
sec01-card-f43.teaching_text: Fifteen-year-old license holders from rural states must wait until sixteen for a Maine operator card.

sec01-card-f44.question_text: What extra proof may a sixteen- or seventeen-year-old transferring driver have to show?
sec01-card-f44.teaching_text: Maine holds minor transfers to the same approved driver-education standard as local teens.

sec01-card-f45.question_text: What happens to your out-of-state license when Maine issues your replacement license?
sec01-card-f45.teaching_text: Drivers may hold only one active state operator license at a time.

sec01-card-f46.question_text: What immediate administrative and legal consequences follow a false statement on a license application?
sec01-card-f46.teaching_text: Falsifying identity, age, or suspension history revokes your Maine driving privilege on the spot.

sec01-card-r55.question_text: Which relatives and household members count as immediate family under Maine's teen passenger rule?
sec01-card-r55.teaching_text: Step, foster, exchange, ward, and deployed-military guardianship youth living together ride exempt from adult supervision.

sec01-card-r56.question_text: Which four family roles may sign the Secretary of State's form certifying practice driving hours?
sec01-card-r56.teaching_text: Unsigned or friend-signed practice logs get rejected when requesting your Maine road test.

sec01-card-r57.question_text: Who may certify practice driving hours when the applicant has no living or available parent?
sec01-card-r57.teaching_text: Maine adds an employer option so working youth without parents can still validate logged hours.

sec01-card-r58.question_text: What must you complete to change your Maine driver license to a different classification?
sec01-card-r58.teaching_text: Moving up to heavier vehicles requires proving both written knowledge and road skill for that class.

sec01-card-r59.question_text: Who may sign a license or instruction-permit application for a minor under age eighteen?
sec01-card-r59.teaching_text: A spouse signing for an under-eighteen applicant must be at least eighteen years old.

sec01-card-f47.question_text: How long is a Maine photo license valid for a driver younger than sixty-five?
sec01-card-f47.teaching_text: Drivers under sixty-five renew on a six-birthday cycle rather than every four years.

sec01-card-f48.question_text: How long does a Maine photo license last for an applicant aged sixty-five or older?
sec01-card-f48.teaching_text: Shorter four-birthday cycles starting at sixty-five keep vision and medical checks current.

sec01-card-f49.question_text: What two legal statuses must you prove with documentation for photo-license processing?
sec01-card-f49.teaching_text: Both federal lawful-presence status and in-state residence must be verified before card printing.

sec01-card-f50.question_text: Who must accompany an applicant under eighteen to sign for photo-license issuance?
sec01-card-f50.teaching_text: Even after passing the road test, minors need parent or guardian authorization for the photo card.

sec01-card-f51.question_text: What two duties apply to your physical driver license every time you drive?
sec01-card-f51.teaching_text: Leaving your wallet at home or refusing an officer's request violates Maine motor-vehicle law.

sec01-card-f52.question_text: Is lending your Maine driver license to a friend or relative ever legal?
sec01-card-f52.teaching_text: Handing your card to someone else invites unlawful-use prosecution and exposes your own driving privilege.

sec01-card-r01.question_text: What penalties can follow altering or changing information printed on a driver license?
sec01-card-r01.teaching_text: Altering birthdates or restrictions turns a plastic card into a revocable criminal offense.

sec01-card-r02.question_text: What two steps should you take if your driver license is lost or destroyed?
sec01-card-r02.teaching_text: Prompt reporting protects against identity misuse while getting legal plastic back in your wallet.

sec01-card-r03.question_text: Roughly how far ahead of expiration does the BMV mail a license renewal notice, and where?
sec01-card-r03.teaching_text: Outdated addresses on file mean missing that forty-five-day reminder and risking expired driving.

sec01-card-r04.question_text: May you legally drive with an expired Maine driver license?
sec01-card-r04.teaching_text: Maine provides zero grace days to keep driving once your birthday expiration passes.

sec01-card-r05.question_text: Within how many days must you notify the Bureau of Motor Vehicles after changing your name or address?
sec01-card-r05.teaching_text: Missing the thirty-day update window can cause missed summons or renewal mailings.

sec01-card-r06.question_text: What is the legal status of driving without corrective lenses or equipment listed on your license?
sec01-card-r06.teaching_text: Ignoring a corrective-lens or daylight-only restriction carries the weight of unlicensed driving.

sec01-card-r07.question_text: Can the Secretary of State require a driver to take a license exam or attend a hearing after issuance?
sec01-card-r07.teaching_text: A driver license remains a conditional privilege subject to safety review whenever concerns arise.

sec01-card-r08.question_text: Whose evaluation may the Secretary of State demand regarding a driver's physical or mental condition?
sec01-card-r08.teaching_text: Physician reports verify whether vision, seizure, or cognitive changes still permit safe driving.

sec01-card-r09.question_text: Who may submit a signed unsafe-driving report that prompts the State to suspend someone's license?
sec01-card-r09.teaching_text: Both law-enforcement officers and concerned everyday citizens can file signed unsafe-driving complaints with state officials.

sec01-card-r10.question_text: How can an adult who cosigned a minor's permit or license later ask the state to suspend it?
sec01-card-r10.teaching_text: Parents or guardians retain authority to withdraw consent and suspend a minor's credential through notarized paperwork.

sec01-card-r11.question_text: What does revocation do to a license, and what is required once the revocation period ends?
sec01-card-r11.teaching_text: Unlike temporary suspension, revocation terminates the credential completely and forces starting fresh afterward.

sec01-card-r12.question_text: How long is license revocation for vehicular manslaughter, and how does alcohol change it?
sec01-card-r12.teaching_text: Causing a fatal crash while alcohol-impaired permanently ends your legal privilege to drive in Maine.

sec01-card-r13.question_text: What is the minimum revocation length for a driver classified as a habitual offender?
sec01-card-r13.teaching_text: Stacking serious convictions triggers at least twelve full months off Maine roads.

sec01-card-r14.question_text: After a suspension period expires on the calendar, when may you actually resume driving?
sec01-card-r14.teaching_text: Driving the day after a suspension term ends—before written notice arrives—counts as driving suspended.

sec01-card-r15.question_text: What happens to your license if you fail to file required proof of insurance?
sec01-card-r15.teaching_text: Letting mandated financial-responsibility paperwork lapse gives state officials grounds to suspend your driving privilege.

sec01-card-r16.question_text: What license consequence follows failing to appear in court for a traffic citation?
sec01-card-r16.teaching_text: Ignoring a ticket date turns a routine citation into an active license suspension.

sec01-card-r17.question_text: What maximum suspension applies upon conviction for street racing, running a roadblock, or fleeing officers?
sec01-card-r17.teaching_text: Street racing, running roadblocks, and fleeing officers carry up to three months off the road.

sec01-card-r18.question_text: How much additional suspension time can follow a conviction for driving after suspension?
sec01-card-r18.teaching_text: Getting caught behind the wheel while suspended tacks two extra months onto your ban.

sec01-card-r19.question_text: How long can your license be suspended if convicted of ignoring an officer's signal to stop?
sec01-card-r19.teaching_text: Refusing an officer's signal to pull over exposes you to a thirty-day license suspension.

sec01-card-r20.question_text: What administrative suspension can result from leaving a crash scene involving bodily injury?
sec01-card-r20.teaching_text: Fleeing an injury collision brings at least a thirty-day suspension alongside criminal exposure.

sec01-card-r21.question_text: What license suspension can follow a conviction for driving alone on a learner permit?
sec01-card-r21.teaching_text: Skipping your required twenty-plus supervisor risks a thirty-day suspension before you ever license.

sec01-card-r22.question_text: What suspension length can follow a conviction for criminal operation without a license?
sec01-card-r22.teaching_text: Driving criminally without a valid credential suspends future licensing eligibility for thirty days.

sec01-card-r23.question_text: What license suspension can hit a driver convicted of passing a stopped school bus flashing red lights?
sec01-card-r23.teaching_text: Blowing past a loading school bus endangers children and puts your license on ice for thirty days.

sec01-card-r24.question_text: Exceeding the posted speed limit by at least how much can trigger a thirty-day license suspension?
sec01-card-r24.teaching_text: Going thirty miles per hour or more above posted signs crosses into suspension territory in Maine.

sec01-card-r25.question_text: What suspension can follow a conviction for altering a license or vehicle registration certificate?
sec01-card-r25.teaching_text: Changing dates or numbers on either your license or registration carries a thirty-day suspension.

sec01-card-r26.question_text: How long a suspension can follow a conviction for lending your driver license to someone else?
sec01-card-r26.teaching_text: Letting someone borrow your ID can park your own driving privileges for thirty days.

sec01-card-r27.question_text: What suspension length may follow a conviction for unlawful use of a driver license?
sec01-card-r27.teaching_text: Misusing any state driver credential carries up to a thirty-day suspension once convicted in court.

sec01-card-r28.question_text: What suspension may result from a conviction for displaying a suspended driver license?
sec01-card-r28.teaching_text: Presenting an already-suspended credential as valid adds another thirty-day suspension onto your driving record.

sec01-card-r29.question_text: What license penalty may follow if you are convicted of lying on a registration or licensing form?
sec01-card-r29.teaching_text: Submitting false paperwork on either registration or licensing forms exposes you to thirty days suspended.

sec01-card-r30.question_text: How long may your license be suspended if convicted of lying to a law-enforcement officer?
sec01-card-r30.teaching_text: Giving a fake name or birthday during a traffic stop risks a thirty-day license suspension.

sec01-card-r31.question_text: How long may a court suspend driving privileges for an under-21 person's first fake-ID liquor offense?
sec01-card-r31.teaching_text: Using false credentials at a bar or liquor store hits your driving record even without a car.

sec01-card-r32.question_text: What license suspension hits an under-21 person adjudicated for a second false-ID liquor offense?
sec01-card-r32.teaching_text: A repeat underage fake-ID offense triples the driving ban from thirty days to ninety.

sec01-card-r33.question_text: How long is the license suspension for any underage false-ID liquor offense after the second?
sec01-card-r33.teaching_text: A third underage false-identification liquor adjudication costs an entire year of driving privileges.

sec01-card-r34.question_text: How many demerit points does Maine assign to the underage false-identification liquor offense?
sec01-card-r34.teaching_text: Six demerit points stack half the way toward point-accumulation trouble from one non-driving offense.

sec01-card-r35.question_text: When do demerit points drop off a Maine driver's record?
sec01-card-r35.teaching_text: Each point ages off individually once twelve clean months pass from assessment.

sec01-card-r36.question_text: What administrative review can a suspended Maine driver request, and what powers does the examiner hold?
sec01-card-r36.teaching_text: A Secretary of State hearing examiner can uphold, adjust, or overturn a license suspension.

sec01-card-r37.question_text: May a driver bring a lawyer to a suspension hearing, and which court hears appeals?
sec01-card-r37.teaching_text: Drivers hold full right to legal counsel at administrative hearings plus Superior Court judicial review.

sec01-card-r38.question_text: What crime class applies when a driver recklessly speeds off, sparking a blue-light-and-siren pursuit?
sec01-card-r38.teaching_text: Sparking a high-speed pursuit after an officer signals you to stop is a felony Class C crime.

sec01-card-r39.question_text: To which crime class does eluding police escalate if someone suffers serious bodily injury?
sec01-card-r39.teaching_text: Serious bodily harm during a police flight elevates the felony from Class C to Class B.

sec01-card-r40.question_text: What crash severity elevates knowingly or recklessly leaving the scene into a Class C felony crime?
sec01-card-r40.teaching_text: Leaving a scene where anyone is gravely hurt or killed carries felony Class C prosecution.

sec01-card-r41.question_text: How many violation-free credit points does each clean calendar year earn, and what is the cap?
sec01-card-r41.teaching_text: Banking up to four clean-driving credit points cushions your record against future demerits.

sec01-card-r42.question_text: How many hours long is Maine's approved Driving Dynamics driver-improvement course?
sec01-card-r42.teaching_text: Completing this five-hour defensive-driving class sharpens hazard habits and trims record points.

sec01-card-r43.question_text: How many points does Maine Driving Dynamics deduct, and how often may you claim that deduction?
sec01-card-r43.teaching_text: Maine limits defensive-driving point reductions to three points once every twelve months.

sec01-card-r44.question_text: Up to how much extra suspension can hit after accumulating three license suspensions within three years?
sec01-card-r44.teaching_text: Stacking three suspensions inside a three-year span triggers up to four extra months off-road.

sec01-card-r45.question_text: How long does a missed-summons or unpaid-fine suspension last, and is a work license available?
sec01-card-r45.teaching_text: Mandatory summons and fine suspensions allow no hardship or work-restricted driving exceptions.

sec01-card-r46.question_text: What BAC threshold, OUI conduct, or test refusal triggers mandatory suspension with zero work-license option?
sec01-card-r46.teaching_text: Impaired driving at 0.08 percent BAC or refusing chemical testing triggers ironclad suspension without work permits.
sec01-card-r46.must_match_memory_hook: OUI or refusal, zero work license

visual_sync.text_span: OUI or refusal, zero work license

sec01-card-r47.question_text: What minimum mandatory suspension—with no work-license option—applies to driving to endanger?
sec01-card-r47.teaching_text: Endangering others locks out your license for at least thirty days with zero work exceptions.

sec01-card-r48.question_text: What minimum ironclad suspension hits a minor caught carrying, holding, or drinking illegal alcohol inside a car?
sec01-card-r48.teaching_text: Even unopened illegal alcohol carried by a minor inside a vehicle brings thirty mandatory days suspended.

sec01-card-r49.question_text: What mandatory suspension hits a minor transporting illegal drugs in a motor vehicle?
sec01-card-r49.teaching_text: Carrying illegal drugs in a car as a minor triggers at least thirty days without work-license relief.

sec01-card-r50.question_text: What stays suspended—and until when—if an uninsured driver causes crash damage?
sec01-card-r50.teaching_text: Both your license and vehicle plates stay locked with no work option until insurance proof is filed.

sec01-card-r51.question_text: When may the Secretary of State suspend a license without holding a prior hearing?
sec01-card-r51.teaching_text: When evidence shows medical or mental inability to drive safely, public safety allows immediate suspension first.

sec01-card-r52.question_text: Does asking for an administrative hearing automatically lift an active suspension while you wait?
sec01-card-r52.teaching_text: Filing a hearing request does not restore driving rights while your hearing date is pending.

sec01-card-r53.question_text: When may a judge suspend your license over an unpaid criminal or civil-violation fine?
sec01-card-r53.teaching_text: Defaulting into court contempt on civil or criminal fines lets a judge suspend driving privileges.

sec01-card-r54.question_text: Can a Maine judge order your driver license suspended for an offense completely unrelated to driving?
sec01-card-r54.teaching_text: Maine courts hold statutory power to suspend licenses as a sanction even outside traffic law.

sec01-card-r60.question_text: Can someone with no driving record at all still earn credit from an approved driver-improvement course?
sec01-card-r60.teaching_text: Even someone without an existing driving record receives point credit after completing an approved program.

sec02-card-f01.question_text: What three baseline legal and mechanical requirements apply to any vehicle operated on Maine public roads?
sec02-card-f01.teaching_text: Taking an unregistered, uninsured, or neglected car onto public pavement violates Maine motor-vehicle law.

sec02-card-f02.question_text: Which legal document officially identifies who owns a vehicle?
sec02-card-f02.teaching_text: Registration plates authorize road use, whereas only the certificate of title establishes legal ownership.

sec02-card-f03.question_text: Alongside proving ownership, what financial claims does a vehicle title record?
sec02-card-f03.teaching_text: Checking the title reveals any unpaid bank or lender debts attached to the vehicle.

sec02-card-f04.question_text: What color title-application copy does a Maine dealer give you for your first registration?
sec02-card-f04.teaching_text: Town clerks and BMV branches check that blue dealer copy before issuing first-time plates.

sec02-card-f05.question_text: What title paperwork must a buyer submit when a vehicle was bought outside a Maine dealership?
sec02-card-f05.teaching_text: Private or out-of-state purchases require either the signed-over prior title or manufacturer's origin certificate.

sec02-card-f06.question_text: Who receives the physical vehicle title when there is no loan versus bank or credit-union financing?
sec02-card-f06.teaching_text: Banks and credit unions hold the paper title as collateral until the auto loan is paid.

sec02-card-f07.question_text: Where should you store your vehicle title instead of inside the car?
sec02-card-f07.teaching_text: Leaving a title in the glove compartment hands a car thief instant ownership paperwork.

sec02-card-f08.question_text: Which older vehicles are exempt from Maine's certificate-of-title requirement?
sec02-card-f08.teaching_text: Classic and older vehicles past the twenty-five-year mark register without needing a Maine title.

sec02-card-f09.question_text: Up to what unloaded weight is a trailer exempt from needing a Maine title?
sec02-card-f09.teaching_text: Small utility and boat trailers weighing 3,000 pounds or under unloaded skip formal titling.

sec02-card-f10.question_text: What should you do promptly if your vehicle title is stolen, lost, destroyed, or mutilated?
sec02-card-f10.teaching_text: Replacing missing or damaged ownership papers early avoids delays when selling or trading the car.

sec02-card-f11.question_text: What must accompany your duplicate application and fee when replacing a mutilated or unreadable title?
sec02-card-f11.teaching_text: Turning in the damaged original prevents two physical titles from circulating for one vehicle.

sec02-card-f12.question_text: Which four categories of road-used units must an owner register in Maine?
sec02-card-f12.teaching_text: Motor vehicles, mobile homes, trailers, and semitrailers moving on Maine roads all require current registration.

sec02-card-f13.question_text: Which local payment is step one of registering a vehicle in Maine?
sec02-card-f13.teaching_text: Maine collects annual vehicle excise tax through your municipal tax collector before issuing registration.

sec02-card-f14.question_text: Which towed commercial unit does the Maine manual list as exempt from vehicle excise tax?
sec02-card-f14.teaching_text: Unlike passenger cars and standard trailers, semitrailers are exempt from the described municipal excise tax.

sec02-card-f15.question_text: Which two vehicle factors determine how much Maine excise tax you owe?
sec02-card-f15.teaching_text: Maine bases excise rates on original manufacturer list price—not purchase price—scaled by vehicle age.

sec02-card-f16.question_text: What second role does your municipal excise-tax receipt serve?
sec02-card-f16.teaching_text: Keep that tax collector's receipt safe because it actually functions as the registration form.

sec02-card-f17.question_text: Which side and color copy of the registration form must you complete and sign before issuance?
sec02-card-f17.teaching_text: Leaving the reverse of the white registration copy unsigned halts plate issuance.

sec02-card-f18.question_text: Whose extra signature is required when someone under eighteen registers a vehicle in Maine?
sec02-card-f18.teaching_text: Minors under eighteen cannot complete a Maine vehicle registration without parent or guardian sign-off.

sec02-card-f19.question_text: Where can you obtain registration and plates once your municipal excise tax is paid?
sec02-card-f19.teaching_text: When town hall cannot finish plate issuance, visit a BMV branch or mail the Bureau.

sec02-card-f20.question_text: Why should you check with your local town office when registering a car in Maine?
sec02-card-f20.teaching_text: Participating municipalities act as registration agents, saving you a separate trip to the BMV.

sec02-card-f21.question_text: What passenger-vehicle registration fee does the Maine manual list?
sec02-card-f21.teaching_text: Standard passenger sedans carry a listed thirty-five-dollar state registration fee on top of excise tax.

sec02-card-f22.question_text: How long does a Maine vehicle registration stay valid?
sec02-card-f22.teaching_text: Registrations expire twelve months from the month issued, marked by your rear plate sticker.

sec02-card-f23.question_text: At what maximum gross vehicle weight does a pickup qualify for the thirty-five-dollar registration fee?
sec02-card-f23.teaching_text: Pickups rated at 6,000 pounds gross weight pay the same $35 state fee as cars.

sec02-card-f24.question_text: How are registration fees scaled for larger trucks above standard pickup weight?
sec02-card-f24.teaching_text: Heavier commercial and work trucks pay progressively higher fees matching road wear from gross weight.

sec02-card-f25.question_text: Which vehicle ages require submitting a title application at first Maine registration?
sec02-card-f25.teaching_text: Cars built within that quarter-century window require formal ownership-title paperwork when first getting Maine plates.

sec02-card-f26.question_text: Which tax form is required at a vehicle's first Maine registration to check if sales tax applies?
sec02-card-f26.teaching_text: First-time Maine registrations screen private and out-of-state purchases with a Use Tax Certificate.

sec02-card-f27.question_text: When must any owed vehicle sales tax be paid if not already collected by a dealer?
sec02-card-f27.teaching_text: Unpaid sales or use tax blocks first-time plate issuance at the counter.

sec02-card-f28.question_text: Who provides the sales-tax form for first registration when you buy from a Maine auto dealer?
sec02-card-f28.teaching_text: Licensed Maine dealers collect tax at sale and hand you the official proof for registration.

sec02-card-f29.question_text: Within how many days of declaring or establishing Maine residency must you apply to register your vehicle?
sec02-card-f29.teaching_text: Maine's thirty-day newcomer clock governs both your driver license and your vehicle registration.

sec02-card-f30.question_text: Who must maintain Maine liability insurance and show proof whenever police ask?
sec02-card-f30.teaching_text: Both the registered owner and whoever is behind the wheel share legal responsibility for coverage.

sec02-card-f31.question_text: Does a vehicle you drive need active liability insurance when someone else owns it?
sec02-card-f31.teaching_text: Driving an uninsured borrowed car puts the ticket and suspension risk directly on you.

sec02-card-f32.question_text: What two insurance habits should you follow before pulling onto the road?
sec02-card-f32.teaching_text: Active coverage at home still earns a citation if you carry no proof inside the car.

sec02-card-f33.question_text: What financial document must you show to register a motor vehicle in Maine?
sec02-card-f33.teaching_text: Registration clerks verify active Maine-compliant liability coverage before handing over plates or stickers.

sec02-card-f34.question_text: Which four types of documents count as valid evidence of Maine vehicle insurance?
sec02-card-f34.teaching_text: An insurer ID card, agent coverage letter, temporary binder, or summarized policy all satisfy police.

sec02-card-f35.question_text: What four details—and minimum standard—must a policy summary show to count as insurance proof?
sec02-card-f35.teaching_text: Any summary must name the car, insured, dates, and coverage meeting Maine minimum liability limits.

sec02-card-f36.question_text: What charge and privilege losses can follow failing to produce required insurance evidence?
sec02-card-f36.teaching_text: Failing to show coverage risks both an uninsured-operation violation and suspension of license and registration.

sec02-card-f37.question_text: What certificate must you file after an adjudication for failing to produce insurance proof?
sec02-card-f37.teaching_text: Skipping required SR-22 financial-responsibility proof suspends both your driver license and vehicle registration.

sec02-card-f38.question_text: How does Maine law classify showing fabricated or altered insurance evidence?
sec02-card-f38.teaching_text: Forging or editing an insurance card upgrades a civil traffic stop into a crime.

sec02-card-f39.question_text: What injury or property-damage threshold bars an at-fault uninsured motorist from driving until insured?
sec02-card-f39.teaching_text: Causing bodily injury or $1,000-plus damage without insurance halts driving until financial proof is filed.

sec02-card-f40.question_text: How long do license and registration stay suspended if a court judgment enters after an uninsured crash?
sec02-card-f40.teaching_text: Unpaid civil crash judgments keep both driving and registration privileges locked indefinitely.

sec02-card-f41.question_text: What protective bodily-injury coverage comes built into every automobile liability policy written in Maine?
sec02-card-f41.teaching_text: Maine policies automatically protect you and your passengers if an uninsured driver injures you.

sec02-card-f42.question_text: What minimum limit governs required uninsured-motorist bodily-injury coverage, and can you buy more?
sec02-card-f42.teaching_text: Policies match Maine Financial Responsibility Law minimums by default while letting buyers elect higher caps.

sec02-card-f43.question_text: Where can a Maine driver obtain coverage when standard insurers turn them down?
sec02-card-f43.teaching_text: The state's assigned-risk plan ensures high-risk drivers can still buy mandatory legal liability coverage.

sec02-card-f44.question_text: How many Maine auto-policy carriers are required to join the state's shared assigned-risk pool?
sec02-card-f44.teaching_text: Mandating universal carrier participation spreads high-risk drivers fairly across the entire state insurance market.

sec02-card-r01.question_text: What safety credential does a Maine-registered motor vehicle need before driving on public roads?
sec02-card-r01.teaching_text: Valid plates alone are not enough; Maine vehicles must pass state mechanical safety inspection.

sec02-card-r02.question_text: How often and where must a Maine vehicle pass its required safety inspection?
sec02-card-r02.teaching_text: Licensed state inspection stations check brakes, tires, lights, and exhaust every twelve months.

sec02-card-r03.question_text: What two penalties can result from driving without a current Maine inspection sticker?
sec02-card-r03.teaching_text: Skipping your annual sticker risks both a wallet fine and demerit impact on your license.

sec02-card-r04.question_text: When may a police officer inspect the mechanical safety of a vehicle?
sec02-card-r04.teaching_text: Even a fresh windshield sticker does not shield bald tires or dead brake lights roadside.

sec02-card-r05.question_text: Alongside standard inspection items, which three cabin faults cause an examiner to refuse a road test?
sec02-card-r05.teaching_text: An unlatched glovebox, wobbly seat, or jammed door cancels your road test before leaving the lot.

sec02-card-r06.question_text: What visibility and tampering rule governs a vehicle's identification number?
sec02-card-r06.teaching_text: Covering, removing, or grinding a VIN plate fails inspection and raises stolen-vehicle flags.

sec02-card-r07.question_text: What physical condition must a rearview mirror meet to pass Maine inspection?
sec02-card-r07.teaching_text: Spiderweb cracks, silvering haze, or jagged glass edges disqualify a rearview mirror.

sec02-card-r08.question_text: From what minimum distance must your vehicle's horn be audible?
sec02-card-r08.teaching_text: A weak horn that cannot carry two hundred feet fails inspection and highway warning duty.

sec02-card-r09.question_text: What inspection standard applies to windshield wipers and wiper blades?
sec02-card-r09.teaching_text: Torn rubber blades or dead wiper motors blind you the moment rain or slush hits.

sec02-card-r10.question_text: What must a vehicle defroster do to count as functioning?
sec02-card-r10.teaching_text: Maine winter frost and interior fog clear only when heated fan airflow reaches the windshield.

sec02-card-r11.question_text: Which five exterior lighting groups—and lens standards—must work for Maine inspection?
sec02-card-r11.teaching_text: Every lamp including the license-plate bulb needs working bulbs behind intact proper-color lenses.

sec02-card-r12.question_text: Which two separate braking systems must every motor vehicle have?
sec02-card-r12.teaching_text: Independent service and parking brakes secure parked hills and provide emergency backup.

sec02-card-r13.question_text: Within how many feet must the foot brake stop a vehicle moving at twenty miles per hour?
sec02-card-r13.teaching_text: Taking longer than thirty feet from twenty miles per hour fails Maine's service-brake standard.

sec02-card-r14.question_text: What performance test must your vehicle's parking brake meet?
sec02-card-r14.teaching_text: Stretched cables that let a car creep on grades fail Maine inspection.

sec02-card-r15.question_text: Which four defects are prohibited on a vehicle's windshield and windows?
sec02-card-r15.teaching_text: Damaged, hazy, or sticker-cluttered cabin glass scatters oncoming glare and hides pedestrians entering crosswalks.

sec02-card-r16.question_text: What condition must steering and front-end suspension parts meet?
sec02-card-r16.teaching_text: Worn ball joints or tie-rod ends cause wandering lanes and sudden steering failure.

sec02-card-r17.question_text: What three problems must a vehicle's exhaust system be free of?
sec02-card-r17.teaching_text: Rusted exhaust leaks seep lethal fumes upward into the passenger cabin while roaring past limits.

sec02-card-r18.question_text: What inspection condition applies to all fuel-system components?
sec02-card-r18.teaching_text: Dripping gasoline lines or porous tanks risk catastrophic underbody fires from a single spark.

sec02-card-r19.question_text: How much tread depth and what sidewall condition do noncommercial vehicle tires need?
sec02-card-r19.teaching_text: Tread worn under 2/32 inch hydroplanes fast, and sidewall cuts invite highway blowouts.

sec02-card-r20.question_text: How must every issued registration plate be mounted and maintained?
sec02-card-r20.teaching_text: Missing front plates or snow-and-mud-covered numbers fail both inspection and patrol stops.

sec02-card-r21.question_text: What body and chassis conditions fail Maine's vehicle safety inspection?
sec02-card-r21.teaching_text: Rotted frame rails weaken crash structure while jagged rusted fenders slice bystanders.

sec02-card-r22.question_text: What operational and anti-tampering rule governs your speedometer and odometer?
sec02-card-r22.teaching_text: Broken speedometers blind you to speed limits, and odometer tampering commits fraud.

sec02-card-r23.question_text: What inspection rule applies to a vehicle's fuel inlet?
sec02-card-r23.teaching_text: Keeping the factory filler neck unaltered prevents evaporative vapor leaks and illegal emissions tampering.

sec02-card-r24.question_text: What installation rule applies to the catalytic converter?
sec02-card-r24.teaching_text: Removing or gutting a catalytic converter fails Maine inspection and spikes toxic tailpipe gases.

sec02-card-r25.question_text: By how much can dirty headlight lenses cut your night vision?
sec02-card-r25.teaching_text: Road salt and grime scatter over fifty percent of your headlamp beam before hitting pavement.

sec02-card-r26.question_text: Why replace burned-out turn-signal or brake-light bulbs and blown fuses right away?
sec02-card-r26.teaching_text: Dead brake or turn circuits leave trailing traffic zero advance warning before you stop or turn.

sec02-card-r27.question_text: Why clean vehicle windows on both the outside and the inside?
sec02-card-r27.teaching_text: Interior dashboard film scatters oncoming headlights at night just as badly as exterior bugs.

sec02-card-r28.question_text: When should you measure tire air pressure for an accurate reading?
sec02-card-r28.teaching_text: Highway friction heats internal air and inflates gauge readings above true cold specification.

sec02-card-r29.question_text: What pedal position and three braking symptoms warn of brake trouble?
sec02-card-r29.teaching_text: Low spongy pedals, metal scraping, squeals, or side pulls demand immediate brake service.

sec02-card-r30.question_text: How much dead steering-wheel movement without tire response signals excessive play?
sec02-card-r30.teaching_text: Turning the rim two inches before front tires respond points to dangerous steering linkage slop.

sec02-card-r31.question_text: What wiper checks and winter reservoir fluid keep your windshield clear?
sec02-card-r31.teaching_text: Plain water freezes solid inside lines and across subzero windshields during Maine winters.

sec02-card-r32.question_text: What three muffler or tailpipe warning signs should a mechanic inspect?
sec02-card-r32.teaching_text: Rattling corroded pipes often hide pinhole leaks that vent exhaust under the floorboards.

sec02-card-r33.question_text: Can you smell carbon monoxide, and what five physical symptoms warn of exposure?
sec02-card-r33.teaching_text: Because carbon monoxide has zero smell, drowsiness, ringing ears, headaches, or nausea mean vent immediately.

sec02-card-r34.question_text: What can happen from prolonged breathing of carbon monoxide?
sec02-card-r34.teaching_text: Idling in closed garages or snowbanks with blocked tailpipes turns cabin air lethal.

sec02-card-r35.question_text: For how many consecutive seconds may a gasoline vehicle emit visible non-vapor smoke before becoming illegal?
sec02-card-r35.teaching_text: Trailing blue or black oil-and-fuel smoke past five seconds violates Maine public-road law.

sec02-card-r36.question_text: Why keep dashboard gauges and warning lights working properly?
sec02-card-r36.teaching_text: Spotting rising coolant heat or dropping oil pressure early saves engines from highway seizure.

sec02-card-r37.question_text: After pushing down firmly on a bumper, how many bounces point to worn shock absorbers?
sec02-card-r37.teaching_text: Healthy shocks damp oscillation fast; bouncing past twice means worn dampers need replacement.

sec02-card-r38.question_text: How do worn shock absorbers hurt vehicle control on the road?
sec02-card-r38.teaching_text: Bouncing tires skip across bumps mid-curve, drifting your car toward neighboring lanes.

sec02-card-r39.question_text: Which four fluids plus one belt check belong in regular under-hood maintenance?
sec02-card-r39.teaching_text: Checking engine oil, coolant, transmission and brake fluid, plus belt wear prevents roadside stalls.

sec02-card-r40.question_text: Every how many miles does the Maine manual recommend changing engine oil alongside periodic tune-ups?
sec02-card-r40.teaching_text: Fresh oil every 3,000 to 5,000 miles plus periodic tune-ups keeps engines reliable.

sec02-card-r41.question_text: Which eight emergency and reference items does the Maine manual recommend carrying?
sec02-card-r41.teaching_text: Packing spare-tire gear, first-aid, flashlight, blanket, manual, and paper maps covers dark rural breakdowns.

sec02-card-r42.question_text: What distance and decibel combination makes public-road vehicle audio illegal in Maine?
sec02-card-r42.teaching_text: Blasting stereos audible past twenty-five feet above eighty-five decibels drowns sirens and breaks law.

sec02-card-r43.question_text: Even without a decibel meter, when else is loud vehicle audio prohibited on a public road?
sec02-card-r43.teaching_text: Location and impact on surrounding residents or pedestrians can make booming audio unlawful anywhere.

sec02-card-r44.question_text: How is a first excessive vehicle-audio violation classified, and what assessment does it carry?
sec02-card-r44.teaching_text: Your first loud-stereo ticket counts as a traffic infraction with a fifty-dollar fine.

sec02-card-r45.question_text: What dollar assessment applies to a second excessive vehicle-audio offense?
sec02-card-r45.teaching_text: Repeating a loud-audio violation doubles the assessment from fifty dollars to one hundred.

sec02-card-r46.question_text: What assessment applies to a third or subsequent excessive vehicle-audio offense?
sec02-card-r46.teaching_text: Repeat loud-stereo violations escalate steeply, hitting third-time offenders with a one-hundred-fifty-dollar court assessment.

sec03-card-f01.question_text: What three essential driving tasks depend directly on clear vision?
sec03-card-f01.teaching_text: Blurry distance sight delays reading highway warnings, misjudges closing gaps, and steals hazard reaction seconds.

sec03-card-f02.question_text: How often should an eye professional examine your vision?
sec03-card-f02.teaching_text: Gradual vision changes sneak up unnoticed unless checked every one or two years.

sec03-card-f03.question_text: Why must you skip sunglasses and tinted lenses when driving after dark?
sec03-card-f03.teaching_text: Darkened glass cuts scarce nighttime light and hides unlit pedestrians or deer.

sec03-card-f04.question_text: What does healthy side vision let you spot while your eyes stay aimed straight ahead?
sec03-card-f04.teaching_text: Peripheral vision catches cross-traffic and merging fenders before your head even turns.

sec03-card-f05.question_text: Does sharp straight-ahead eyesight automatically guarantee accurate distance judgment?
sec03-card-f05.teaching_text: Reading crisp letters on a chart does not ensure you accurately gauge oncoming closing distance.

sec03-card-f06.question_text: Does passing a daytime vision check guarantee safe sight in dusk or oncoming headlight glare?
sec03-card-f06.teaching_text: Many drivers with crisp noon acuity struggle badly in dim twilight or bright oncoming beams.

sec03-card-f07.question_text: Which three outside sounds can alert you to unseen danger, including a car hidden in your blind spot?
sec03-card-f07.teaching_text: Your ears often catch a hidden blind-spot car's tire roar before mirrors show anything.

sec03-card-f08.question_text: How can drivers with hearing loss make up for missed audio cues?
sec03-card-f08.teaching_text: Frequent mirror sweeps and full head turns replace faint horns or tire hum.

sec03-card-f09.question_text: What cabin audio and earpiece rules keep outside emergency warnings audible?
sec03-card-f09.teaching_text: Loud speakers or plugged earbuds seal off sirens, train horns, and screeching tires.

sec03-card-f10.question_text: How does the Maine manual define fatigue and its three main triggers?
sec03-card-f10.teaching_text: Mental or physical exhaustion builds from long strain, sickness, or skimping on rest.

sec03-card-f11.question_text: Which mental, reaction, and mood changes happen when you drive fatigued?
sec03-card-f11.teaching_text: Tired brains process brake lights sluggishly while losing patience with surrounding traffic.

sec03-card-f12.question_text: Why must you stay out from behind the wheel when excessively tired?
sec03-card-f12.teaching_text: Willpower cannot stop an exhausted brain from nodding off into oncoming lanes.

sec03-card-f13.question_text: Why shouldn't a drowsy driver count on caffeine, loud music, or rolled-down windows?
sec03-card-f13.teaching_text: Cold air and caffeine mask tiredness briefly while your brain still slips toward sleep.

sec03-card-f14.question_text: How long do unnoticed highway microsleeps typically last?
sec03-card-f14.teaching_text: Drifting unconscious for five seconds at highway speed sends your car blind down a football field.

sec03-card-f15.question_text: What is the single cure that actually repays a buildup of lost sleep?
sec03-card-f15.teaching_text: No energy drink or willpower shortcut substitutes for genuine hours of sleep.

sec03-card-f16.question_text: How should you schedule pre-trip rest and driving hours for a long journey?
sec03-card-f16.teaching_text: Starting well-rested during normal daytime hours works with your natural circadian alertness.

sec03-card-f17.question_text: What should you do when drowsiness hits instead of trying to push through to home?
sec03-card-f17.teaching_text: Most fatigue crashes happen near home when drivers stubbornly try finishing the last miles.

sec03-card-f18.question_text: Between which overnight hours does the manual advise taking a safe sleep break?
sec03-card-f18.teaching_text: Human alertness plunges deepest between midnight and six a.m. regardless of grit.

sec03-card-f19.question_text: In what two ways can a qualified passenger help fight highway fatigue?
sec03-card-f19.teaching_text: Light conversation engages the mind while swapping licensed drivers lets tired eyes rest.

sec03-card-f20.question_text: Who should stay awake up front, and where should an off-duty driver buckle up to nap?
sec03-card-f20.teaching_text: A sleeping front-seat passenger spreads yawns, so nappers belong belted in back.

sec03-card-f21.question_text: Every how many hours or miles should you plan a road-trip break?
sec03-card-f21.teaching_text: Stepping out every 100 miles or two hours—or sooner if drowsy—resets highway focus.

sec03-card-f22.question_text: How many minutes does the Maine manual describe for a roadside fatigue refresher nap?
sec03-card-f22.teaching_text: Parking somewhere secure for a brief quarter-hour rest restores short-term alertness without deep grogginess.

sec03-card-f23.question_text: What pre-drive check applies to medications alongside avoiding alcohol and impairing drugs?
sec03-card-f23.teaching_text: Everyday allergy or cold pills can sedate reflexes just as heavily as alcohol.

sec03-card-f24.question_text: Name the six physical and mental warning signs that fatigue is taking over?
sec03-card-f24.teaching_text: Nodding heads, missing road memories, lane drift, and wandering thoughts mean sleep is seconds away.

sec03-card-f25.question_text: How many drowsiness warning signs must appear before you pull off for a safe nap?
sec03-card-f25.teaching_text: Waiting for a second or third warning often means waking up off the shoulder.

sec03-card-f26.question_text: What does a driving distraction pull away from operating the vehicle?
sec03-card-f26.teaching_text: Anything pulling thoughts, eyes, or hands off driving creates a dangerous attention gap.

sec03-card-f27.question_text: Which four cabin distractions should you settle before shifting out of Park?
sec03-card-f27.teaching_text: Handling navigation, snacks, grooming, and loose cargo parked keeps both hands free rolling.

sec03-card-f28.question_text: Which four everyday habits should you avoid while your vehicle is moving?
sec03-card-f28.teaching_text: Heated cabin arguments, burgers, calls, and texts combine cognitive, manual, and visual distraction.

sec03-card-f29.question_text: How must children and pets ride so they stay safe and non-distracting?
sec03-card-f29.teaching_text: Unkempt pets climbing onto laps or unbuckled kids turn minor stops into crashes.

sec03-card-r53.question_text: What range of nightly sleep hours does the Maine manual note across different people?
sec03-card-r53.teaching_text: Knowing whether your body needs closer to ten hours than six prevents hidden fatigue.

sec03-card-f30.question_text: What defines a visual driving distraction?
sec03-card-f30.teaching_text: Looking at screens, billboards, or floor mats leaves your car rolling blind.

sec03-card-f31.question_text: What defines a manual driving distraction?
sec03-card-f31.teaching_text: Reaching for drinks or bags leaves one—or zero—hands ready for sudden swerves.

sec03-card-f32.question_text: What defines a cognitive driving distraction?
sec03-card-f32.teaching_text: Daydreaming or emotional stress causes inattention blindness even while staring straight ahead.

sec03-card-f33.question_text: What duration limit and purpose keep mirror or gauge checks safe while moving?
sec03-card-f33.teaching_text: Keeping every mirror or speedometer check under a single second preserves continuous forward hazard tracking.

sec03-card-f34.question_text: What must you do with the vehicle before dialing a phone number yourself?
sec03-card-f34.teaching_text: Punching phone digits while rolling steals both visual focus and steering hands from highway control.

sec03-card-f35.question_text: How can a passenger help when a phone call needs to be placed during a trip?
sec03-card-f35.teaching_text: Handing phone duty to a rider keeps your eyes and hands dedicated to traffic.

sec03-card-f36.question_text: Which three pieces of information should you give first when calling in a roadside emergency?
sec03-card-f36.teaching_text: Dispatchers send ambulances or cruisers fastest when told who is needed, where, and apparent injuries.

sec03-card-f37.question_text: Why mount a portable phone in a secure cradle rather than tossing it on a seat?
sec03-card-f37.teaching_text: Sudden stops launch unsecured phones across the cabin at dangerous impact speed.

sec03-card-f38.question_text: How does Maine law treat a driver under eighteen using a mobile phone or handheld device?
sec03-card-f38.teaching_text: Any handheld electronic use behind the wheel under eighteen draws a traffic-infraction ticket.

sec03-card-f39.question_text: Which five unsafe behaviors does the Maine manual group under aggressive driving?
sec03-card-f39.teaching_text: Combining excess speed, bumper-riding, unblinkered cuts, and blown signs multiplies crash severity.

sec03-card-f40.question_text: How should you respond when another driver makes a mistake or acts rudely?
sec03-card-f40.teaching_text: Patience and courtesy defuse mistakes before ego escalates them into road rage.

sec03-card-r54.question_text: What type of equipment does the manual recommend if an adult uses an in-vehicle phone?
sec03-card-r54.teaching_text: Speakerphone or hands-free setups keep both hands anchored on the steering wheel.

sec03-card-f41.question_text: How much alcohol may a driver younger than twenty-one consume before driving in Maine?
sec03-card-f41.teaching_text: Maine enforces strict underage zero tolerance, meaning any measurable alcohol violates state driving law.

sec03-card-f42.question_text: At least how long does a driver younger than twenty-one lose their license upon an OUI conviction?
sec03-card-f42.teaching_text: An underage OUI conviction strips driving privileges for a minimum of twelve months.

sec03-card-f43.question_text: Beyond license loss, what financial, program, and custody penalties accompany an underage OUI conviction?
sec03-card-f43.teaching_text: Court fines, reinstatement fees, mandatory substance-abuse evaluation/treatment, and possible jail stack fast.

sec03-card-f44.question_text: Which four core driving abilities do alcohol and impairing drugs disrupt?
sec03-card-f44.teaching_text: Impaired brains misread red-green signals, blur distance, misjudge risk, and brake late.

sec03-card-f45.question_text: What responsibility do you have when someone around you has been drinking and reaches for keys?
sec03-card-f45.teaching_text: Stepping in to arrange a sober ride saves your friend and innocent strangers.

sec03-card-f46.question_text: What three mental skills make up good driving judgment?
sec03-card-f46.teaching_text: Accurate reading of time, space, and closing distance depends on sharp sober thinking.

sec03-card-f47.question_text: How does alcohol affect judgment as someone continues drinking?
sec03-card-f47.teaching_text: Because self-assessment erodes first, impaired drinkers become the worst judges of their own fitness.

sec03-card-f48.question_text: Which three visual functions suffer after drinking alcohol?
sec03-card-f48.teaching_text: Oncoming headlights blind impaired eyes longer while peripheral vision and depth perception shrink.

sec03-card-f49.question_text: What drug class does alcohol belong to, and how does it shift emotions and risk-taking?
sec03-card-f49.teaching_text: Central-nervous-system depression lowers normal inhibitions and invites reckless gambles behind the steering wheel.

sec03-card-f50.question_text: How does drinking raise the odds of falling asleep at the wheel or running off the road?
sec03-card-f50.teaching_text: Sedated concentration and clumsy physical coordination make single-vehicle roadway departures far more likely.

sec03-card-f51.question_text: Which five on-road mistakes is a drinking driver much more likely to commit?
sec03-card-f51.teaching_text: Spotting lane wandering, blown signals, bad passes, or erratic speed warns you to keep clear.

sec03-card-f52.question_text: What mental illusion can alcohol create even while actual driving skills deteriorate?
sec03-card-f52.teaching_text: Feeling sharper while sight, coordination, and reflexes drop is alcohol's classic trap.

sec03-card-f53.question_text: Which four drink sizes carry roughly the same amount of pure alcohol in the Maine manual?
sec03-card-f53.teaching_text: Twelve ounces beer, four wine, ten wine cooler, and one ounce 100-proof liquor hit equally.

sec03-card-f54.question_text: What actually causes intoxication—switching drink types or total alcohol consumed?
sec03-card-f54.teaching_text: Sticking to beer all night impairs you identically if total alcohol intake climbs.

sec03-card-f55.question_text: Can black coffee, cold showers, or workouts sober up a drinker?
sec03-card-f55.teaching_text: Coffee makes only a wide-awake drunk; liver metabolism runs strictly on clock time.

sec03-card-f56.question_text: What blood or breath alcohol measurement marks Maine's criminal OUI threshold?
