sec03-card-f56.teaching_text: Measuring 0.08 grams per 100 milliliters blood or 210 liters breath triggers criminal OUI.

sec03-card-f57.question_text: After an OUI arrest, can the Secretary of State suspend your license before your court date?
sec03-card-f57.teaching_text: Police reports and chemical results trigger administrative suspension long before criminal trial.

sec03-card-f58.question_text: In what units and by what method is breath alcohol concentration measured?
sec03-card-f58.teaching_text: Chemical analysis measures alcohol weight inside two hundred ten liters of exhaled breath.

sec03-card-f59.question_text: Which three personal and timing factors determine your breath alcohol concentration?
sec03-card-f59.teaching_text: Smaller body weight and shorter elimination time push concentration higher from the same drinks.

sec03-card-f60.question_text: Which two bodily samples does Maine chemical alcohol testing use?
sec03-card-f60.teaching_text: Maine implied-consent testing measures alcohol concentration through either breath or drawn blood.

sec03-card-f61.question_text: Which test do officers normally give first, and when is a blood draw required instead?
sec03-card-f61.teaching_text: Breath testing comes standard unless crash injuries or circumstances make breath testing unreasonable.

sec03-card-f62.question_text: When a blood alcohol draw is required, when may the driver choose the physician?
sec03-card-f62.teaching_text: Maine lets you request your own physician provided that doctor is reasonably available promptly.

sec03-card-f63.question_text: Up to how long can refusing an implied-consent alcohol test suspend your license administratively?
sec03-card-f63.teaching_text: Test refusal triggers instant administrative license loss—without waiting for court—up to six years.

sec03-card-f64.question_text: Can a driver be convicted of OUI in court without a chemical alcohol-test result?
sec03-card-f64.teaching_text: Observed weaving, slurred speech, and failed sobriety checks support OUI guilt even without numbers.

sec03-card-r01.question_text: When must a driver submit to a chemical test for drugs other than alcohol?
sec03-card-r01.teaching_text: Implied consent covers impairing drugs too whenever probable cause points to drugged driving.

sec03-card-r02.question_text: What happens to an administrative OUI suspension if a court later finds the driver not guilty?
sec03-card-r02.teaching_text: Bureau administrative suspensions operate on an independent track separate from criminal courtroom verdicts.

sec03-card-r03.question_text: How does a test refusal affect penalties if police testimony still convicts you of OUI?
sec03-card-r03.teaching_text: Refusing fails to block conviction and tacks an extra OUI suspension onto your refusal ban.

sec03-card-r04.question_text: What minimum fine applies to a first 0.08–0.14 OUI conviction, and how does refusal raise it?
sec03-card-r04.teaching_text: Refusing chemical testing hikes the mandatory minimum first-offense fine from $500 to $600.

sec03-card-r05.question_text: How long is license loss—plus added requirements—for a standard 0.08–0.14 first OUI conviction?
sec03-card-r05.teaching_text: Even an unaggravated first OUI costs at least 150 license-free days plus treatment and fees.

sec03-card-r06.question_text: Which five factors turn a first OUI conviction into an aggravated OUI?
sec03-card-r06.teaching_text: High 0.15 tests, 30-over speeding, fleeing police, refusing tests, or under-21 passengers mandate jail.

sec03-card-r07.question_text: How many mandatory jail hours apply to an aggravated first OUI versus one involving test refusal?
sec03-card-r07.teaching_text: Aggravators put first-timers behind bars two full days—or four full days for refusing testing.

sec03-card-r08.question_text: Alongside jail, what license loss, fee, and program apply to an aggravated first OUI?
sec03-card-r08.teaching_text: Serving jail time does not replace the 150-day license suspension, fee, and treatment mandate.

sec03-card-r09.question_text: What extra financial filing must a second or subsequent OUI offender show before reinstatement?
sec03-card-r09.teaching_text: Repeat OUI offenders cannot regain driving rights without verified liability insurance on file.

sec03-card-r10.question_text: Can you get a work or limited hardship license during your minimum OUI-conviction suspension?
sec03-card-r10.teaching_text: Maine bars any limited or work-restricted driving throughout the mandatory minimum OUI suspension.

sec03-card-r11.question_text: What strict alcohol rule comes attached to any license reinstated after an OUI conviction?
sec03-card-r11.teaching_text: Reinstated OUI drivers lose the 0.08 adult margin and must drive completely alcohol-free.

sec03-card-r12.question_text: How long does conditional zero-alcohol status last after a first OUI versus a second or later OUI?
sec03-card-r12.teaching_text: A second OUI extends zero-alcohol conditional licensing tenfold to an entire decade.

sec03-card-r13.question_text: What happens if a conditional licensee drives with any measurable alcohol?
sec03-card-r13.teaching_text: Any trace of alcohol behind the wheel triggers an immediate one-year suspension pre-hearing.

sec03-card-r14.question_text: Which suspension tier hits a conditional licensee caught driving at 0.08 grams or higher?
sec03-card-r14.teaching_text: Hitting 0.08 on a conditional license escalates your administrative suspension straight to repeat-offender length.

sec03-card-r15.question_text: What suspension hits a conditional licensee who refuses an alcohol test?
sec03-card-r15.teaching_text: Refusing on a conditional card tacks two full years onto any earlier OUI suspension.

sec03-card-r16.question_text: Does holding a valid doctor's prescription excuse impaired driving in Maine?
sec03-card-r16.teaching_text: Driving impaired by legal pharmacy or over-the-counter medication still violates Maine OUI law.

sec03-card-r17.question_text: How do over-the-counter cold/allergy meds versus stimulant/diet pills impair drivers?
sec03-card-r17.teaching_text: Antihistamines make eyes droop while diet or stimulant pills trigger dizziness and scattered focus.

sec03-card-r18.question_text: Whom should you consult—alongside reading package labels—when unsure how a medicine affects driving?
sec03-card-r18.teaching_text: Doctors and pharmacists spot sedating interactions before you get behind the wheel.

sec03-card-r19.question_text: What mental hazards can amphetamine stimulants trigger while active and as they wear off?
sec03-card-r19.teaching_text: Stimulants distort perception and concentration, then drop drivers into sudden exhaustion and depression.

sec03-card-r20.question_text: What happens when someone mixes tranquilizers with alcohol?
sec03-card-r20.teaching_text: Stacking two central-nervous-system depressants compounds heavy sedation and wrecks physical balance behind the wheel.

sec03-card-r21.question_text: Which five impairments can excessive barbiturate use cause?
sec03-card-r21.teaching_text: Shaking hands, mental fog, clumsy coordination, and sedation ruin steering and braking control.

sec03-card-r22.question_text: How does marijuana affect alertness and perception of time and space?
sec03-card-r22.teaching_text: Misjudging closing time and following space makes intersections and lane merges hazardous.

sec03-card-r23.question_text: What scanning mistake do some marijuana-impaired drivers make?
sec03-card-r23.teaching_text: Locking eyes onto a single bumper or sign leaves cross-traffic and pedestrians unseen.

sec03-card-r24.question_text: Which four essential driving faculties can illegal drugs impair?
sec03-card-r24.teaching_text: Illicit substances attack every sensory and decision channel needed for safe vehicle control.

sec03-card-r25.question_text: Why is mixing alcohol with another drug worse than taking either substance by itself?
sec03-card-r25.teaching_text: Drug-alcohol synergy multiplies sedation and triggers unpredictable reactions that neither substance produces by itself.

sec03-card-r26.question_text: What flat rule governs combining alcohol with other drugs or driving after using either?
sec03-card-r26.teaching_text: Keeping alcohol and impairing medications completely separate from driving prevents synergistic crashes.

sec03-card-r27.question_text: How do Maine punishments for drug-impaired driving compare with alcohol OUI—whether legal or illegal?
sec03-card-r27.teaching_text: Court fines, license loss, and jail match alcohol OUI even when the drug was prescribed.

sec03-card-r28.question_text: What can happen to the car itself upon an OUI arrest or driving under OUI suspension?
sec03-card-r28.teaching_text: Impoundment, towing bills, storage fees, fines, and jail stack onto license consequences.

sec03-card-r29.question_text: When must any crash-involved driver submit to chemical testing, and what does refusal cost?
sec03-card-r29.teaching_text: Any crash causing or likely to cause death mandates chemical testing or a one-year suspension.

sec03-card-r30.question_text: What immediate BMV suspension applies when impaired negligent driving causes a death?
sec03-card-r30.teaching_text: At least one year of immediate suspension stacks on top of any test-refusal penalty.

sec03-card-r31.question_text: What prison and revocation penalties hit vehicular homicide, and how does intoxication change revocation?
sec03-card-r31.teaching_text: Five-year minimum revocation turns permanent for life when intoxication caused the fatal crash.

sec03-card-r32.question_text: When does a driver violate Maine's public-road open-container law?
sec03-card-r32.teaching_text: Even if only a passenger sips or holds an unsealed bottle in the cabin, the operator violates law.

sec03-card-r33.question_text: Where may an unsealed alcohol container ride legally in a hatchback, SUV, or pickup without a trunk?
sec03-card-r33.teaching_text: Stowing resealed bottles behind the rearmost upright seat keeps them out of passenger reach.

sec03-card-r34.question_text: Which hired passenger vehicles qualify—and which one is excluded—under the fare-paying open-container exception?
sec03-card-r34.teaching_text: Chartered buses and limousines qualify for fare-paying riders, whereas taxicabs remain strictly off-limits.

sec03-card-r35.question_text: Where inside recreational vehicles does Maine's open-container exception allow passenger possession or drinking?
sec03-card-r35.teaching_text: Passengers inside dedicated living quarters of motor homes, trailers, or truck campers are excepted.

sec03-card-r36.question_text: When is transporting open alcohol to or from a catered event legal?
sec03-card-r36.teaching_text: Operators or employers holding an active off-premise catering license may transport event stock.

sec03-card-r37.question_text: Beyond BMV license penalties, what lasting legal record does an OUI conviction create?
sec03-card-r37.teaching_text: Maine OUI is a crime—not a simple traffic ticket—following you on background checks.

sec03-card-r55.question_text: What vehicle-device program does Maine offer for qualifying OUI offenders?
sec03-card-r55.teaching_text: Breath-tested ignition interlocks block engine starts whenever alcohol registers on a qualifying offender's breath.

sec03-card-r38.question_text: Is alcohol a stimulant or a depressant when the first sip makes someone feel talkative?
sec03-card-r38.teaching_text: That lively initial buzz comes from depressing brain centers that normally restrain behavior.

sec03-card-r39.question_text: Below what age is buying alcohol illegal in Maine?
sec03-card-r39.teaching_text: State liquor statutes strictly prohibit anyone from purchasing alcohol before reaching age twenty-one.

sec03-card-r40.question_text: Under which two narrow exceptions may someone younger than twenty-one transport alcohol in a vehicle?
sec03-card-r40.teaching_text: Outside work deliveries or an explicit parent/guardian errand, underage vehicle alcohol brings mandatory suspension.

sec03-card-r41.question_text: Is transporting illegal drugs in a motor vehicle ever lawful?
sec03-card-r41.teaching_text: Carrying illicit drugs inside any motor vehicle triggers serious criminal charges and license consequences.

sec03-card-r42.question_text: What minimum license loss hits an under-21 driver for any blood alcohol or refusing chemical testing?
sec03-card-r42.teaching_text: Either blowing positive or refusing breath/blood testing under twenty-one costs at least one year.

sec03-card-r43.question_text: How do Maine OUI rules classify every license held by someone younger than twenty-one?
sec03-card-r43.teaching_text: For alcohol enforcement, under-21 licenses remain provisional and immediately suspendable right up to twenty-one.

sec03-card-r44.question_text: What safe alternatives should you use instead of riding with a driver who has been drinking?
sec03-card-r44.teaching_text: Calling a sober relative, friend, bus, or cab beats gambling your life as a passenger.

sec03-card-r45.question_text: How can strong worry, excitement, fear, anger, or sadness affect your driving?
sec03-card-r45.teaching_text: Flooded emotions hijack working memory and delay spotting brake lights or stop signs.

sec03-card-r46.question_text: What three options do you have when strong emotions threaten your focus behind the wheel?
sec03-card-r46.teaching_text: Waiting until calm, leaving extra travel margin, or letting someone else drive prevents emotional mistakes.

sec03-card-r47.question_text: What should you do when a temporary illness or minor physical ailment affects you?
sec03-card-r47.teaching_text: Fever, flu aches, or stiff necks sap stamina and head-check mobility more than drivers expect.

sec03-card-r48.question_text: Who judges fitness for short-term illness versus long-term medical conditions?
sec03-card-r48.teaching_text: You bench yourself for a cold, whereas the Bureau helps evaluate ongoing medical conditions.

sec03-card-r49.question_text: How can a Maine license examiner assist a driver living with a long-term condition?
sec03-card-r49.teaching_text: Examiners help match adaptive equipment or conditions so qualified drivers stay mobile safely.

sec03-card-r50.question_text: When can a medical condition affecting alertness still qualify for a Maine driver license?
sec03-card-r50.teaching_text: Documented medical stability and treatment let drivers with managed conditions retain licensing.

sec03-card-r51.question_text: What may certain physical disabilities require for safe driving and add to the license?
sec03-card-r51.teaching_text: Hand controls, spinner knobs, or specialized training pair with matching license restriction codes.

sec03-card-r52.question_text: What may be required if your medical condition changes or you start using new adaptive equipment?
sec03-card-r52.teaching_text: An on-road evaluation verifies you master new hand or pedal adaptations cleanly in traffic.

sec04-card-f01.question_text: How should your back and feet be positioned once seated behind the wheel?
sec04-card-f01.teaching_text: Anchored shoulders and planted feet give stable leverage for emergency braking and brisk steering.
sec04-card-f01.must_match_memory_hook: Sit upright, back flat, feet planted

visual_sync.text_span: Sit upright, back flat, feet planted

sec04-card-f02.question_text: Which four comfort and safety goals guide adjusting your seat and mirrors?
sec04-card-f02.teaching_text: Balancing sightlines, easy pedal reach, relaxed arms, and airbag clearance prevents fatigue and injury.

sec04-card-f03.question_text: How should a shorter driver gain road visibility without crowding the steering wheel?
sec04-card-f03.teaching_text: Lifting height with seat controls or a firm cushion beats sliding dangerously close to the wheel.

sec04-card-f04.question_text: Where should your right heel stay while switching between accelerator and brake?
sec04-card-f04.teaching_text: Keeping your heel anchored on the floor speeds smooth transitions between gas and brake.

sec04-card-f05.question_text: How high should the top of the steering wheel sit relative to your shoulders and chin?
sec04-card-f05.teaching_text: Keeping the upper rim below your chin clears your sightline and directs airbags toward your chest.

sec04-card-f06.question_text: How many inches belong between your breastbone and the steering wheel, and how should the seatback sit?
sec04-card-f06.teaching_text: Airbags inflate explosively in milliseconds, needing ten inches of room while upright backs stop submarine sliding.

sec04-card-f07.question_text: Where against the back of your head should the head restraint make contact?
sec04-card-f07.teaching_text: Setting the restraint too low lets your neck snap backward over the top in a rear-end hit.
sec04-card-f07.must_match_memory_hook: Touch back of head, above ears

visual_sync.text_span: Touch back of head, above ears

sec04-card-f08.question_text: What should your interior rearview mirror cleanly frame?
sec04-card-f08.teaching_text: Centering the full rear glass maximizes straight-back highway sightlines without tilting your head.

sec04-card-f09.question_text: Why adjust your inside mirror's day-night setting to match outside lighting?
sec04-card-f09.teaching_text: Switching to night mode dims high-mounted SUV beams behind you without losing traffic awareness.

sec04-card-f10.question_text: When must you finish adjusting your interior and exterior mirrors?
sec04-card-f10.teaching_text: Tweaking side mirrors mid-lane pulls both hands and eyes away from moving traffic.

sec04-card-f11.question_text: How do you position your head and aim the left outside mirror to shrink blind spots?
sec04-card-f11.teaching_text: Swinging the mirror outward until your rear fender barely shows when leaning left eliminates overlap.

sec04-card-f12.question_text: Where do you lean your head when aiming the right exterior mirror?
sec04-card-f12.teaching_text: Adjusting from center cabin until the right flank barely appears sweeps out the right blind zone.

sec04-card-f13.question_text: What overall field of view should properly aimed exterior mirrors deliver?
sec04-card-f13.teaching_text: Aiming mirrors outward into neighboring lanes beats staring at your own painted doors.

sec04-card-f14.question_text: Whose seatbelts and child seats must the driver confirm before pulling away?
sec04-card-f14.teaching_text: Unbuckled passengers become lethal cabin projectiles that crush belted riders during rollovers.

sec04-card-f15.question_text: Beyond cutting injury and death inside the car, what fatal crash outcome do seatbelts prevent?
sec04-card-f15.teaching_text: Being thrown through cabin glass onto hard pavement multiplies crash fatality odds dramatically.

sec04-card-f16.question_text: How does wearing a safety belt help you avoid a secondary crash during violent swerves?
sec04-card-f16.teaching_text: Sliding across the seat during hard braking or an initial hit leaves nobody steering.

sec04-card-f17.question_text: What happens to an unbelted rider the instant a crashing vehicle stops?
sec04-card-f17.teaching_text: Momentum hurls unbelted bodies at pre-crash speed straight into glass, pillars, or dashboards.

sec04-card-f18.question_text: Even without a crash, how do safety belts help you on bumpy or winding roads?
sec04-card-f18.teaching_text: Snug belts support upright posture over bumps and curves so muscles tire slower.

sec04-card-f19.question_text: Why must you fasten your safety belt before starting the engine?
sec04-card-f19.teaching_text: Parking-lot and intersection hits strike in split seconds with no chance to grab webbing.

sec04-card-f20.question_text: Where must the shoulder belt cross your torso, and which two shortcuts are dangerous?
sec04-card-f20.teaching_text: Tucking straps under an arm crushes ribs on impact, while routing behind forfeits upper-body restraint.

sec04-card-f21.question_text: Where across your lower body should a snug lap belt sit?
sec04-card-f21.teaching_text: Straps riding high across your soft stomach cause severe internal organ trauma in a crash.

sec04-card-f22.question_text: Do airbags replace safety belts or work alongside them?
sec04-card-f22.teaching_text: Airbags are designed strictly around belted riders; unbelted occupants hit deploying bags too close.

sec04-card-f23.question_text: Which parts of the body do belts and frontal airbags team up to keep off the wheel and dash?
sec04-card-f23.teaching_text: Cushioning your head and chest together prevents lethal steering-hub and windshield impact trauma.

sec04-card-f24.question_text: Where should you look for rules and warnings tailored to your specific car's airbags?
sec04-card-f24.teaching_text: Side-curtain zones, weight sensors, and switch locations vary across vehicle makes and years.

sec04-card-r01.question_text: Which seating row is safest for a child of any age?
sec04-card-r01.teaching_text: Back seats sit farthest from frontal crumple zones and explosive dashboard airbags.

sec04-card-r02.question_text: Where must a rear-facing child safety seat never be installed?
sec04-card-r02.teaching_text: An inflating front airbag slams the back of a rear-facing shell right above an infant's head.

sec04-card-r03.question_text: Which two guides govern installing a child seat, and what two fastening steps matter?
sec04-card-r03.teaching_text: Even a top-rated car seat fails if anchored loosely to the car or strapped loosely on the child.

sec04-card-r04.question_text: How and where does the Maine manual advise children younger than two to ride?
sec04-card-r04.teaching_text: Rear-facing shells cradle fragile infant necks and spines across the whole shell back.

sec04-card-r05.question_text: What harm can an inflating airbag inflict on an unrestrained occupant?
sec04-card-r05.teaching_text: Sliding forward during braking puts an unbelted head directly into the airbag's blast zone.

sec04-card-r06.question_text: May an infant ride in the front seat of a vehicle equipped with a passenger-side airbag?
sec04-card-r06.teaching_text: Passenger airbags deploy at speeds built for belted adults, making front seats lethal for infants.

sec04-card-r07.question_text: How should front-row occupants—especially short, pregnant, or older riders—position their seats?
sec04-card-r07.teaching_text: Maximizing gap from the wheel or dash softens airbag contact while maintaining pedal control.

sec04-card-r08.question_text: Which federal safety benchmark defines a lawful child safety seat in Maine?
sec04-card-r08.teaching_text: Look for the FMVSS certification label before trusting any infant or convertible carrier.

sec04-card-r09.question_text: How does Maine define a federally approved child-restraint booster system?
sec04-card-r09.teaching_text: Boosters raise smaller kids so adult lap-and-shoulder straps cross hips and collarbones properly.

sec04-card-r10.question_text: Below what weight must a child ride secured inside a child safety seat?
sec04-card-r10.teaching_text: Maine law requires a harnessed child safety seat for every passenger under fifty-five pounds.

sec04-card-r11.question_text: Which age and weight bracket requires a federally approved child-restraint booster system?
sec04-card-r11.teaching_text: Kids under eight weighing 55 up to under 80 pounds need booster elevation before adult belts fit.

sec04-card-r12.question_text: When does a passenger under eighteen graduate to a standard seat belt?
sec04-card-r12.teaching_text: Once past age eight or fifty-seven inches tall—and clear of lower seat rules—youth wear belts.

sec04-card-r13.question_text: What seatbelt rule applies to passengers aged eighteen or older in belt-equipped vehicles?
sec04-card-r13.teaching_text: Maine enforces primary seatbelt use for every adult passenger front and rear.

sec04-card-r14.question_text: Must the vehicle operator wear a safety belt unless a specific statutory exemption applies?
sec04-card-r14.teaching_text: Operators of belt-required vehicles must stay buckled behind the wheel outside narrow delivery exceptions.

sec04-card-r15.question_text: When is a United States Postal Service rural carrier exempt from Maine's seatbelt rule?
sec04-card-r15.teaching_text: Frequent mailbox stops exempt rural USPS carriers during active delivery routes only.

sec04-card-r16.question_text: Is a taxi or limousine driver legally responsible if a fare-paying passenger leaves their belt unfastened?
sec04-card-r16.teaching_text: Adult fare-paying cab or limo riders bear their own seatbelt responsibility rather than the chauffeur.

sec04-card-r17.question_text: When is a newspaper delivery driver exempt from wearing a safety belt?
sec04-card-r17.teaching_text: Constant stop-and-exit paper drops qualify for belt exemption only during active route delivery.

sec06-card-f01.question_text: How should you treat right-of-way even when the law gives you priority?
sec06-card-f01.teaching_text: Insisting on your turn against a distracted driver wins an argument on paper while causing a real crash.

sec06-card-f02.question_text: Who stops and who goes first when drivers arrive one after another at a four-way stop?
sec06-card-f02.teaching_text: Rolling a four-way stop confuses waiting drivers and wrecks the predictable turn order.

sec06-card-f03.question_text: When two adjacent drivers reach a four-way stop at the exact same moment, who yields?
sec06-card-f03.teaching_text: Giving priority to the vehicle on your right breaks ties cleanly without hesitant wave-throughs.

sec06-card-f04.question_text: Who has priority when you pull onto a public street from a private road or driveway?
sec06-card-f04.teaching_text: Main-road drivers and sidewalk pedestrians expect uninterrupted flow when passing private driveways and entrances.

sec06-card-f05.question_text: Between a car on an interstate entrance ramp and traffic already on the highway, who yields?
sec06-card-f05.teaching_text: Through highway traffic carries high momentum and has no obligation to brake for an entering car.

sec06-card-f06.question_text: What must you wait for before pulling out of a parked position into a travel lane?
sec06-card-f06.teaching_text: Pulling from a curb starts from zero speed, so oncoming lane traffic needs a wide gap to stay safe.

sec06-card-f07.question_text: What must you never do when a vehicle ahead stops at a crosswalk for pedestrians?
sec06-card-f07.teaching_text: The stopped car blocks your view of the pedestrian stepping directly into the adjacent lane.

sec06-card-f08.question_text: At an intersection with no signs or signals, who goes if vehicles arrive at roughly the same time?
sec06-card-f08.teaching_text: Unmarked neighborhood crossings rely on the same right-hand rule used at simultaneous four-way stops.

sec06-card-f09.question_text: How must you respond to vehicles that have already entered an intersection ahead of you?
sec06-card-f09.teaching_text: Charging into an occupied intersection traps turning or clearing cars with nowhere to escape.

sec06-card-f10.question_text: Who yields when a vehicle approaches to enter a rotary or traffic circle?
sec06-card-f10.teaching_text: Keeping circulating traffic flowing stops the entire ring from locking into gridlock.

sec06-card-f11.question_text: What exact steps must you take when an emergency vehicle approaches from any direction with siren and flashing lights?
sec06-card-f11.teaching_text: Stopping inside an intersection blocks rescue trucks that need room to swing wide around corners.

sec06-card-f12.question_text: How does Maine law classify failing to yield properly to an emergency vehicle using siren and flashing lights?
sec06-card-f12.teaching_text: Maine treats blocking an active ambulance, cruiser, or fire engine as a criminal offense, not a minor ticket.

sec06-card-f13.question_text: How must a left-turning driver handle an oncoming bicyclist or roller skier?
sec06-card-f13.teaching_text: Misjudging how fast a bike or roller skier closes distance causes classic left-cross collisions.

sec06-card-f14.question_text: What must you do for pedestrians in a marked crosswalk where no signal or officer directs traffic?
sec06-card-f14.teaching_text: Painted crosswalk lines give walkers legal priority even where no stoplight hangs overhead.

sec06-card-f15.question_text: Who has priority when you are turning at a signalized intersection and pedestrians are crossing with the light?
sec06-card-f15.teaching_text: Sharing a green phase never lets a turning bumper cut off someone walking legally in the crosswalk.

sec06-card-f16.question_text: What must you do before driving across a sidewalk out of an alley or driveway?
sec06-card-f16.teaching_text: Buildings and hedges along alleys hide joggers and strollers until your nose reaches the sidewalk edge.

sec06-card-f17.question_text: What is your duty whenever schoolchildren are crossing the street?
sec06-card-f17.teaching_text: Younger kids judge vehicle speed poorly and may dart unexpectedly while walking in groups.

sec06-card-f18.question_text: Besides signs, lights, and pavement lines, whose spoken or hand directions count as official traffic controls?
sec06-card-f18.teaching_text: Human flaggers, officers, and crossing guards adapt live intersection flow during crashes, work zones, and school dismissal.

sec06-card-f19.question_text: Is cutting through a corner parking lot legal to skip waiting at a red light or stop sign?
sec06-card-f19.teaching_text: Drivers backing out of store spaces never expect commuter traffic speeding diagonally across parking aisles.

sec06-card-f20.question_text: How are red, yellow, and green lenses arranged on vertical and horizontal traffic signals?
sec06-card-f20.teaching_text: Standardized positions let color-vision-deficient drivers read any traffic signal instantly by location.

sec06-card-f21.question_text: When does a steady green traffic light actually allow you to move through an intersection?
sec06-card-f21.teaching_text: Green grants permission, not armor, so always verify late cross-traffic and walkers have cleared.

sec06-card-f22.question_text: What does a steady yellow traffic signal warn you of, and what action does it call for?
sec06-card-f22.teaching_text: Treating yellow as a speed-up challenge puts you into the intersection right as cross traffic gets green.

sec06-card-f23.question_text: Where must you stop and wait when facing a steady red traffic light?
sec06-card-f23.teaching_text: Creeping past the painted line blocks crosswalk ramps and crowds turning trucks.

sec06-card-f24.question_text: Under what conditions may you turn right at a steady red light in Maine?
sec06-card-f24.teaching_text: Skipping the full stop or missing a no-turn-on-red sign is one of the fastest road-test failures.

sec06-card-f25.question_text: How should you respond when approaching a flashing yellow traffic signal?
sec06-card-f25.teaching_text: Flashing yellow flags a high-conflict spot where cross traffic or turning cars may pull out suddenly.

sec06-card-f26.question_text: What must you do at a flashing red traffic light before entering the intersection?
sec06-card-f26.teaching_text: A flashing red acts like a stop sign, demanding a complete halt and clear cross-traffic scan.

sec06-card-f27.question_text: At a railroad crossing with flashing red lights and lowered gates, when may you finally drive across?
sec06-card-f27.teaching_text: Weaving around gates or moving while lights still flash risks getting struck by a second train.
sec06-card-f27.must_match_memory_hook: Wait till lights stop, gates rise

visual_sync.text_span: Wait till lights stop, gates rise

sec06-card-f28.question_text: What movement is allowed when a signal shows both a red light and a lighted green arrow?
sec06-card-f28.teaching_text: Only the arrow movement is open, and pedestrians or clearing cars in that path still require caution.

sec06-card-f29.question_text: What is the purpose of a steady yellow arrow on a turn signal?
sec06-card-f29.teaching_text: Your protected turn phase is ending, so avoid jumping late in front of oncoming lanes.

sec06-card-f30.question_text: Which direction of travel does a steady upward-pointing green arrow allow?
sec06-card-f30.teaching_text: Directional arrows restrict turns when intersection geometry forbids turning across adjacent lanes.

sec06-card-f31.question_text: What must drivers in that turn lane do when facing a steady red turn arrow?
sec06-card-f31.teaching_text: A red turn arrow locks out turning until the signal cycles back to a green indication.

sec06-card-f32.question_text: When several traffic signals hang across a wide roadway, which signal governs you?
sec06-card-f32.teaching_text: Reading a neighbor lane's green arrow while your own lane sits on red triggers angled crashes.

sec06-card-f33.question_text: What does a steady red X suspended directly over a traffic lane mean?
sec06-card-f33.teaching_text: Reversible lanes under a red X often carry head-on traffic flowing straight toward you.

sec06-card-f34.question_text: What action must you take when you see a steady yellow X above your lane?
sec06-card-f34.teaching_text: The lane direction is about to flip to closed, so merge smoothly out right away.

sec06-card-f35.question_text: For what single maneuver may you use a lane marked with an overhead flashing yellow X?
sec06-card-f35.teaching_text: Using a shared turn lane for through driving puts you bumper-to-bumper with opposing left turners.

sec06-card-f36.question_text: What does a downward-pointing green arrow mounted over a traffic lane tell you?
sec06-card-f36.teaching_text: Overhead lane-control signals confirm which reversible lanes are open to your travel direction right now.

sec06-card-f37.question_text: What standard color, shape, and markings identify most general road warning signs?
sec06-card-f37.teaching_text: Spotting a yellow diamond from afar cues you to scan for curves, crossings, or merges early.

sec06-card-f38.question_text: What roadway feature ahead is announced by a yellow diamond bearing a bold black cross?
sec06-card-f38.teaching_text: Rural crossroads can hide behind trees or hills where side traffic enters at highway speed.

sec06-card-f39.question_text: What does a yellow diamond showing a vertical black line met by one side branch warn about?
sec06-card-f39.teaching_text: Vehicles turning out of a hidden side road may merge into your lane with short sightlines.

sec06-card-f40.question_text: What type of junction ahead is indicated by a bold black letter T on a yellow diamond?
sec06-card-f40.teaching_text: Your current road ends ahead, so prepare to slow down and turn either left or right.

sec06-card-f41.question_text: What passing restriction is marked by a sideways-pointing yellow pennant sign?
sec06-card-f41.teaching_text: Mounted on the left side of two-lane roads, the pennant stays visible even behind tall trucks.

sec06-card-f42.question_text: What lies ahead when a yellow diamond displays a winding S-shaped black arrow?
sec06-card-f42.teaching_text: Repeated bends demand steady reduced speed before entering the first turn in the series.

sec06-card-f43.question_text: What does a yellow diamond with a black arrow curving smoothly to the right warn of?
sec06-card-f43.teaching_text: Slowing before the bend starts keeps lateral tire grip calm through the entire curve.

sec06-card-f44.question_text: Which warning sign shows two opposing arrows splitting around the nose of a center island?
sec06-card-f44.teaching_text: Keep to the right of the upcoming median island so you never drift onto the wrong side.

sec06-card-f45.question_text: Which warning sign depicts opposing arrows coming back together past the end of a center island?
sec06-card-f45.teaching_text: Once the barrier disappears, oncoming traffic returns right across a painted yellow center line.

sec06-card-f46.question_text: What does a yellow warning sign with one outer black line angling inward toward the other mean?
sec06-card-f46.teaching_text: Spotting the lane drop early lets you signal and merge smoothly instead of squeezing at the taper.

sec06-card-f47.question_text: What traffic situation ahead is shown by a diagonal black branch blending into an upward arrow?
sec06-card-f47.teaching_text: Scanning the ramp side and adjusting space helps incoming drivers blend safely into flow.

sec06-card-f48.question_text: What does a warning sign with two upward arrows separated by a short dashed line indicate?
sec06-card-f48.teaching_text: Entering traffic gets its own fresh lane ahead, so neither stream has to fight immediately for one space.

sec06-card-f49.question_text: What is ahead when you pass a yellow diamond displaying a vertical red-yellow-green light symbol?
sec06-card-f49.teaching_text: Advance signal warnings sit before hills or curves that hide stopped queues at a hidden intersection.

sec06-card-f50.question_text: What does a yellow warning diamond showing a red octagon below an upward black arrow tell you?
sec06-card-f50.teaching_text: Advance notice prevents skidding past a rural stop sign tucked right behind blind trees or a crest.

sec06-card-f51.question_text: What hazard does a rectangular yellow panel with a bold black V-shaped chevron mark?
sec06-card-f51.teaching_text: Rows of chevrons trace the outside edge of a tight bend so you can judge how hard it turns.

sec06-card-f52.question_text: What information does a small yellow speed plaque mounted below a curve diamond give?
sec06-card-f52.teaching_text: Engineers calculate that advisory speed for dry pavement, so slick weather calls for going even slower.

sec06-card-f53.question_text: Which special five-sided yellow sign shows two walking figures inside?
sec06-card-f53.teaching_text: Only school warnings use the house-shaped pentagon, signaling children near the street.

sec06-card-f54.question_text: What does a yellow diamond bearing a single walking person symbol warn drivers to watch for?
sec06-card-f54.teaching_text: Ease off the gas and scan curb edges where walkers may step into a midblock or corner crossing.

sec06-card-f55.question_text: Which warning combines a bicycle, a car, and a plaque reminding motorists about bicycles?
sec06-card-f55.teaching_text: Narrow shoulders mean cyclists legally occupy part of the travel lane ahead, requiring patient passing space.

sec06-card-f56.question_text: What does a yellow diamond displaying only a black bicycle symbol warn of?
sec06-card-f56.teaching_text: Multi-use trails often cross Maine roads midblock where riders emerge quickly from tree cover.

sec06-card-f57.question_text: What pavement condition is warned of by a car silhouette above two curvy skid lines?
sec06-card-f57.teaching_text: Rain mixes with road oil on bridges and polished asphalt, slashing tire grip during sudden braking.

sec06-card-f58.question_text: How should you respond when you pass a round yellow warning sign marked with a black X and railroad letters?
sec06-card-f58.teaching_text: Rural Maine crossings often lack gates or bells, making your own eyes and ears the primary warning.

sec06-card-f59.question_text: What does a white X-shaped railroad crossbuck mark, and where must you stop for an approaching train?
sec06-card-f59.teaching_text: Overhanging freight cars extend wider than the steel rails, so always stay well back behind the line.

sec06-card-f60.question_text: Why must you scan for additional tracks and trains even if no track-count plaque is posted?
sec06-card-f60.teaching_text: Assuming only one track exists can blindside you when a second train approaches from the opposite direction.

sec06-card-f61.question_text: Once clear, how should you drive across railroad tracks, and what must you never do on them?
sec06-card-f61.teaching_text: Entering tracks before enough room clears on the far side can trap your car directly on the rails.

sec06-card-f62.question_text: Right after a train finishes crossing ahead of you, how long must you wait before moving?
sec06-card-f62.teaching_text: The caboose or last car can hide a fast train coming the other way on an adjacent track.
sec06-card-f62.must_match_memory_hook: Wait till train clears, gates allow

visual_sync.text_span: Wait till train clears, gates allow

sec06-card-f63.question_text: Where must you wait if traffic or a red signal forces a stop near railroad tracks?
sec06-card-f63.teaching_text: Waiting before the tracks guarantees you never get boxed onto the crossing when traffic stalls ahead.

sec06-card-f64.question_text: What background color and shapes distinguish temporary work-zone warning signs?
sec06-card-f64.teaching_text: Bright orange signs alert you immediately to altered lanes, heavy equipment, and roadside crews ahead.

sec06-card-f65.question_text: Which common hazards and route changes do orange work-zone signs alert drivers to?
sec06-card-f65.teaching_text: Expect narrow temporary lanes, sudden stops for flaggers, and shifted routes around active roadwork.

sec06-card-f66.question_text: What authority do a highway work-zone flagger's paddle or hand signals carry?
sec06-card-f66.teaching_text: Flaggers coordinate single-lane alternating traffic safely around blind construction equipment and active road crews.

sec06-card-f67.question_text: Where should you stop when facing a red portable traffic signal in a construction zone?
sec06-card-f67.teaching_text: Stopping back at the temporary white line leaves turning clearance for oncoming traffic squeezing through one lane.

sec06-card-f68.question_text: What do orange barrels, cones, tubes, and a Road Closed barrier tell you in a work zone?
sec06-card-f68.teaching_text: Driving past a Road Closed barricade can put you onto fresh concrete, open trenches, or crew zones.

sec06-card-f69.question_text: What three driving habits keep you safe while traveling through an active work zone?
sec06-card-f69.teaching_text: Rear-end crashes spike in work zones when tailgaters get caught off guard by a sudden flagger stop.

sec06-card-f70.question_text: What happens to the fine if you are ticketed for speeding inside a Maine work zone?
sec06-card-f70.teaching_text: Doubled fines back up the serious risk high speeds pose to workers standing feet from bumpers.

sec06-card-r01.question_text: What kind of rules do regulatory signs state, and what topics do they commonly cover?
sec06-card-r01.teaching_text: Unlike advisory warnings, regulatory signs post binding traffic laws that carry citations if ignored.

sec06-card-r02.question_text: What universal message does a red circle with a diagonal red bar across a black symbol send?
sec06-card-r02.teaching_text: Spotting the red slash lets you recognize banned maneuvers instantly even before reading any text.

sec06-card-r03.question_text: What maneuver is outlawed by a left-pointing arrow inside a red circle and diagonal slash?
sec06-card-r03.teaching_text: Turning left there often sends you straight against a one-way street or high-crash median opening.

sec06-card-r04.question_text: What maneuver is outlawed by a right-pointing arrow inside a red circle and diagonal slash?
sec06-card-r04.teaching_text: Intersections ban right turns where narrow corners, heavy crosswalks, or one-way exits conflict.

sec06-card-r05.question_text: What maneuver is forbidden when a bent U-shaped arrow sits inside a red circle and slash?
sec06-card-r05.teaching_text: Tight medians or fast oncoming sightlines make swinging a turnaround dangerous at that spot.

sec06-card-r06.question_text: What movement does a white regulatory sign showing a single upward black arrow require?
sec06-card-r06.teaching_text: Turning from a mandatory straight-through lane cuts directly across legal turning lanes beside you.

sec06-card-r07.question_text: What must drivers do when positioned in a lane governed by a left-turn-only regulatory sign?
sec06-card-r07.teaching_text: Going straight out of a turn-only pocket surprises through drivers and runs out of pavement.

sec06-card-r08.question_text: Which two movements are allowed by a regulatory sign combining an upward arrow with a right branch?
sec06-card-r08.teaching_text: Left turns remain illegal from that lane even though straight and right options share space.

sec06-card-r09.question_text: Under what roadway conditions does a black-and-white speed-limit sign state the maximum legal speed?
sec06-card-r09.teaching_text: Fog, snow, glare, or heavy traffic require slowing well below the number printed on the sign.

sec06-card-r10.question_text: What unique shape and color combination identifies a standard stop sign?
sec06-card-r10.teaching_text: Eight-sided geometry lets you recognize a stop sign even from behind or when covered in snow.

sec06-card-r11.question_text: Where must your vehicle come to rest at a stop sign when a stop line or crosswalk is painted?
sec06-card-r11.teaching_text: Rolling onto the crosswalk forces pedestrians out into live cross traffic to get around your hood.

sec06-card-r12.question_text: Where do you stop at a stop sign when neither a stop line nor a crosswalk is painted?
sec06-card-r12.teaching_text: Nose up just enough to check cross streets while keeping your front bumper out of cross lanes.

sec06-card-r13.question_text: Once you make a full stop at a stop sign, when may you finally pull forward?
sec06-card-r13.teaching_text: Stopping does not transfer priority to you if cross-street traffic is still approaching fast.

sec06-card-r14.question_text: What shape and colors identify modern yield signs, and what colors might older ones still show?
sec06-card-r14.teaching_text: Recognizing that inverted three-sided silhouette tells you cross traffic has priority from any angle.

sec06-card-r15.question_text: How must you drive when approaching a yield sign with cross traffic or pedestrians nearby?
sec06-card-r15.teaching_text: Be ready to come to a full stop whenever gaps are too tight to enter without making others brake.

sec06-card-r16.question_text: What maneuver is a shared center left-turn lane built for, and what two uses are forbidden?
sec06-card-r16.teaching_text: Cruising or overtaking down the shared middle lane sets up high-speed head-on crashes.

sec06-card-r17.question_text: How must you travel when entering or driving along a signed one-way street?
sec06-card-r17.teaching_text: Turning against a one-way arrow puts every lane on that block coming straight at your windshield.

sec06-card-r18.question_text: What must drivers and pedestrians do when a police officer is directing traffic?
sec06-card-r18.teaching_text: An officer's live hand signals override normal signs and stoplights at crash scenes or events.

sec06-card-r19.question_text: What are the legal consequences of ignoring police traffic orders or trying to flee an officer?
sec06-card-r19.teaching_text: Trying to outrun a traffic stop escalates a routine stop into license loss and criminal peril.

sec06-card-r20.question_text: When no officer is present on scene, what legal weight do posted traffic signs and signals carry?
sec06-card-r20.teaching_text: Posted signs and lights enforce traffic statutes twenty-four hours a day even on empty roads.

sec06-card-r21.question_text: How does Maine law view removing, stealing, or defacing roadway traffic signs?
sec06-card-r21.teaching_text: A missing stop or curve warning sign can directly cause a fatal crash for the next driver through.

sec06-card-r22.question_text: Which three background colors and shapes are generally used on guide signs, and what do they point out?
sec06-card-r22.teaching_text: Green guides routes and exits, brown marks parks and recreation, and blue points to motorist services.

sec06-card-r23.question_text: What do the distinct shapes and colors of highway route markers help you tell apart?
sec06-card-r23.teaching_text: Reading shield shapes at a glance confirms you stayed on your planned highway through busy junctions.

sec06-card-r24.question_text: What colors and layout identify an official Interstate highway route marker?
sec06-card-r24.teaching_text: Spotting the red-and-blue shield confirms controlled-access freeway rules and exit ramps ahead.

sec06-card-r25.question_text: How does a United States numbered highway marker look compared with an Interstate shield?
sec06-card-r25.teaching_text: Federal numbered highways can include town intersections and driveways unlike fully fenced Interstates.

sec06-card-r26.question_text: What black-and-white design identifies a state-route marker in the Maine handbook?
sec06-card-r26.teaching_text: Knowing the state marker shape stops you from mixing up county or federal numbers at rural forks.

sec06-card-r27.question_text: How should you prepare and navigate when driving through unfamiliar territory?
sec06-card-r27.teaching_text: Studying maps or setting satellite navigation beforehand prevents sudden swerves across exit gores.

sec06-card-r28.question_text: What five traffic functions do painted pavement markings perform on the road surface?
sec06-card-r28.teaching_text: Road paint reinforces overhead signs right in your line of sight so you never guess lane rules.

sec06-card-r29.question_text: What traffic directions and passing rule does a single broken yellow center line indicate?
sec06-card-r29.teaching_text: Dashed yellow means sight distance allows passing, provided oncoming pavement is completely clear.

sec06-card-r30.question_text: Where a solid yellow line runs beside a broken yellow center line, which side is allowed to pass?
sec06-card-r30.teaching_text: If the solid line sits closest to your lane, hills or curves block safe passing sight distance ahead.

sec06-card-r31.question_text: What passing rule applies when two solid yellow lines divide the center of the road?
sec06-card-r31.teaching_text: Crossing double yellow to overtake risks a blind head-on crash over a crest or around a bend.
sec06-card-r31.must_match_memory_hook: Double yellow bans passing both ways

visual_sync.text_span: Double yellow bans passing both ways

sec06-card-r32.question_text: What lane flow and maneuver does a broken white divider line indicate?
sec06-card-r32.teaching_text: White always separates traffic moving the same way, whereas yellow always warns of opposing traffic.

sec06-card-r33.question_text: During normal through driving, how should you choose which travel lane to stay in?
sec06-card-r33.teaching_text: Avoiding lanes clogged with constant brake-and-go turns cuts crash risk and saves fuel.

sec06-card-r34.question_text: When a roadway offers three or more lanes in your direction, which lane usually flows smoothest?
sec06-card-r34.teaching_text: Staying centered keeps you clear of left-lane speeders and right-lane ramp merges.

sec06-card-r35.question_text: On a multilane road, what specific purposes belong to the left lane versus the right lane?
sec06-card-r35.teaching_text: Camping slowly in the left lane forces faster drivers into risky right-side weave maneuvers.
sec06-card-r35.must_match_memory_hook: Left passes, turns; right slower, exits

visual_sync.text_span: Left passes, turns; right slower, exits

sec06-card-r36.question_text: When there are two lanes traveling in your direction, which lane generally offers smoother flow?
sec06-card-r36.teaching_text: Keeping right except to overtake leaves the left lane open for passing and left turns.

sec06-card-r37.question_text: On which side is overtaking and passing another vehicle normally performed?
sec06-card-r37.teaching_text: Drivers expect overtakers in their left mirror and have narrower blind spots on the driver side.

sec06-card-r38.question_text: Are you ever allowed to drive off the paved road surface onto the shoulder to pass someone?
sec06-card-r38.teaching_text: Soft gravel shoulders, guardrails, and parked breakdowns quickly turn off-pavement passing attempts into rollovers.

sec06-card-r39.question_text: May you pull into a signed center turning-only lane to overtake slower through traffic?
sec06-card-r39.teaching_text: Drivers entering from the opposite direction to turn left will never expect a fast passer there.

sec06-card-r40.question_text: When may you pass on the right of a vehicle waiting to make a left turn?
sec06-card-r40.teaching_text: Only pass on the right if true two-lane pavement width exists without dropping tires off the edge.

sec06-card-r41.question_text: Besides passing a left-turning car, when else is passing on the right legal?
sec06-card-r41.teaching_text: Marked multilane streets allow moving past slower left-lane traffic while staying cleanly in your lane.

sec06-card-r42.question_text: Which lanes must trucks other than pickups use on three-lane stretches of the Maine Turnpike or Interstate ninety-five?
sec06-card-r42.teaching_text: Keeping heavy rigs out of the far-left lane preserves clear passing sightlines on busy freeway corridors.

sec06-card-r43.question_text: Which lane do you approach a left turn from, and how should you wait near the intersection midpoint?
sec06-card-r43.teaching_text: Positioning beside the center line keeps right-side through traffic flowing while you wait for a gap.

sec06-card-r44.question_text: How should you position your vehicle before and during a right turn?
sec06-card-r44.teaching_text: Swinging wide left before turning right tricks drivers behind into squeezing inside your right flank.

sec06-card-r45.question_text: Into which lane of the cross street must you complete a left turn?
sec06-card-r45.teaching_text: Drifting wide into the outer right lane mid-turn sideswipes oncoming cars turning right simultaneously.

sec06-card-r46.question_text: Into which lane of the receiving street must you finish a right turn?
sec06-card-r46.teaching_text: Turning curb-to-curb into the nearest right lane leaves adjacent lanes safe for through traffic.

sec06-card-r47.question_text: Where on the roadway should you position before turning left off a one-way street?
sec06-card-r47.teaching_text: With zero opposing traffic on a one-way street, the far-left edge is the proper turn lane.

sec06-card-r48.question_text: If you want a different lane on the new street, when may you move over?
sec06-card-r48.teaching_text: Changing lanes mid-intersection surprises other drivers who expect you to stay in your receiving lane.

sec06-card-r49.question_text: Why must you keep your front wheels pointed straight ahead while waiting to turn left?
sec06-card-r49.teaching_text: Pre-turned tires steer your car straight into oncoming traffic if someone rear-ends you from behind.

sec06-card-r50.question_text: What should you do if you realize mid-intersection that you picked the wrong turn or route?
sec06-card-r50.teaching_text: Panic-swerving out of a turn lane mid-intersection blindsides cars right beside your quarter panel.

sec06-card-r51.question_text: On a standard two-lane control sign with left-only on the left and straight-right on the right, how does each lane move?
sec06-card-r51.teaching_text: Reading lane-use arrows early lets you pick the right pocket before solid white lines begin.

sec06-card-r52.question_text: When three lane-use signs show left-straight, straight-only, and right-only from left to right, what does each lane allow?
sec06-card-r52.teaching_text: Matching overhead lane signs before the intersection prevents illegal cross-lane turns at green.

sec06-card-r53.question_text: What does a solid white line between lanes moving the same direction signify?
sec06-card-r53.teaching_text: Solid white channelizes turn pockets and weave zones where late lane hopping triggers sideswipes.

sec06-card-r54.question_text: What do broken white lines between lanes tell drivers about direction and lane changes?
sec06-card-r54.teaching_text: Even where broken white lines allow moving over, always signal and check mirrors and blind spots.

sec06-card-r55.question_text: Where must you stop when a painted stop line sits ahead of a crosswalk at a sign or light?
sec06-card-r55.teaching_text: The stop line sets your bumper back far enough for walkers and wide-turning buses to clear safely.

sec06-card-r56.question_text: Where do you stop at a stop control when no crosswalk or stop line is marked on the pavement?
sec06-card-r56.teaching_text: Stopping before the curb line protects unmarked corner crossings while giving a view down cross streets.

sec06-card-r57.question_text: Where can pedestrian crosswalks be located, and what paint colors commonly mark them?
sec06-card-r57.teaching_text: Watching only at street corners misses midblock village and campus crossings painted across Maine main streets.

sec06-card-r58.question_text: How must you respond to a school crossing guard, and where must you yield to crossing students?
sec06-card-r58.teaching_text: Rural Maine roads lack sidewalks and signals, yet crossing students hold full right-of-way outside towns too.

sec06-card-r59.question_text: Why is it important to stop cleanly behind a painted stop line?
sec06-card-r59.teaching_text: Overrunning the stop bar crowds people on foot toward fast-moving cross traffic.

sec06-card-r60.question_text: While turning on a green light, must you yield to pedestrians in unmarked crosswalks as well as painted ones?
sec06-card-r60.teaching_text: Every street corner creates a legal crosswalk extension whether paint stripes are visible or not.

sec06-card-r61.question_text: How far away must you halt and how long must you wait for a pedestrian using a white cane or guide dog?
sec06-card-r61.teaching_text: Stopping at least ten feet back avoids startling a guide dog or crowding a blind walker's path.

sec06-card-r62.question_text: What fine range applies in Maine for failing to yield to a visually impaired pedestrian?
sec06-card-r62.teaching_text: Maine enforces white-cane right-of-way strictly with steep fines up to a thousand dollars.

sec06-card-r63.question_text: What four checks and signals must you complete before pulling into a shared center left-turn lane?
sec06-card-r63.teaching_text: Checking ahead as well as your left blind spot catches opposing cars entering the same turn pocket.

sec06-card-r64.question_text: How is a shared center left-turn lane marked on the pavement?
sec06-card-r64.teaching_text: Outer solid lines with inner dashed yellow lines plus opposing arrows distinguish shared turn lanes from passing zones.

sec06-card-r65.question_text: Why must you always check the overhead signal before entering a reversible traffic lane?
sec06-card-r65.teaching_text: A lane that carried outbound evening rush traffic yesterday may run inbound against you this morning.

sec06-card-r66.question_text: What pavement lines edge a reversible lane, and which overhead symbols open or close it?
sec06-card-r66.teaching_text: Double dashed yellow borders alert you to look straight up for a green arrow or red X.

sec07-card-f01.question_text: What visual checks, signal step, and lane positioning come right before making a turn?
sec07-card-f01.teaching_text: Moving into the closest legal turn lane early prevents last-second cutting across adjacent traffic.

sec07-card-f02.question_text: Where should you aim your eyes during a turn, how do you apply throttle, and what do you check after?
sec07-card-f02.teaching_text: A blinker left flashing after a corner tricks cross-street drivers into pulling out right in front of you.

sec07-card-f03.question_text: From which part of your lane should you start a right turn, and what steering mistake must you avoid?
sec07-card-f03.teaching_text: Swinging left before turning right invites cyclists or impatient cars into the gap on your right.

sec07-card-f04.question_text: Where inside your lane do you start a left turn, and which traffic stream gets priority?
sec07-card-f04.teaching_text: Cutting a left turn in front of fast oncoming traffic is a leading cause of severe intersection crashes.

sec07-card-f05.question_text: When two side-by-side lanes allow turning the same direction, how must you track through the corner?
sec07-card-f05.teaching_text: Drifting out of your parallel arc mid-corner sideswipes the vehicle turning right beside you.

sec07-card-f06.question_text: Besides standard crossroads, what other meeting points count as intersections under the Maine handbook?
sec07-card-f06.teaching_text: Shopping-center entrances and private driveways create conflict points just as real as marked street corners.

sec07-card-f07.question_text: Why must you look both ways even before crossing a signed one-way street?
sec07-card-f07.teaching_text: A confused driver or cyclist going the wrong way can strike you if you only scan one direction.

sec07-card-f08.question_text: What six elements should you slow down and actively scan for as you approach any intersection?
sec07-card-f08.teaching_text: Catching a slick patch, hidden cyclist, or parked truck blocking sightlines early gives smooth braking margin.

sec07-card-f09.question_text: Why should you check cross traffic even when they face a red light or stop sign?
sec07-card-f09.teaching_text: A red light cannot physically stop a distracted driver, so stay ready to yield and save yourself.

sec07-card-f10.question_text: After stopping at an intersection, what directional visual pattern checks for vehicles and cyclists before entry?
sec07-card-f10.teaching_text: Cross traffic from the left reaches your side of the road first, so give left a final check.

sec07-card-f11.question_text: What two things must you verify before rolling forward when your traffic signal turns green?
sec07-card-f11.teaching_text: Jumping off the line the instant green lights up puts you in the path of late red-light runners.

sec07-card-f12.question_text: Why is it dangerous to pull out in front of an oncoming car just because its turn signal is blinking?
sec07-card-f12.teaching_text: That driver may have forgotten an old blinker or meant to turn into a driveway past your corner.

sec07-card-f13.question_text: How should you handle a corner where a building, hedge, or snowbank blocks your cross-street view?
sec07-card-f13.teaching_text: Edging forward at a crawl exposes minimal hood while opening a clear sightline before you commit.

sec07-card-f14.question_text: What should you do when vehicles in the nearest cross lane block your view of the next lane beyond them?
sec07-card-f14.teaching_text: Poking your bumper past a screening truck puts your front end blindly into fast adjacent traffic.

sec07-card-f15.question_text: Unless an officer or traffic device directs otherwise, who holds priority at a roundabout or traffic circle?
sec07-card-f15.teaching_text: Letting vehicles inside the ring keep moving prevents circular backups across every entry leg.

sec07-card-f16.question_text: To which side of the central island do you enter a roundabout, and which rotational way do you drive?
sec07-card-f16.teaching_text: Entering right of the splitter island channels every car smoothly one way around the circle.

sec07-card-f17.question_text: What is the raised inner pavement around a small roundabout island built for, and where do passenger cars stay?
sec07-card-f17.teaching_text: Long trailer wheels track over the raised apron while everyday cars stay cleanly in the paved outer lane.

sec07-card-f18.question_text: Which turn leaves a traffic circle, and what visual guides keep you in the proper exit path?
sec07-card-f18.teaching_text: Multilane circles assign specific exit legs by lane, so reading pavement arrows prevents cutting across outer traffic.

sec07-card-f19.question_text: Unless signs or markings direct otherwise, when does the handbook advise choosing the rightmost lane of a rotary?
sec07-card-f19.teaching_text: Starting on the outside when leaving soon avoids weaving across outer traffic right at your exit.

sec07-card-f20.question_text: What four actions sum up safe entry, travel, and exit through a traffic circle?
sec07-card-f20.teaching_text: Signaling your exit tells waiting entry drivers they have a clean gap instead of guessing your path.

sec07-card-f21.question_text: Why aren't mirror glances alone enough before changing lanes, and what physical check must you add?
sec07-card-f21.teaching_text: Physically turning your head toward the target lane sweeps the rear quarter blind zone mirrors miss.

sec07-card-f22.question_text: What two factors create blind spots around a motor vehicle?
sec07-card-f22.teaching_text: Roof pillars, headrests, and finite mirror angles all hide spaces wide enough to conceal bikes or cars.

sec07-card-f23.question_text: What six-step sequence takes you safely through a complete lane change from start to finish?
sec07-card-f23.teaching_text: Looking one more time after signaling catches a fast overtaker closing the gap while you prepared.

sec07-card-f24.question_text: Besides switching lanes mid-road, what two other maneuvers require full lane-change precautions?
sec07-card-f24.teaching_text: Entering from a ramp or roadside shoulder crosses into active travel lanes with identical sideswipe risk.

sec07-card-f25.question_text: What specific traffic does each mirror check and shoulder glance target before moving sideways?
sec07-card-f25.teaching_text: A car overtaking fast shows up in mirrors first, then disappears beside your rear fender until you look.

sec07-card-f26.question_text: Which two slim road users require special attention during every lane-change check?
sec07-card-f26.teaching_text: Two-wheeled riders present a narrow profile that easily slips behind a door pillar or mirror frame.

sec07-card-f27.question_text: Why must your over-the-shoulder checks stay brief while driving in moving traffic?
sec07-card-f27.teaching_text: Staring backward too long leaves you blind if brake lights suddenly flare in the lane ahead.

sec07-card-f28.question_text: Why must you scan beyond just the immediate target lane on a multilane road?
sec07-card-f28.teaching_text: On three-lane highways, a car two lanes over can merge inward into the exact spot you chose.

sec07-card-f29.question_text: How far in advance must you turn on your signal before changing lanes or turning?
sec07-card-f29.teaching_text: Flipping the lever only as you turn the wheel gives surrounding drivers zero warning time.

sec07-card-f30.question_text: How should you use an expressway acceleration lane before blending into highway traffic?
sec07-card-f30.teaching_text: Building up to highway pace on the ramp lets you slip into traffic without forcing trucks to slam brakes.

sec07-card-f31.question_text: What signaling, checking, and follow-up steps complete a standard expressway merge?
sec07-card-f31.teaching_text: Checking both the mirror and left shoulder confirms your chosen highway gap stayed clear before moving left.

sec07-card-f32.question_text: How do you enter an expressway when the entrance has no acceleration lane?
sec07-card-f32.teaching_text: Without a parallel runway to build speed, wait before entry for an extra-long gap so you can accelerate cleanly.

sec07-card-f33.question_text: Does traffic already cruising on an expressway have to yield to merging cars, and what speed mistake must mergers avoid?
sec07-card-f33.teaching_text: Merging sluggishly into fast freeway traffic creates an instant rear-end or swerve emergency.

sec07-card-f34.question_text: Which expressway lane should you normally stay in, and which passing sides are off-limits?
sec07-card-f34.teaching_text: Keeping right except to overtake makes freeway flow predictable and leaves left lanes clear.

sec07-card-f35.question_text: Before pulling left to pass on an expressway, what three checks and signals confirm clearance?
sec07-card-f35.teaching_text: High-speed traffic in the passing lane closes distance fast, so verify your left blind spot first.

sec07-card-f36.question_text: What speed mistake must you never make while another driver is overtaking you?
sec07-card-f36.teaching_text: Accelerating traps the passing car out in the left lane longer and escalates highway conflict.

sec07-card-f37.question_text: How quickly should you pass, and what mirror cue tells you it is safe to move back right?
sec07-card-f37.teaching_text: Waiting until both headlights of the passed vehicle show in your inside mirror prevents clipping their front bumper.

sec07-card-f38.question_text: Where beside neighboring highway vehicles should you avoid cruising steadily?
sec07-card-f38.teaching_text: Camping off someone's rear fender leaves you invisible the moment they decide to change lanes.

sec07-card-f39.question_text: Where should you position and signal before an expressway exit, and where do you start braking?
sec07-card-f39.teaching_text: Braking hard inside the main travel lane risks getting rear-ended at highway speed before the ramp.

sec07-card-f40.question_text: Once on the exit ramp, what speed should you drop down to and what control check finishes the exit?
sec07-card-f40.teaching_text: Highway speed perception tricks drivers into entering tight ramp curves way faster than they feel.

sec07-card-f41.question_text: For what reason may you stop along an expressway, and how should you pull off?
sec07-card-f41.teaching_text: Even shoulder stops near fast freeway lanes are dangerous, so only true breakdowns justify stopping.

sec07-card-f42.question_text: After making an emergency stop on the expressway shoulder, how does the handbook say to signal for assistance?
sec07-card-f42.teaching_text: An open hood tells passing state troopers at a glance that your car is disabled.

sec07-card-f43.question_text: What three actions must you never do on the traveled lanes of an expressway?
sec07-card-f43.teaching_text: Backing up for a missed exit or standing in highway lanes invites catastrophic high-speed impacts.

sec07-card-f44.question_text: What mental hazard can long stretches of straight highway driving trigger?
sec07-card-f44.teaching_text: Monotonous straightaways lull attention unless you actively keep eyes and mind engaged.

sec07-card-f45.question_text: Which four cabin and driving habits does the Maine manual suggest to stay alert on long highway drives?
sec07-card-f45.teaching_text: Fresh cool air and active visual scanning beat warm, silent cabins that put drivers to sleep.

sec07-card-f46.question_text: What should you do at the very first sign of drowsiness behind the wheel?
sec07-card-f46.teaching_text: Willpower cannot stop microsleeps once heavy eyelids start, so pull into a rest area immediately.

sec07-card-f47.question_text: Why shouldn't tired drivers rely on stay-awake pills or stimulants to keep driving?
sec07-card-f47.teaching_text: Stimulants mask fatigue briefly without restoring reaction speed, then wear off with a sudden crash.

sec07-card-f48.question_text: Why does passing on a two-lane road demand signaling and waiting for a wide-open view?
sec07-card-f48.teaching_text: Every second spent passing on a two-lane road puts you nose-to-nose with opposing traffic's path.

sec07-card-f49.question_text: About how many seconds does the manual estimate a highway pass takes at fifty to fifty-five miles per hour?
sec07-card-f49.teaching_text: Counting ten-plus seconds shows how much open pavement closes between two opposing highway cars.

sec07-card-f50.question_text: Which five upcoming features must you evaluate passing space before?
sec07-card-f50.teaching_text: Hills, bends, crossroads, and roadside obstacles can hide or introduce oncoming cars mid-pass.

sec07-card-f51.question_text: What three checks and signal action precede pulling into the left lane to pass?
sec07-card-f51.teaching_text: Checking behind before pulling left stops you from cutting off a car already overtaking you.

sec07-card-f52.question_text: What three steps confirm a safe return to the right lane after overtaking on a two-lane road?
sec07-card-f52.teaching_text: Combining the full-car mirror sight with a right shoulder glance guarantees generous front bumper clearance.

sec07-card-f53.question_text: Once safely back in the right travel lane after passing, what two final adjustments do you make?
sec07-card-f53.teaching_text: Easing back to cruising pace and shutting off the blinker resets smooth, predictable highway travel.

sec07-card-f54.question_text: How should you position and control your speed while another vehicle overtakes you?
sec07-card-f54.teaching_text: Keeping predictable lane position and pace lets the passing driver judge return timing accurately.

sec07-card-f55.question_text: When might you actually increase speed slightly if an overtaking driver aborts a pass?
sec07-card-f55.teaching_text: If the passer brakes to duck back behind you before oncoming traffic arrives, pulling forward clears room behind.

sec07-card-f56.question_text: Roughly how much road distance do two opposing highway vehicles eat up together during a single pass?
sec07-card-f56.teaching_text: Because both cars rush toward each other at highway pace, closing distance vanishes twice as fast.

sec07-card-f57.question_text: What visual illusion makes distant oncoming highway traffic dangerous when judging a pass?
sec07-card-f57.teaching_text: Head-on vehicles show almost zero sideways motion, tricking eyes into thinking they are crawling or parked.

sec07-card-f58.question_text: How close to a view-blocking hill or curve is starting a pass prohibited?
sec07-card-f58.teaching_text: An unseen car cresting a hill at fifty-five miles per hour leaves zero escape room.

sec07-card-f59.question_text: Why should you avoid passing near intersections, crossroads, or shopping-center entrances?
sec07-card-f59.teaching_text: Drivers turning right onto the road often check only left and pull straight into an overtaker.

sec07-card-f60.question_text: Which two fixed roadway crossings prohibit overtaking as you approach them?
sec07-card-f60.teaching_text: Narrow bridge decks and active train crossings eliminate shoulder escape room if something goes wrong.

sec07-card-r01.question_text: What roadside hazards ahead might cause the driver in front of you to swerve suddenly into the passing lane?
sec07-card-r01.teaching_text: If the car ahead dodges a cyclist, pothole, or narrow bridge abutment right as you pass, you collide.

sec07-card-r02.question_text: What rule governs return space before starting a pass behind a line of cars?
sec07-card-r02.teaching_text: Never gamble on passing a long string at once or assuming tight cars will kindly part for you.

sec07-card-r03.question_text: Where must you finish your pass and be back in your own lane relative to a no-passing zone?
sec07-card-r03.teaching_text: Still riding left past the start of solid yellow or a pennant sign breaks no-passing law.

sec07-card-r04.question_text: When is passing banned based on the yellow center stripe closest to your lane?
sec07-card-r04.teaching_text: A solid yellow stripe on your half of the centerline marks blind sightlines ahead.

sec07-card-r05.question_text: Even when the center line on your side is broken, what condition must hold before you pass?
sec07-card-r05.teaching_text: Broken yellow permits passing geometry, not priority over oncoming cars already approaching.

sec07-card-r06.question_text: Which two roadside signs, one mounted left and one mounted right, outlaw passing?
sec07-card-r06.teaching_text: Pairing the left-side yellow pennant with the right-side white regulatory sign ensures visibility behind tall trucks.

sec07-card-r07.question_text: How must you adjust speed and lateral clearance when overtaking a bicyclist in Maine?
sec07-card-r07.teaching_text: Three feet of side air protects riders from mirror strikes, wind blast, and sudden pothole wobbles.

sec07-card-r08.question_text: Where must traffic from both directions stop for a school bus flashing its red lights?
sec07-card-r08.teaching_text: Maine extends full red-light school-bus stops onto school grounds and public parking areas as well as streets.

sec07-card-r09.question_text: Once stopped for a flashing-red school bus on an undivided road, when may you start moving again?
sec07-card-r09.teaching_text: Students dropping papers or crossing late stay safe when cars wait until the bus rolls or driver waves.

sec07-card-r10.question_text: On a divided road, when are oncoming drivers excused from stopping for a school bus with red lights or stop arm?
sec07-card-r10.teaching_text: Painted center turn lanes do not count as physical barriers, so only a solid median excuses opposing lanes.

sec07-card-r11.question_text: In the divided-road school-bus rules, how should stopped drivers proceed once red lights stop and the arm retracts?
sec07-card-r11.teaching_text: Rolling forward cautiously lets you react instantly if a child doubles back toward the bus.

sec07-card-r12.question_text: What overarching safety standard governs anywhere you leave a parked vehicle?
sec07-card-r12.teaching_text: A parked car jutting into sightlines or travel lanes forces moving drivers into blind swerves.

sec07-card-r13.question_text: How should you align your vehicle along a street unless painted lines show angle stalls?
sec07-card-r13.teaching_text: Nose-in parking where no angle stalls exist leaves your rear bumper sticking out into live lanes.

sec07-card-r14.question_text: How much clearance must you leave between your parked vehicle and cars parked ahead or behind?
sec07-card-r14.teaching_text: Two feet of fore-and-aft buffer gives trapped neighbors enough swing angle to exit cleanly.

sec07-card-r15.question_text: Where should you position your vehicle relative to travel lanes when parking along a road?
sec07-card-r15.teaching_text: Using full shoulder width keeps side mirrors and opening doors well clear of passing traffic.

sec07-card-r16.question_text: What is the maximum legal distance your wheels may sit from the curb when parked alongside it?
sec07-card-r16.teaching_text: Parking wider than eighteen inches narrows the street and risks road-test failure or a citation.

sec07-card-r17.question_text: How should you secure the brake and transmission when parking an automatic versus a manual car?
sec07-card-r17.teaching_text: Combining the parking brake with park, or first or reverse gear in a manual, provides dual roll protection.

sec07-card-r18.question_text: Which principle guides turning your front wheels when parking on any hill, with or without a curb?
sec07-card-r18.teaching_text: Turning wheels uphill away from a curb, and right everywhere else, keeps a runaway car out of center lanes.

sec07-card-r19.question_text: Which side should you exit from when possible, and what must you check before opening a street-side door?
sec07-card-r19.teaching_text: Swinging a street-side door open blindly into a bike lane causes severe dooring crashes.

sec07-card-r20.question_text: What three security steps should you take before walking away from a parked vehicle?
sec07-card-r20.teaching_text: Shutting off the motor, pocketing the key, and locking doors prevents theft and accidental rollaways.

sec07-card-r21.question_text: What is required to legally park in a reserved disability parking space?
sec07-card-r21.teaching_text: Reserved accessible stalls keep close, level access open for drivers and passengers with mobility impairments.

sec07-card-r22.question_text: What state-law fine does the Maine manual list for misusing disability license plates or placards?
sec07-card-r22.teaching_text: Borrowing someone else's placard when the permit holder is absent carries a steep state penalty.

sec07-card-r23.question_text: How may towns and cities regulate curbside loading zones?
sec07-card-r23.teaching_text: Blocking signed delivery zones forces box trucks to double-park out in active travel lanes.
