sec08-card-f64.question_text: Because tires and road surface set your available grip, when must worn tires be replaced?
sec08-card-f64.teaching_text: Brakes only stop the wheels, whereas healthy rubber tread actually stops the car on the road.

sec08-card-f65.question_text: How fast may you safely travel at night relative to your headlights' reach?
sec08-card-f65.teaching_text: Outrunning your headlight beams means a moose or stalled car appears closer than your stopping distance.

sec08-card-f66.question_text: What should you do when blinding rain, blizzard snow, or thick fog blocks vision even at low speed?
sec08-card-f66.teaching_text: Creeping blind inside active travel lanes invites high-speed chain-reaction pileups from drivers approaching behind.

sec08-card-f67.question_text: How fast should you approach an intersection where buildings, fences, or trees hide cross streets?
sec08-card-f67.teaching_text: Matching entry speed to sight distance ensures you can halt if hidden cross traffic pulls out.

sec08-card-f68.question_text: Why must you drop speed before topping a steep hill crest or entering a blind curve?
sec08-card-f68.teaching_text: A stalled logging truck, cyclist, or crash scene could sit dead still right over the crest.

sec08-card-f69.question_text: How should you position and prepare your speed when driving past a line of curbside parked cars?
sec08-card-f69.teaching_text: Children darting between bumpers and sudden swinging car doors appear with almost zero warning.

sec08-card-f70.question_text: Why does heavy traffic require reducing your driving speed?
sec08-card-f70.teaching_text: Packed lanes shrink escape paths on every side, making lower speed your best safety margin.

sec08-card-f71.question_text: In which five kinds of tight or high-activity places should you proactively lower speed?
sec08-card-f71.teaching_text: Narrow bridge walls, toll lanes, and playground zones compress steering room while multiplying surprises.

sec08-card-f72.question_text: Why is constantly overtaking slower cars risky even if you never exceed the posted speed limit?
sec08-card-f72.teaching_text: Every lane change and pass exposes you to fresh blind spots and misjudged gaps.

sec08-card-f73.question_text: If a string of vehicles stacks up trying to pass you, how should you respond?
sec08-card-f73.teaching_text: Helping faster traffic clear safely dissolves frustrated tailgating packs behind your bumper.

sec08-card-f74.question_text: What speed goal should you hit in a freeway entrance lane before merging?
sec08-card-f74.teaching_text: Blending in at matching speed keeps traffic flowing smoothly without sudden braking.

sec08-card-f75.question_text: When leaving an expressway, where must you wait to start slowing down?
sec08-card-f75.teaching_text: Slowing early in the high-speed travel lane catches fast following traffic off guard.

sec08-card-r01.question_text: When should you adjust speed for a slow-moving vehicle ahead, especially on hills or merges?
sec08-card-r01.teaching_text: Closing rate fools the eye fast when a heavy tractor or truck loses speed climbing a grade.

sec08-card-r02.question_text: What rear emblem marks vehicles that typically travel twenty-five miles per hour or slower?
sec08-card-r02.teaching_text: Spotting that reflective orange-and-red triangle on farm equipment or buggies warns of a huge speed gap.

sec08-card-r03.question_text: What driving adjustment do yellow warning signs call for as you approach a hazard?
sec08-card-r03.teaching_text: Easing off the throttle as soon as you read a diamond sign gives calm reaction space ahead.

sec08-card-r04.question_text: What sign warns drivers that a red-yellow-green traffic signal lies ahead?
sec08-card-r04.teaching_text: Advance signal diamonds alert highway drivers to prepare to stop past curves or hills.

sec08-card-r05.question_text: What does a yellow warning diamond showing a diagonal right branch blending into a vertical arrow mean?
sec08-card-r05.teaching_text: Check the right ramp and adjust speed or lane position so entering traffic blends cleanly.

sec08-card-r06.question_text: What traffic change is warned of by a yellow diamond bearing opposing up-and-down black arrows?
sec08-card-r06.teaching_text: You are leaving a one-way or divided stretch, so keep right of the yellow centerline.

sec08-card-r07.question_text: What does the divided-highway-ends warning sign tell you about the median ahead?
sec08-card-r07.teaching_text: Prepare to return to undivided two-way flow with oncoming traffic right across painted lines.

sec08-card-r08.question_text: What roadway change ahead is announced by the divided-highway-begins warning sign?
sec08-card-r08.teaching_text: Steer smoothly to the right side of the median nose as opposing directions split apart.

sec08-card-r09.question_text: What hazard does a yellow diamond bearing a black deer silhouette warn you to expect?
sec08-card-r09.teaching_text: Scan forest edges closely, especially around dawn and dusk when Maine deer move most.

sec08-card-r10.question_text: Which lane move does a right-lane-ends warning sign prepare right-lane drivers to make?
sec08-card-r10.teaching_text: Signal left and find a four-second gap early before the right pavement tapers away.

sec08-card-r11.question_text: What extra awareness does a yellow bicycle warning sign call for?
sec08-card-r11.teaching_text: Expect riders sharing narrow shoulders or crossing where bike paths intersect the roadway.

sec08-card-r12.question_text: What lies ahead when a yellow warning diamond displays a bold black cross symbol?
sec08-card-r12.teaching_text: Cover the brake and scan both left and right approaches for hidden cross-road traffic.

sec08-card-r13.question_text: What control ahead is announced by an upward black arrow above a red octagon symbol?
sec08-card-r13.teaching_text: Ease off speed right away so a blind corner or hill never catches you braking too late.

sec08-card-r14.question_text: What is a space cushion, and why do defensive drivers maintain one?
sec08-card-r14.teaching_text: Keeping clear pavement around your car gives room to brake or steer away when someone errs.

sec08-card-r15.question_text: Where around your vehicle should you maintain a space cushion, and what scales its size?
sec08-card-r15.teaching_text: Higher speeds and slick roads demand stretching your front, rear, and side buffers wider.

sec08-card-r16.question_text: What minimum following interval does the Maine handbook set for normal conditions, and when do you add more?
sec08-card-r16.teaching_text: Maine tests a full four-second rule, longer than some states, so keep four seconds clear on the exam.
sec08-card-r16.must_match_memory_hook: At least four seconds; more bad

visual_sync.text_span: At least four seconds; more bad

sec08-card-r17.question_text: How do you measure your following interval using a roadside landmark?
sec08-card-r17.teaching_text: Starting your count as their tail passes a shadow or sign pole works accurately at any speed.

sec08-card-r18.question_text: What should you do if your front bumper reaches the landmark before you finish counting four seconds?
sec08-card-r18.teaching_text: Lifting slightly off the gas rebuilds a full four-second buffer without jarring brake taps.

sec08-card-r19.question_text: Why must you stretch following distance on slick roads and behind bicycles or motorcycles?
sec08-card-r19.teaching_text: Motorcycles stop fast and can go down instantly on wet metal grates, gravel, or potholes.

sec08-card-r20.question_text: What small speed adjustment helps an overtaking driver finish passing you safely?
sec08-card-r20.teaching_text: A gentle lift off the throttle shortens their time out in the oncoming lane.

sec08-card-r21.question_text: Why do large trucks and trailers call for extra following distance behind them?
sec08-card-r21.teaching_text: Hanging back lets you see signals ahead while bringing your car into the trucker's side mirrors.

sec08-card-r22.question_text: Why must you never squeeze past the right side of a large truck that may turn right?
sec08-card-r22.teaching_text: Tractor-trailers often swing wide left just to clear right curbs, crushing cars that sneak inside.

sec08-card-r23.question_text: How do uphill climbs versus downhill grades affect passing a heavy truck?
sec08-card-r23.teaching_text: Gravity slows loaded rigs climbing hills yet pushes them fast down grades where passing takes much longer.

sec08-card-r24.question_text: Why should you leave extra bumper gap when stopping behind a heavy truck or bus on an incline?
sec08-card-r24.teaching_text: Heavy manual rigs can roll backward several feet as the driver moves from brake to clutch.

sec08-card-r25.question_text: Which visibility, speed, and vehicle-weight conditions require stretching beyond four seconds?
sec08-card-r25.teaching_text: Night darkness delays perception while heavy cargo or a trailer stretches mechanical braking distance.

sec08-card-r26.question_text: Which two vehicle types should you expect to stop at railroad crossings, and how do you prepare behind them?
sec08-card-r26.teaching_text: School buses and flammable-liquid tankers stop at tracks even when crossing lights stay dark.

sec08-card-r27.question_text: How should you avoid riding side-by-side next to another vehicle on multilane roads?
sec08-card-r27.teaching_text: Staggering lane positions keeps side escape lanes open and clears you out of neighbor blind spots.

sec08-card-r28.question_text: How should you position within your lane on undivided two-way roads?
sec08-card-r28.teaching_text: Giving oncoming traffic generous lateral margin protects mirrors if an opposing car drifts wide.

sec08-card-r29.question_text: When safe and practical, how can through-lane drivers help vehicles merging onto the highway?
sec08-card-r29.teaching_text: Shifting left a lane or opening a calm gap turns a tight ramp merge into a non-event.

sec08-card-r30.question_text: Why should you avoid driving directly alongside another car right near a freeway exit ramp?
sec08-card-r30.teaching_text: Drivers realizing late they want, or do not want, an exit swerve abruptly across exit gores.

sec08-card-r31.question_text: Who deserves extra side clearance along town streets besides parked vehicles?
sec08-card-r31.teaching_text: Unprotected walkers, kids, and cyclists have zero steel cage if a stumble or gust shifts them.

sec08-card-r32.question_text: Where inside your lane should you guide your car while a tractor-trailer overtakes you?
sec08-card-r32.teaching_text: Moving slightly right widens air-buffet separation and keeps you clear of wide trailer tires.

sec08-card-r33.question_text: How can you protect your rear bumper before slowing or turning when traffic follows behind?
sec08-card-r33.teaching_text: Extra front cushion lets you brake gradually while early blinkers give tailing drivers long warning.

sec08-card-r34.question_text: If a tailgater rides your bumper and an open lane sits to your right, what should you do?
sec08-card-r34.teaching_text: Putting a tailgater in front of you beats risking a rear-end crash if traffic stops ahead.

sec08-card-r35.question_text: When there is no right lane to move into, how do you safely encourage a tailgater to pass?
sec08-card-r35.teaching_text: Waiting for a safe passing stretch before easing speed avoids encouraging a blind head-on pass.

sec08-card-r36.question_text: Where do you steer when parked cars line the right curb and oncoming traffic approaches on the left?
sec08-card-r36.teaching_text: Threading a balanced middle track avoids both swinging car doors and oncoming side mirrors.

sec08-card-r37.question_text: How do you handle a bicyclist ahead when an oncoming car will reach the same spot at once?
sec08-card-r37.teaching_text: Splitting hazards one at a time lets oncoming traffic clear so you can give three full feet.

sec08-card-r38.question_text: What standard defines a big-enough gap when merging, crossing, or turning into moving traffic?
sec08-card-r38.teaching_text: If oncoming or lane drivers have to hit the brakes for you, the gap was too small.

sec08-card-r39.question_text: What time gap does the Maine manual call for when changing lanes or merging onto roads and freeways?
sec08-card-r39.teaching_text: A four-second hole lets you slip in while preserving safe following cushions ahead and behind.

sec08-card-r40.question_text: Why must you refuse to squeeze into an undersized traffic gap?
sec08-card-r40.teaching_text: Forcing into a cramped slot erases both drivers' stopping margin if traffic ahead checks up.

sec08-card-r41.question_text: How should you change across several same-direction lanes on a multilane road?
sec08-card-r41.teaching_text: Stopping in traffic or sweeping diagonally across three lanes at once blindsides fast overtakers.

sec08-card-r42.question_text: From a full stop, roughly how much clear gap do the handbook examples call for to cross a city street versus a highway?
sec08-card-r42.teaching_text: Highway traffic covers ground roughly twice as fast, demanding a full block of open sightline.

sec08-card-r43.question_text: Roughly how much gap do the examples call for to turn into and accelerate with city versus highway traffic?
sec08-card-r43.teaching_text: Turning and building up to cruising speed takes longer than shooting straight across.

sec08-card-r44.question_text: When is stopping halfway across a divided highway acceptable?
sec08-card-r44.teaching_text: If the median island is narrower than your car's length, your bumper hangs out in live fast lanes.

sec08-card-r45.question_text: May you pull into an intersection on a green light if backed-up traffic blocks your exit side?
sec08-card-r45.teaching_text: Getting stranded mid-intersection when the light turns red gridlocks every cross-street lane.

sec08-card-r46.question_text: Before pulling out in front of a signaling car, what must you wait to see?
sec08-card-r46.teaching_text: Watching wheels slow and angle into the turn beats gambling on a forgotten blinker.

sec08-card-r47.question_text: Why is running low-beam headlights smart during bright daytime hours as well as at night?
sec08-card-r47.teaching_text: Lighted headlamps help oncoming drivers judge your distance on shaded wooded Maine two-lanes.

sec08-card-r48.question_text: Which two daytime visibility or weather triggers legally require turning your headlights on in Maine?
sec08-card-r48.teaching_text: Turning headlights on whenever wipers run continuously lights both your nose and your rear taillights in rain.

sec08-card-r49.question_text: During what daily timeframe does Maine law require headlights on every moving vehicle?
sec08-card-r49.teaching_text: Dusk and pre-dawn twilight hide unlit dark cars against shadows long before pitch black arrives.

sec08-card-r50.question_text: Why should you switch headlights on when driving away from a rising or setting sun?
sec08-card-r50.teaching_text: Drivers coming toward you stare straight into sun glare, so your headlights cut through the haze.

sec08-card-r51.question_text: May you drive using only parking lights during times when headlights are required?
sec08-card-r51.teaching_text: Dim amber marker bulbs mark parked cars and provide zero road illumination while moving.

sec08-card-r52.question_text: In what dark driving situations, assuming no close traffic, are high-beam headlights especially valuable?
sec08-card-r52.teaching_text: High beams reach much farther down dark rural roads to reveal walkers, deer, or cones early.

sec08-card-r53.question_text: At what distances must you dim high beams, and shut off auxiliary fog lights, for oncoming versus leading cars?
sec08-card-r53.teaching_text: Five hundred feet ahead and three hundred behind are prime Maine exam numbers that prevent night glare.

sec08-card-r54.question_text: Which headlight beam setting works best in fog, falling snow, or heavy rain, and why?
sec08-card-r54.teaching_text: High beams angle upward and bounce blinding white light straight back off water droplets and flakes.

sec08-card-r55.question_text: How should you respond when an oncoming driver forgets to dim blinding high beams?
sec08-card-r55.teaching_text: Flashing your brights back leaves two blinded drivers hurtling toward each other in the dark.

sec08-card-r56.question_text: When is sounding your vehicle's horn appropriate, and when should you leave it alone?
sec08-card-r56.teaching_text: Your horn is a safety warning tool, never a vent for traffic frustration.

sec08-card-r57.question_text: When can a brief, light tap on the horn prevent a close call?
sec08-card-r57.teaching_text: A polite early tap catches a drifting driver or stepping walker before danger turns urgent.

sec08-card-r58.question_text: Why must you avoid blasting the horn right beside cyclists or horses unless immediate danger demands it?
sec08-card-r58.teaching_text: A sudden loud blast can spook a horse or startle a rider straight into your path.

sec08-card-r59.question_text: Which six common turning and lateral maneuvers always call for using turn signals?
sec08-card-r59.teaching_text: Signaling driveways and parking-lot turns matters just as much as major street corners.
sec08-card-r59.must_match_memory_hook: Lanes, turns, merges, ramps, lots, drives

visual_sync.text_span: Lanes, turns, merges, ramps, lots, drives

sec08-card-r60.question_text: When should you lightly tap the brake pedal to flash an early warning behind you?
sec08-card-r60.teaching_text: Drivers behind rarely expect midblock driveway turns or curb parking without an early brake flash.

sec08-card-r61.question_text: Should you still signal when the road looks empty, and what minimum distance applies before turning?
sec08-card-r61.teaching_text: Signaling every time catches the cyclist, pedestrian, or cruiser you missed seeing.

sec08-card-r62.question_text: How must you communicate turns and stops if your car's electrical turn signals stop working?
sec08-card-r62.teaching_text: Standardized left-arm signals keep surrounding drivers informed until you replace the bulb or fuse.

sec08-card-r63.question_text: When you plan to turn into a driveway just past an intersection, when should you turn your signal on?
sec08-card-r63.teaching_text: Signaling before the cross street tricks waiting corner drivers into pulling out in front of you.

sec08-card-r64.question_text: What should you always verify right after completing a lane change or gentle turn?
sec08-card-r64.teaching_text: Gentle lane changes often don't trip the steering column's automatic cancel cam.

sec08-card-r65.question_text: How do you position your left arm out the window to hand-signal a left turn?
sec08-card-r65.teaching_text: Extending your left arm straight points directly toward the leftward path you intend to take.

sec08-card-r66.question_text: How do you position your left arm out the window to hand-signal a right turn?
sec08-card-r66.teaching_text: Bending the elbow straight upward makes your hand visible over the roofline to cars on the right.

sec08-card-r67.question_text: What does a driver's left arm bent straight downward out the window signal?
sec08-card-r67.teaching_text: Pointing palm-back toward the pavement alerts trailing cars and cyclists that you are braking.

sec08-card-r68.question_text: Where should you move a disabled vehicle during a breakdown, and which lights warn traffic?
sec08-card-r68.teaching_text: Clearing all four tires off the travel lane plus running four-way flashers prevents roadside strikes.

sec08-card-r69.question_text: Besides raising the hood, what kind of terrain must you avoid stopping on during a breakdown?
sec08-card-r69.teaching_text: Stopping just beyond a blind hilltop or sharp bend leaves oncoming cars zero sightline to react.

sec08-card-r70.question_text: If you carry emergency warning flares, how far behind your disabled vehicle should you set them?
sec08-card-r70.teaching_text: Warning traffic at least a hundred feet upstream gives drivers room to merge left smoothly.

sec08-card-r71.question_text: What should you do after a breakdown if you do not have emergency flares in the car?
sec08-card-r71.teaching_text: Staying well clear of asphalt keeps you safe while a bright cloth or flag signals trouble.

sec08-card-r72.question_text: When must you refuse to change a flat tire yourself on the roadside?
sec08-card-r72.teaching_text: No tire or rim is worth crouching beside live highway traffic, so limp to safety or call a tow.

sec08-card-r73.question_text: Where relative to neighboring cars should you avoid lingering so other drivers can always see you?
sec08-card-r73.teaching_text: Hovering slightly behind and beside another car hides your hood right inside their rear blind zone.

sec08-card-r74.question_text: How should you handle another driver's blind spot during normal cruising and while overtaking?
sec08-card-r74.teaching_text: Either ease back or accelerate past promptly so you spend minimal seconds hidden beside their quarter panel.

sec11-card-f01.question_text: How does darkness change sight distance, and where should your eyes scan?
sec11-card-f01.teaching_text: Headlights illuminate only a narrow cone ahead, so sweeping both pavement edges spots walkers or wildlife early.

sec11-card-f02.question_text: When should you use high-beam headlights at night, and when must you dim them?
sec11-card-f02.teaching_text: High beams maximize rural sight distance until an oncoming vehicle appears and needs glare-free low beams.

sec11-card-f03.question_text: Where should you look if an oncoming driver forgets to dim bright high beams?
sec11-card-f03.teaching_text: Glancing along the right edge line preserves night-adapted vision while keeping your car centered safely.

sec11-card-f04.question_text: Behind traffic and in which three weather conditions must you run low-beam headlights?
sec11-card-f04.teaching_text: High beams blind drivers ahead through mirrors and bounce white glare straight back off fog, rain, or snow.

sec11-card-f05.question_text: Why should you keep scanning past the bright pool of your headlights at night?
sec11-card-f05.teaching_text: Dark shapes, unlit obstacles, or crossing animals often blot out background light beyond your main beam reach.

sec11-card-f06.question_text: Why must you avoid sunglasses or colored lenses at night and on overcast days?
sec11-card-f06.teaching_text: Dark or colored lenses filter away the faint contrast cues your eyes rely on in dim light.

sec11-card-f07.question_text: At least how much extra following time does the Maine manual add for ordinary night driving?
sec11-card-f07.teaching_text: Depth perception drops after sunset, so stretching your normal daytime interval by one second builds reaction space.

sec11-card-f08.question_text: How much time should you add to your following gap on unfamiliar roads at night?
sec11-card-f08.teaching_text: Hidden curves, sudden junctions, and surprise grades on unknown dark roads require adding at least two seconds.

sec11-card-f09.question_text: What three roadway changes commonly appear inside a construction work zone?
sec11-card-f09.teaching_text: Normal lane memory fails when work zones close lanes, shift detours, and move heavy machinery near traffic.

sec11-card-f10.question_text: Why must you still slow down through a work zone when no workers are on site?
sec11-card-f10.teaching_text: Tight concrete barriers, dropped shoulders, and grooved asphalt remain dangerous even after crews go home.

sec11-card-f11.question_text: Which five markers, vehicles, and people require active scanning in a work zone?
sec11-card-f11.teaching_text: Tracking signs, cones, and barrels alongside dump trucks and workers catches sudden merges or flagger stops early.

sec11-card-f12.question_text: What does a flashing or sequencing arrow panel warn of, and how should you respond?
sec11-card-f12.teaching_text: Merging smoothly toward the pointed open lane early beats racing to the cones and forcing a squeeze.

sec11-card-f13.question_text: What color combination and typical shape identify construction warning signs?
sec11-card-f13.teaching_text: Spotting an orange diamond ahead tells you instantly to drop speed and scan for temporary construction changes.

sec11-card-f14.question_text: Which five physical devices guide traffic safely along construction paths?
sec11-card-f14.teaching_text: Temporary cones, drums, vertical panels, barricades, and concrete walls mark live travel boundaries where painted lines end.

sec11-card-f15.question_text: How should you position your car and set your speed alongside construction channeling devices?
sec11-card-f15.teaching_text: Drifting close to barrels or speeding through narrow chutes leaves zero margin for workers stepping behind cones.

sec11-card-f16.question_text: What lane-change rule applies as you are leaving a construction work zone?
sec11-card-f16.teaching_text: Darting across lanes before clearing the final taper cuts off drivers emerging beside construction barrels.

sec11-card-f17.question_text: What gear and signals do work-zone flaggers use, and how must drivers respond?
sec11-card-f17.teaching_text: Flaggers hold legal traffic-control authority to protect crews around blind one-lane Alternating zones.

sec11-card-f18.question_text: What three speed and spacing adjustments protect you inside every work zone?
sec11-card-f18.teaching_text: Chain-reaction rear-enders happen fast in construction chutes when drivers keep highway speeds and tight gaps.

sec11-card-f19.question_text: How should you position around crews and equipment, and how should you treat empty night work zones?
sec11-card-f19.teaching_text: Darkness hides temporary lane drops and unlit equipment edges even when crews have wrapped up.

sec11-card-f20.question_text: How far must you keep obeying temporary work-zone controls?
sec11-card-f20.teaching_text: Temporary limits and lane rules remain legally active all the way to the End Road Work marker.

sec11-card-f21.question_text: Which three pre-trip steps help you handle construction delays calmly?
sec11-card-f21.teaching_text: Planning extra minutes or choosing an alternate corridor eliminates rush frustration before reaching orange cones.

sec11-card-f22.question_text: Why must you drop speed and stretch your following gap on dirt or gravel roads?
sec11-card-f22.teaching_text: Rolling stones under your tread stretch braking distances and kick windshield dust or chips toward close followers.

sec11-card-f23.question_text: How should you drive along narrow rural roads where opposing cars may crowd the middle?
sec11-card-f23.teaching_text: Country roads often lack shoulders or center stripes, so controlled speed and lane centering guard against wide oncoming cars.

sec11-card-f24.question_text: Who holds priority at a single-lane rural bridge, and how should traffic flow?
sec11-card-f24.teaching_text: Yielding to whichever car reaches the narrow deck first and alternating cleanly prevents head-on standoffs.

sec11-card-f25.question_text: What three adjustments apply when crossing an open-grating or steel bridge?
sec11-card-f25.teaching_text: Wet steel and open grates feel slick and tug front tires slightly sideways unless hands stay steady.

sec11-card-f26.question_text: How should you drive where dense woods, tall crops, or hill crests block sightlines?
sec11-card-f26.teaching_text: Hidden driveways, farm tractors, or stopped cars can sit just past a blind crest or tree line.

sec11-card-f27.question_text: How should you approach a rural intersection that has no traffic signals or stop-or-yield signs?
sec11-card-f27.teaching_text: Unmarked country crossroads demand low approach speeds so you can yield to crossing vehicles or sudden left turns.

sec11-card-f28.question_text: Which three driving adjustments belong on slick winter pavement?
sec11-card-f28.teaching_text: Smooth braking and steering paired with lower speeds and wide gaps preserve scarce snow-and-ice traction.

sec11-card-f29.question_text: Which vehicle parts and systems should be checked and inspected before winter weather arrives?
sec11-card-f29.teaching_text: Cold snaps expose weak batteries, cracked hoses, leaky exhausts, worn tires, and uneven brakes fast.
sec11-card-f29.must_match_memory_hook: Tires, antifreeze, hoses, exhaust, battery, brakes

visual_sync.text_span: Tires, antifreeze, hoses, exhaust, battery, brakes

sec11-card-f30.question_text: What engine-oil and battery-terminal care helps vehicles start reliably in Maine winters?
sec11-card-f30.teaching_text: Thick summer oil resists cranking in freezing cold while corroded battery terminals starve starter current.

sec11-card-f31.question_text: How can you safely gauge road grip and pick a safe speed in winter?
sec11-card-f31.teaching_text: Tapping brakes lightly at low speed away from traffic reveals black ice before a downhill stop surprises you.

sec11-card-f32.question_text: Why must you avoid sudden hard braking on snowy or icy pavement?
sec11-card-f32.teaching_text: Once tires lock solid on ice, steering disappears and the sliding vehicle follows road camber or momentum.

sec11-card-f33.question_text: How much space should you leave behind the car ahead on snow-covered or icy roads?
sec11-card-f33.teaching_text: Stopping on packed snow or glare ice can take several times longer than bare pavement requires.

sec11-card-f34.question_text: How should you approach winter hills and curves and handle the steering wheel?
sec11-card-f34.teaching_text: Shedding speed on the straightaway before a bend or grade lets gradual steering inputs hold traction.

sec11-card-f35.question_text: Which glass, heating, lighting, and fluid checks maintain winter visibility?
sec11-card-f35.teaching_text: Road salt spray blinds windshields in moments if washer fluid runs dry or wipers and defrosters fail.
sec11-card-f35.must_match_memory_hook: Clear glass, wipers, defroster, headlights, washer

visual_sync.text_span: Clear glass, wipers, defroster, headlights, washer

sec11-card-f36.question_text: What four techniques help free a vehicle stuck in deep snow without digging deeper?
sec11-card-f36.teaching_text: Spinning tires polish snow into glare ice, whereas straight wheels, cleared tire paths, and sand or litter bite.

sec11-card-f37.question_text: Where should you stay while rescue help is on the way during a winter breakdown?
sec11-card-f37.teaching_text: Leaving your car on foot in freezing wind and blowing snow leads quickly to frostbite and lost bearings.

sec11-card-r01.question_text: What visual markers should you display on and around a winter-stranded vehicle?
sec11-card-r01.teaching_text: A bright red flag stands out against snowdrifts while flares ahead and behind warn approaching plows.

sec11-card-r02.question_text: How should you and your passengers stay warm inside a winter-stranded car?
sec11-card-r02.teaching_text: Layering packed blankets and extra winter gear retains body heat without burning fuel continuously.

sec11-card-r03.question_text: Why must you keep snow cleared away from a stranded vehicle's exhaust pipe?
sec11-card-r03.teaching_text: Snow banking up over the tailpipe forces odorless, lethal carbon monoxide gas back inside the cabin.

sec11-card-r04.question_text: Which eight items belong in the Maine manual's suggested winter emergency kit?
sec11-card-r04.teaching_text: Packing digging, traction, battery-jump, warmth, and red-flag flare gear prepares you for remote Maine storms.
sec11-card-r04.must_match_memory_hook: Shovel, scraper, sand, cables, gear, flares

visual_sync.text_span: Shovel, scraper, sand, cables, gear, flares

sec11-card-r05.question_text: Which drivers must take reasonable steps to prevent snow or ice from blowing off their vehicle?
sec11-card-r05.teaching_text: Maine requires drivers of cars, SUVs, and pickups under ten thousand pounds to clear loose snow and ice.

sec11-card-r06.question_text: What is the safest choice in heavy fog, and how fast may you drive if travel is unavoidable?
sec11-card-r06.teaching_text: Never overdrive visibility in fog because a stopped car can appear at the edge of sight.

sec11-card-r07.question_text: Which headlight setting and pavement reference help guide you through fog?
sec11-card-r07.teaching_text: Low beams angle beneath suspended water droplets while painted right-edge lines keep you centered in lane.

sec11-card-r08.question_text: What should you do if dense fog drops visibility too low to continue safely?
sec11-card-r08.teaching_text: Stopping inside a live travel lane invites rear-end collisions, so pull completely off-road with flashers running.

sec11-card-r09.question_text: What three speed, space, and steering habits prevent skids on wet roads?
sec11-card-r09.teaching_text: Wet asphalt cuts tire friction, stretching brake distances and turning abrupt steering jerks into slides.

sec11-card-r10.question_text: Why is pavement especially slippery right as light rain begins falling?
sec11-card-r10.teaching_text: Initial raindrops lift grease and oil film onto the surface before steady downpours wash residue away.

sec11-card-r11.question_text: Which three vehicle features help you see and stay visible during rain?
sec11-card-r11.teaching_text: Clear blades and defrosted glass sharpen your forward view while headlights cut through gray road spray.

sec11-card-r12.question_text: How should you adjust turn signals and braking timing in rainy traffic?
sec11-card-r12.teaching_text: Drivers behind you need extra distance on wet roads too, so early blinkers and brake lights prevent rear-enders.

sec11-card-r13.question_text: What happens between your tires and the pavement during hydroplaning?
sec11-card-r13.teaching_text: Water building faster than tread grooves can channel lifts rubber off asphalt and strips steering grip.

sec11-card-r14.question_text: Which three speed and tire-care steps lower hydroplaning risk?
sec11-card-r14.teaching_text: Deep tread channels and proper tire pressure clear standing water while moderate speed prevents planing.

sec11-card-r15.question_text: Should you ever try driving across a flooded stretch of roadway?
sec11-card-r15.teaching_text: Even shallow-looking floodwater can stall engines, float passenger cars, and sweep occupants downstream.

sec11-card-r16.question_text: What structural hazard can murky floodwater hide, and when is it hardest to spot?
sec11-card-r16.teaching_text: Culvert washouts leave gaping chasms beneath calm-looking water that become nearly invisible after sunset.

sec11-card-r17.question_text: What must you do promptly if your vehicle stalls inside a flooded roadway?
sec11-card-r17.teaching_text: Rising currents sweep stalled vehicles rapidly, so evacuate immediately toward higher ground.

sec11-card-r18.question_text: Why should you combine extra caution with lower speeds after dark?
sec11-card-r18.teaching_text: Trimming speed keeps your stopping distance inside the shorter road segment your headlights reveal.

sec11-card-r19.question_text: Do wildlife collisions happen only during peak seasons, or when must Maine drivers stay alert?
sec11-card-r19.teaching_text: Knowing peak months helps, yet letting your guard down in winter or midsummer invites surprise wildlife strikes.

sec11-card-r20.question_text: During which season do Maine deer crashes climb, and which single month peaks?
sec11-card-r20.teaching_text: Breeding season and autumn movement put far more deer crossing Maine highways throughout November.

sec11-card-r21.question_text: Which two late-spring months mark peak moose collisions in Maine, alongside autumn?
sec11-card-r21.teaching_text: Test questions contrast November deer peaks against May and June when moose seek roadside salt and browse.

sec11-card-r22.question_text: Why are moose harder to spot by eye shine at night than deer?
sec11-card-r22.teaching_text: Deer eyes sit down inside headlight beams and glow, whereas a tall moose's eyes stand above the beam.

sec11-card-r23.question_text: During which daily hours are moose and deer most active, and can crossings happen outside them?
sec11-card-r23.teaching_text: Low-light twilight through sunrise brings peak movement, though animals still cross at midday too.

sec11-card-r24.question_text: What do posted moose and deer warning signs tell you about that stretch of road?
sec11-card-r24.teaching_text: Highway crews place wildlife signs specifically at corridors with heavy animal crossings or past collisions.

sec11-card-r25.question_text: Why must you keep scanning after one deer or moose clears your lane?
sec11-card-r25.teaching_text: Accelerating right behind one crossing deer often hits the second or third animal trailing out of the trees.

sec11-card-r26.question_text: What should you do when you encounter a moose standing on or beside the road?
sec11-card-r26.teaching_text: Thousand-pound moose rarely bolt gracefully like deer and need unpressured space and time to wander off.

sec11-card-r27.question_text: Why must you never try squeezing around a moose or stepping out to shoo it off?
sec11-card-r27.teaching_text: Cornered or startled moose can charge cars or trample people who step outside.

sec11-card-r28.question_text: What is the initial rule if a collision with an animal in your path cannot be avoided?
sec11-card-r28.teaching_text: Staying straight under hard braking beats swerving into oncoming traffic or trees at highway speed.

sec11-card-r29.question_text: How far may cargo project past the left and right fenders of a passenger vehicle in Maine?
sec11-card-r29.teaching_text: Left-side cargo overhangs risk clipping oncoming traffic, so zero inches apply left and six inches max right.

sec11-card-r30.question_text: When is carrying passengers or cargo inside your cabin unlawful?
sec11-card-r30.teaching_text: Stacked boxes or crowded riders that hide side mirrors or bump the shifter cripple emergency responses.

sec11-card-r31.question_text: Are riders ever permitted to perch on the exterior hood, roof, or trunk while moving?
sec11-card-r31.teaching_text: Even a low-speed parking-lot tap throws unrestrained riders off exterior sheet metal onto pavement.

sec11-card-r32.question_text: In which enclosed cargo areas and towed trailers is riding barred on a highway?
sec11-card-r32.teaching_text: Trunks and towed camp, mobile-home, semi, or utility trailers lack crash protection and strands riders in wrecks.

sec11-card-r33.question_text: Under what age must pickup passengers ride inside the cab, and what four exceptions exist?
sec11-card-r33.teaching_text: Riders under nineteen belong inside the cab barring work or training, licensed hunting trips, parades, or belted factory seats.

sec11-card-r34.question_text: How must a dog riding in an open pickup bed be protected on public ways, and what exceptions apply?
sec11-card-r34.teaching_text: Unsecured dogs can leap or get thrown into traffic, with narrow carveouts only for active farm work or hunting.
